title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
相稱一則曰使中外文
由科舉而選嗚呼我
太祖以神武取天下而於干戈
集之秋汲汲汲焉興賢興能進
岩壑詩書之士而庸之當時
得士之盛治安之效實爲
國家豐芑之仁
punctuated: 相稱。一則曰：「使中外文由科舉而選。」嗚呼！我太祖以神武取天下，而於干戈集之秋，汲汲汲焉興賢興能，進岩壑詩書之士而庸之。當時得士之盛、治安之效，實爲國家豐芑之仁。
translation_en: …corresponded to one another. One provision stated: “Let civil [officials?] at court and in the provinces be selected through the civil-service examinations.” Alas! Our Taizu won the empire through divine martial prowess, yet even when weapons were massed for war, he urgently sought to raise up the worthy and capable, bringing forward men versed in the Odes and Documents who lived in secluded mountains and valleys, and employing them in office. The abundance of talent secured at that time, and the resulting good government and peace, were truly acts of benevolence that nurtured the dynasty’s future generations, like luxuriant millet.

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承益崇益重三年率由未
始愆忒于今百三十餘年上
之取于下下之應於上皆不
能是越而其所以取所以應
者又皆本諸六經四書之
濂洛關閩之論而一切異
之說罷黜不用此我
===
朝取士之途所以惟科舉為最
正得人為最盛天下所共榮
而他途弗齒也弘治辛酉又
維其期巡按河南監察御史
羅〔賢〕自惟監臨之重舉舊典
謀協于鎮守太監藍〔忠〕巡撫
右副都御史鄭〔齡〕清戎監察
punctuated:
列聖相承，益崇益重，三年率由，未始愆忒。于今百三十餘年，上之取于下，下之應於上，皆不能是越。而其所以取、所以應者，又皆本諸六經四書之、濂洛關閩之論，而一切異之說罷黜不用。此我朝取士之途所以惟科舉為最正，得人為最盛，天下所共榮，而他途弗齒也。
弘治辛酉，又維其期。巡按河南監察御史羅〔賢〕自惟監臨之重，舉舊典，謀協于鎮守太監藍〔忠〕、巡撫右副都御史鄭〔齡〕、清戎監察
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors inherited this practice, esteeming it ever more highly and attaching ever greater importance to it. They observed the three-year cycle without deviation. For more than 130 years down to the present, neither the selection of men from below by those above nor the response of those below to those above has been able to depart from this system. Both the means of selection and the means of responding have been grounded in the Six Classics and Four Books [?] and in the teachings of the Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min traditions; all divergent doctrines [?] have been rejected and left unused. This is why, among our dynasty’s avenues for recruiting officials, the civil-service examinations alone are regarded as the most proper and as yielding the greatest abundance of worthy men. They confer an honor shared throughout the realm, while other avenues are not held in comparable esteem.
In the xinyou year of the Hongzhi reign [1501], the appointed time came around again. Luo Xian, the Investigating Censor on regional inspection in Henan, reflected on the weighty responsibility of supervising the examination. Invoking established precedents, he sought agreement with Lan Zhong, the Grand Eunuch serving as Regional Defender; Zheng Ling, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief serving as Grand Coordinator; and the Investigating Censor responsible for rectifying military affairs …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
御史董〔鑰〕暨諸藩臬僉謂是
重事也其慎之哉乃相與師
儒是擇惟公罔私幣聘來至
而〔鼎〕與訓導陳〔言〕實典考試
學正張〔曙〕教諭劉〔濟望〕亢〔時霖〕朱
〔濙〕曾〔憲〕訓導張〔琭〕何〔繼周〕談〔一鳳〕
則同考試于時提調則左布
===
政使李〔進〕右布政使曹〔元〕監
試則按察使文〔貴〕僉事彭〔綱〕
與凡百執事慎選咸備而巡
按御史實總理監臨之皆精
白以即事八月辛亥鎖院癸
丑之夕相與焚香告天矢得
真材啓經命題杜革私弊甲
punctuated:
御史董〔鑰〕暨諸藩臬僉謂：「是重事也，其慎之哉！」乃相與師儒是擇，惟公罔私，幣聘來至，而〔鼎〕與訓導陳〔言〕實典考試，學正張〔曙〕、教諭劉〔濟望〕、亢〔時霖〕、朱〔濙〕、曾〔憲〕、訓導張〔琭〕、何〔繼周〕、談〔一鳳〕則同考試。于時提調則左布政使李〔進〕、右布政使曹〔元〕，監試則按察使文〔貴〕、僉事彭〔綱〕，與凡百執事，慎選咸備，而巡按御史實總理監臨之，皆精白以即事。
八月辛亥鎖院，癸丑之夕，相與焚香告天，矢得真材，啓經命題，杜革私弊。甲
translation_en:
…Censor Dong Yue, together with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, all declared: “This is a weighty matter; we must approach it with care!” Together they selected learned teachers, acting impartially and without private favoritism. Those invited with gifts duly arrived. I, Ding, and Assistant Instructor Chen Yan served as Examiners. Instructor Zhang Shu, Instructors Liu Jiwang, Kang Shilin, Zhu Ying, and Zeng Xian, and Assistant Instructors Zhang Lu, He Jizhou, and Tan Yifeng served as Associate Examiners. At this time, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Jin and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Cao Yuan served as Proctors; Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Wen Gui and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Peng Gang supervised the examination. These and all other functionaries were carefully selected, and every post was filled. The Regional Inspector exercised overall direction and supervision. All took up their duties with the utmost purity of intent.
On the xinhai day of the eighth month, the examination compound was sealed. On the evening of guichou, we together burned incense and made an announcement to Heaven, pledging to find men of true talent. We opened the Classics and set the questions, preventing and eliminating favoritism and malpractice. On the jia…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
寅試之丁巳再試之庚申三
試之來試之士一千六百有
畸皆董學副使車〔璽〕之所造
就校閱而巡按御史又從而
覆簡之者也凡所以供試之
事與所以防之者視昔加備
且嚴而相與維持賛襄於外
===
著則左叅政熊〔祿〕右叅政陳
〔周〕常〔麟〕李〔延壽〕副使崔〔文奎〕張〔恕〕
陳〔壮〕左叅議康〔紹宗〕右叅議温
〔璽〕僉事馬〔騆〕閻〔璽〕王〔欽〕沙〔立〕
實皆心志克協共濟厥業也
〔鼎〕等受事惟謹窮晝夜竭精
力公去取摘其文之合程式
punctuated:
寅試之，丁巳再試之，庚申三試之。來試之士一千六百有畸，皆董學副使車〔璽〕之所造就、校閱，而巡按御史又從而覆簡之者也。凡所以供試之事與所以防之者，視昔加備且嚴。而相與維持賛襄於外著，則左叅政熊〔祿〕、右叅政陳〔周〕、常〔麟〕、李〔延壽〕、副使崔〔文奎〕、張〔恕〕、陳〔壮〕、左叅議康〔紹宗〕、右叅議温〔璽〕、僉事馬〔騆〕、閻〔璽〕、王〔欽〕、沙〔立〕，實皆心志克協，共濟厥業也。
〔鼎〕等受事惟謹，窮晝夜，竭精力，公去取，摘其文之合程式
translation_en:
…on the jiayin day, they were examined; on the dingsi day, they were examined a second time; and on the gengshen day, a third time. More than sixteen hundred candidates came to sit the examination. All had been trained and assessed by Che Xi, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner overseeing education, and subsequently reviewed and selected by the Regional Inspector. All arrangements for conducting the examination and guarding against abuses were more thorough and stringent than before. Those who jointly sustained and assisted the work outside the examination compound [?] were Xiong Lu, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; Chen Zhou, Chang Lin, and Li Yanshou, Administration Vice Commissioners of the Right; Cui Wenkui, Zhang Shu, and Chen Zhuang, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Kang Shaozong, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left; Wen Xi, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Right; and Ma Diao, Yan Xi, Wang Qin, and Sha Li, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. They were truly united in purpose and worked together to accomplish their task.
Ding and his colleagues undertook their duties with utmost care, working throughout day and night and exhausting their energies. Impartial in rejecting or accepting candidates, they selected those essays that conformed to the prescribed standards…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
者得八十人遵
制額也爰次其姓氏與其文之
尤者萃而為錄〔鼎〕當序其首
自鄉舉里選之法壞後世始
設科以取士若孝悌力田若
孝廉賢良若博學宏詞明經
進士諸科是也時勢益殊取
===
士之法不得不歸之科舉然
在諸士子特進身之階耳古
之人所以取重於當時流聲
實於後世者或以道德或以
功業或以文章而科第不與
焉今爾諸士子登名斯錄行
當上春官對
punctuated:
者，得八十人，遵制額也。爰次其姓氏，與其文之尤者，萃而為錄。〔鼎〕當序其首。
自鄉舉里選之法壞，後世始設科以取士，若孝悌力田，若孝廉賢良，若博學宏詞、明經、進士諸科是也。時勢益殊，取士之法不得不歸之科舉。然在諸士子，特進身之階耳。古之人所以取重於當時、流聲實於後世者，或以道德，或以功業，或以文章，而科第不與焉。今爾諸士子登名斯錄，行當上春官，對
translation_en:
…we obtained eighty men, conforming to the quota prescribed by imperial decree. We therefore arranged their names in order and compiled them, together with the finest of their writings, into this record. It falls to Ding to write the preface at its beginning.
After the system of recommending men from the districts and selecting them from the villages broke down, later generations began establishing categories for recruiting officials. These included filial devotion, fraternal respect, and diligence in farming; filial devotion and incorruptibility; worthiness and goodness; broad learning and literary accomplishment; mastery of the Classics; and jinshi. As circumstances changed ever further, the recruitment of officials inevitably came to depend on the civil-service examinations. Yet for you candidates, these are merely a step toward advancement. The men of antiquity who won esteem in their own day and transmitted their reputation and substantive achievements to later generations did so through moral virtue, accomplishments in service, or literary writings; examination rank played no part in this. Now you candidates have your names inscribed in this record. Soon you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites and answer…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
大廷鄉里榮之親戚榮之朋友榮
之可樂也然方其始進也人
惟科第之榮及其既仕也則
將官守言責是求備焉一弗
勝則辱及矣其不大可懼哉
可樂而以懼樂斯在矣懼非
患難樂非安榮弗樂猶可弗
===
懼債我古今人有進身於科
第而正直而忠誠而廉潔而
功業文章赫然琅然為天下
後世所仰望者則懼其無之
也有進身於科第而脂韋而
激詭而貪墨敗度而不恤居
職早計後來者則懼其有之
punctuated:
大廷，鄉里榮之，親戚榮之，朋友榮之，可樂也。然方其始進也，人惟科第之榮；及其既仕也，則將官守言責，是求備焉。一弗勝，則辱及矣，其不大可懼哉！可樂而以懼，樂斯在矣。懼非患難，樂非安榮。弗樂猶可，弗懼債我。
古今人有進身於科第，而正直而忠誠而廉潔，而功業文章赫然琅然，為天下後世所仰望者，則懼其無之也；有進身於科第，而脂韋而激詭，而貪墨敗度，而不恤居職、早計後來者，則懼其有之
translation_en:
…at the imperial court. Your fellow villagers take pride in you, your relatives take pride in you, and your friends take pride in you: this is cause for joy. Yet when you first advance, people consider only the glory of examination success. Once you enter office, however, they will demand that you fully discharge your official duties and your responsibility to speak out. Fail in any one of these, and disgrace will follow. Is this not greatly to be feared? When you temper occasions for joy with fear, true joy lies therein. Fear is not calamity, nor is joy ease and honor. To be without joy may still be permissible; to be without fear incurs a debt [?].
Among people past and present, some have advanced through examination success and have been upright, loyal, sincere, and incorruptible, their achievements resplendent and their writings ringing clear, winning the admiration of the world and of later generations. You should fear that you lack these qualities. Others have advanced through examination success but have been pliant and accommodating, extreme and devious, corrupt and destructive of established standards, neglecting their duties in office while planning early for their future advantage. You should fear that you possess these faults…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
也懼可既哉無其所可懼則
有其所可樂是故達之而可
行窮之而可傳內之而心其
民外之而心其君畢之而無
不宜高之而無不勝樂又可
既哉則
聖詔所謂名實相稱者其庶幾乎
===
不知出此徒以科第為蹊徑
而惟世俗耳目是關以役其
心焉其不負科目負所學負
人望也哉姑以是勗諸子
順天府通州儒學學正逯〔鼒〕
謹序
punctuated:
也。懼可既哉？無其所可懼，則有其所可樂。是故達之而可行，窮之而可傳，內之而心其民，外之而心其君，畢之而無不宜，高之而無不勝。樂又可既哉？則聖詔所謂名實相稱者，其庶幾乎！不知出此，徒以科第為蹊徑，而惟世俗耳目是關，以役其心焉，其不負科目、負所學、負人望也哉？姑以是勗諸子。
順天府通州儒學學正逯〔鼒〕謹序。
translation_en:
… Can such apprehension ever end? If there is nothing to occasion apprehension, then there is something to rejoice in. Thus, in advancement, one’s learning can be put into practice; in obscurity, it can be handed down. Inwardly, one takes the people to heart; outwardly, one takes the ruler to heart [?]. Carried through to completion, nothing is inappropriate; raised on high, there is nothing it cannot sustain. Can such joy ever end? Then one might approach what the sagely edict calls “reputation and reality matching one another”!
If one does not know to follow this course, but merely treats examination success as a shortcut, attending only to what the world hears and sees and enslaving one’s mind to it, would one not betray the examination system, betray one’s learning, and betray others’ expectations? For now, I offer these words to exhort you gentlemen.
Preface respectfully written by Lu 〔Zi〕, School Instructor of the Confucian School of Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture.

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
弘治十四年河南鄉試
監臨官
巡按河南監察御史羅賢〔大用山西清源縣人庚戌進士〕
提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使李進〔時勉山西曲沃縣人己丑進士〕
河南等處承宣布政使司右布政使曹元〔以貞大寧前衞官籍直隷含山縣人乙未進士〕
監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使文貴〔天爵湖廣湘鄉縣籍廣寧左屯衞人乙未進士〕
河南等處提刑按察司僉事彭綱〔性仁江西清江縣人乙未進士〕
===
考試官
順天府通州儒學學正逯鼐〔調元山東章丘縣人壬子貢士〕
直隷松江府儒學訓導陳言〔大猷浙江慈谿縣人丙午貢士〕
同考試官
陜西延安府鄜州儒學學正張曙〔啓東遼東廣寧左衞人乙卯貢士〕
湖廣武昌府通城縣儒學教諭劉濟望〔充仁江西安福縣人丙午貢士〕
山西潞州長子縣儒學教諭亢時霖〔希說陜西藍田縣人丙午貢士〕
湖廣武昌府江夏縣儒學教諭朱淤〔源潔福建晋江縣人己酉貢士〕
應天府溧水縣儒學教諭曾憲〔勉章江西泰和縣人己酉貢士〕
punctuated:
弘治十四年河南鄉試

監臨官
巡按河南監察御史羅賢〔大用，山西清源縣人，庚戌進士〕。

提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使李進〔時勉，山西曲沃縣人，己丑進士〕。
河南等處承宣布政使司右布政使曹元〔以貞，大寧前衞官籍，直隷含山縣人，乙未進士〕。

監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使文貴〔天爵，湖廣湘鄉縣籍，廣寧左屯衞人，乙未進士〕。
河南等處提刑按察司僉事彭綱〔性仁，江西清江縣人，乙未進士〕。

考試官
順天府通州儒學學正逯鼐〔調元，山東章丘縣人，壬子貢士〕。
直隷松江府儒學訓導陳言〔大猷，浙江慈谿縣人，丙午貢士〕。

同考試官
陜西延安府鄜州儒學學正張曙〔啓東，遼東廣寧左衞人，乙卯貢士〕。
湖廣武昌府通城縣儒學教諭劉濟望〔充仁，江西安福縣人，丙午貢士〕。
山西潞州長子縣儒學教諭亢時霖〔希說，陜西藍田縣人，丙午貢士〕。
湖廣武昌府江夏縣儒學教諭朱淤〔源潔，福建晋江縣人，己酉貢士〕。
應天府溧水縣儒學教諭曾憲〔勉章，江西泰和縣人，己酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Henan Provincial Examination, the Fourteenth Year of Hongzhi (1501)

Supervising Official
Luo Xian, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Henan, courtesy name Dayong, was a native of Qingyuan County, Shanxi, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the gengxu year.

Proctors
Li Jin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan, courtesy name Shimian, was a native of Quwo County, Shanxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Cao Yuan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan, courtesy name Yizhen, was registered in an officer household of the Daning Front Guard. He was a native of Hanshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili) and a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Examination Inspectors
Wen Gui, Surveillance Commissioner of Henan, courtesy name Tianjue, was registered in Xiangxiang County, Huguang, and was a native of the Guangning Left Garrison Guard. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.
Peng Gang, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Henan, courtesy name Xingren, was a native of Qingjiang County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Examiners
Lu Nai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, courtesy name Diaoyuan, was a native of Zhangqiu County, Shandong, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the renzi year.
Chen Yan, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Dayou, was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student of the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners
Zhang Shu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Fuzhou, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, courtesy name Qidong, was a native of the Guangning Left Guard, Liaodong, and a tribute student of the yimao year.
Liu Jiwang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Tongcheng County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Chongren, was a native of Anfu County, Jiangxi, and a tribute student of the bingwu year.
Kang Shilin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Changzi County, Luzhou, Shanxi, courtesy name Xishuo, was a native of Lantian County, Shaanxi, and a tribute student of the bingwu year.

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
當仁不讓於師
道也者不可須臾離也可離非道也是故
君子戒愼乎其所不睹恐懼乎其所
不聞莫見乎隱莫顯乎微故君子愼
其獨也喜怒哀樂之未發謂之中發
而皆中節謂之和中也者天下之大
本也和也者天下之達道也
易其田疇薄其稅斂民可使富也食之以
時用之以禮財不可勝用也
===
易
勞謙君子萬民服也
利有攸往利涉大川
是故蓍之德圓而神卦之德方以知六爻
之義易以貢
萬物出乎震震東方也齊乎巽巽東南也
齊也者言萬物之潔齊也離也者明
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

當仁，不讓於師。

道也者，不可須臾離也；可離，非道也。是故君子戒愼乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所不聞。莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子愼其獨也。喜怒哀樂之未發，謂之中；發而皆中節，謂之和。中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。

易其田疇，薄其稅斂，民可使富也。食之以時，用之以禮，財不可勝用也。

易

勞謙君子，萬民服也。

利有攸往，利涉大川。

是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。

萬物出乎震，震，東方也。齊乎巽，巽，東南也。齊也者，言萬物之潔齊也。離也者，明
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When faced with the practice of humaneness, do not yield even to your teacher.

The Way cannot be departed from for even a moment. If it could be departed from, it would not be the Way. Therefore, the gentleman is watchful over what he does not see and apprehensive about what he does not hear. Nothing is more manifest than what is hidden, and nothing more evident than what is minute. Thus the gentleman is vigilant when alone. Before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise, this is called equilibrium; when they arise and all attain their proper measure, this is called harmony. Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven.

Cultivate their fields and lighten their taxes, and the people can be made prosperous. Consume resources at the proper seasons and use them according to ritual propriety, and wealth will be inexhaustible.

Book of Changes

The gentleman who labors yet remains modest commands the allegiance of the myriad people.

It is beneficial to have somewhere to go; it is beneficial to cross the great river.

Thus the virtue of the milfoil stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and wise; the meaning of the six lines is to disclose through change.

The myriad things emerge in Zhen. Zhen is the east. They come into orderly array in Xun. Xun is the southeast. By ‘coming into orderly array’ is meant that the myriad things become fully and neatly arrayed. Li means brightness …

面而聽天下嚮明而治益取諸此也
坤也者地也萬物皆致養焉故曰致
役乎坤兊正秋也萬物之所說也故
曰說言乎兊戰乎乾乾西北之卦也
言陰陽相薄也坎者水也正北方之
卦也勞卦也萬物之所歸也故曰勞
乎坎艮東北之卦也萬物之所成終
而所成始也故曰成言乎艮
===
書
食哉惟時柔遠能邇惇德允元而難任人
蠻夷率服
克享天心受天明命
而靡而色曰予攸好德
昔君文武丕平富不務咎底至齊信用昭
明于天下則亦有熊羆之士不二心
之臣保乂王家用端命于上帝皇天
用訓厥道付畀四方
punctuated:
也，萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，益取諸此也。坤也者，地也，萬物皆致養焉，故曰：「致役乎坤。」兊，正秋也，萬物之所說也，故曰：「說言乎兊。」戰乎乾，乾，西北之卦也，言陰陽相薄也。坎者，水也，正北方之卦也，勞卦也，萬物之所歸也，故曰：「勞乎坎。」艮，東北之卦也，萬物之所成終而所成始也，故曰：「成言乎艮。」

書

食哉惟時，柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人，蠻夷率服。

克享天心，受天明命。

而靡而色，曰：「予攸好德。」

昔君文武，丕平富，不務咎，底至齊信用昭明于天下，則亦有熊羆之士、不二心之臣，保乂王家，用端命于上帝。皇天用訓厥道，付畀四方。
translation_en:
…brightness; all things become visible to one another. It is the trigram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern; he also [?] takes his example from this. Kun is earth: all things receive nourishment from it. Hence it is said, “They perform their service in Kun.” Dui is mid-autumn, in which all things rejoice. Hence it is said, “They rejoice in Dui.” “They contend in Qian”: Qian is the trigram of the northwest, signifying that yin and yang press against one another. Kan is water, the trigram of due north. It is the trigram of toil, to which all things return. Hence it is said, “They toil in Kan.” Gen is the trigram of the northeast, where all things complete their ending and establish their beginning. Hence it is said, “They reach completion in Gen.”

Book of Documents

Food! Attend to it at the proper time. Be gentle toward those far away and welcoming toward those nearby; esteem the virtuous and trust the good, but make it difficult for flatterers to advance. Then the Man and Yi peoples will all submit.

He was able to win Heaven’s favor and receive Heaven’s illustrious mandate.

Your demeanor is yielding [?], and you say, “What I cherish is virtue.”

The former rulers, Wen and Wu, brought great peace and prosperity. They did not make punishment their chief concern, but attained the utmost impartiality and trustworthiness, thereby displaying their brilliance throughout all under Heaven. They also had warriors like bears and great bears, and ministers of undivided loyalty, who protected and governed the royal house, thereby securing its mandate from the Lord on High. August Heaven accordingly approved their Way and entrusted the four quarters to them.

translation_en:
Book of Odes

He looked toward Chu and Tang, surveying the hills and high mounds.

When the guests first took their places at the mats, those to left and right were in orderly array. The bamboo and wooden vessels were neatly arranged; meats and fruits were set out. The wine was mild and fine, and the drinkers were in complete harmony. Bells and drums were in place; they offered toasts with easy grace. The great archery target was raised, and bows and arrows were made ready. The archers had assembled: display your skill in shooting! Shoot at that target to seek your cup of wine.

Solemn and majestic was King Wen. Ah, ever radiant was his reverence! Great indeed was Heaven’s mandate!

May you be aided in attaining venerable old age and preserve it forever. Truly splendid and abundant are the blessings! Illustrious and accomplished lords, may you be blessed with manifold good fortune and brought to enduring brilliance amid great blessings.

是故清明象天廣大象地終始象四時周
===
還象風雨五色成文而不亂八風從
律而不姦百度得數而有常小大相
成終始相生倡和清濁迭相為經故

Book of Rites
Ritual and righteousness are employed as instruments; thus the conduct of affairs has a standard against which it may be examined.
Thus, in its purity and brightness, [music] resembles Heaven; in its breadth and greatness, it resembles Earth; in its endings and beginnings, it resembles the four seasons; in its recurring cycles, it resembles wind and rain. The five colors form patterns without disorder; the winds of the eight directions follow the pitch standards without deviation; the many measures attain their proper numerical proportions and have constancy. Small and great complete one another; ending and beginning generate one another; the leading and responding voices, the high and low tones, take turns providing the guiding thread. Thus, when music is performed, relationships become clear, hearing and sight become keen, blood and vital energy become harmonious and balanced, prevailing practices and customs are transformed, and all under Heaven are at peace.
The uses of material things are brought to fulfillment so as to establish guiding norms for the people.
The meaning of the district drinking ceremony is this: the host bows and welcomes the guest outside the gate of the district school. Upon entering, they exchange three bows before reaching the steps, and yield precedence three times before ascending. This fully expresses respect and deference. Washing the hands, washing the cup, and raising the drinking goblet fully express purity. Bowing at the guest’s arrival…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第叄塲
策〔五道〕
問我
太祖皇帝既定天下致太平懼臣民之或悍于
法也乃製
大誥以昭示之使皆知所趨避伏讀
官親起稿一章有曰秦不可法自周至于漢
晉唐宋當時賢人君子臣於斯歷代者受任
方隅所任之事必躬親理之又伏讀胡元制
===
治一章有曰臨政之時袖手高坐謀由吏出
縱是文章之士不異胡人大哉
皇言一哉
皇心蓋深懲胡元以吏為源之弊而警飭臣工
以勤自勵以惰自戒也
聖訓流布瀰久彌彰
聖子神孫率由靡忘所以百數十年來勤實道
昌浮惰俗革官稱其職吏供其役治效
之盛比隆成周而軼漢晉唐宋矣夫古
punctuated:
第叄塲
策〔五道〕
問：我太祖皇帝既定天下，致太平，懼臣民之或悍于法也，乃製《大誥》以昭示之，使皆知所趨避。伏讀〈官親起稿〉一章，有曰：「秦不可法。自周至于漢、晉、唐、宋，當時賢人君子臣於斯歷代者，受任方隅，所任之事必躬親理之。」又伏讀〈胡元制治〉一章，有曰：「臨政之時，袖手高坐，謀由吏出，縱是文章之士，不異胡人。」大哉，皇言！一哉，皇心！蓋深懲胡元以吏為源之弊，而警飭臣工以勤自勵，以惰自戒也。聖訓流布，瀰久彌彰。聖子神孫率由靡忘，所以百數十年來，勤實道昌，浮惰俗革，官稱其職，吏供其役。治效之盛，比隆成周，而軼漢、晉、唐、宋矣。夫古
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕
Question: After our Emperor Taizu had pacified All Under Heaven and brought about great peace, he feared that some among his subjects might defy the law. He therefore composed the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) to instruct them clearly, so that all would know what to pursue and what to avoid. Reverently reading the chapter “Officials Must Personally Draft Documents,” we find it states: “Qin cannot serve as a model. From Zhou through Han, Jin, Tang, and Song, the worthy and exemplary men who served as subjects under these successive dynasties, when entrusted with regional responsibilities, invariably attended personally to the affairs committed to them.” Again, reverently reading the chapter “Governance under the Mongol Yuan,” we find it states: “When administering government, they sit aloof with hands tucked into their sleeves, leaving plans to originate with clerks. Even if they are men of literary accomplishment, they are no different from the Mongols.” How great are these imperial words! How consistent is the imperial mind! They profoundly condemn the failing of the Mongol Yuan in making clerks the source of governmental action, and admonish officials to spur themselves on through diligence and guard against indolence.
The sagely instructions have circulated widely, becoming ever more manifest with the passage of time. His sagely sons and divine grandsons have followed them without forgetting. Thus, for more than a hundred years, diligence and substantive achievement have flourished, while habits of superficiality and indolence have been reformed. Officials have fulfilled their offices, and clerks have performed their duties. The splendid results of this governance rival the flourishing Zhou and surpass Han, Jin, Tang, and Song. Now, in ancient times…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
昔方隅之臣能親理所任之事者多矣
姑舉一二與諸生論之北山大夫朝夕
從事城彼東方夙夜匪懈何事不親理
也諸生講之乎賢否盡知各有記籍精
力推行不辭米鹽何事不親理也諸生
慕之乎惜分陰而屏曠達者人謂其似
孔明勤勸課而絕縱橫者自謂某繼芊
公有政尚清毅吏不敢犯者有數陳剖
判下筆如流者洗雪寃滯何瘴癘之不
===
悼簿書文檄何檢察之必親之數子者
果如
聖制之所指乎抑亦有當式效者乎綜核名實
漢道以興清虛相尚晉轍不洛近年以
來俗尚漸移日享優閑者目之為高致
歲困簿書者槩之以常員此其漸不可
不塞也昔人有云諸公道德恢弘當令
之世稱俗吏者非我而何其言是歟非
歟文章可以潤身政事可以及物其言
punctuated: 昔方隅之臣，能親理所任之事者多矣。姑舉一二與諸生論之。北山大夫，朝夕從事；城彼東方，夙夜匪懈。何事不親理也？諸生講之乎？賢否盡知，各有記籍；精力推行，不辭米鹽。何事不親理也？諸生慕之乎？惜分陰而屏曠達者，人謂其似孔明；勤勸課而絕縱橫者，自謂某繼芊公。有政尚清毅、吏不敢犯者，有數陳剖判、下筆如流者。洗雪寃滯，何瘴癘之不悼？簿書文檄，何檢察之必親？之數子者，果如聖制之所指乎？抑亦有當式效者乎？綜核名實，漢道以興；清虛相尚，晉轍不洛。近年以來，俗尚漸移，日享優閑者目之為高致，歲困簿書者槩之以常員。此其漸不可不塞也。昔人有云：「諸公道德恢弘，當令之世稱俗吏者，非我而何？」其言是歟非歟？文章可以潤身，政事可以及物，其言
translation_en:
…in former times, many officials serving in the regions personally attended to the affairs entrusted to them. Let us take one or two examples and discuss them with you candidates. The officer of “Northern Mountain” performed his duties morning and evening; those who “built fortifications in the east” were unremitting day and night. What business did they not attend to personally? Have you candidates studied these examples? Knowing fully who was worthy and who was not, keeping records of each, energetically carrying measures into effect, and not disdaining even the minutiae of rice and salt—what business did such an official not attend to personally? Do you candidates admire him?

The man who treasured every moment and rejected careless unconcern was said to resemble Kongming. The man who diligently encouraged and supervised work and rejected political maneuvering said of himself, “I carry on the work of Lord Qian [?].” There were those whose administration prized integrity and firmness, so that subordinate clerks dared not transgress; there were those who set out figures and adjudicated cases [?], their writing flowing freely. In redressing long-standing injustices, what suffering from pestilential vapors did they not deplore? Why did they insist on personally inspecting registers, documents, and proclamations? Did these several men indeed exemplify what the imperial decree indicates? Or were there also things about them that ought to serve as models for imitation?

By comprehensively scrutinizing names against actual performance, the Han brought its governance to flourishing prosperity; by mutually esteeming purity and emptiness, the Jin’s course “did not Luo” [?; the text is unclear]. In recent years, prevailing attitudes have gradually changed. Those who enjoy leisure day after day are regarded as men of lofty refinement, while those who toil over registers year after year are dismissed as ordinary functionaries. This developing tendency must be checked. Someone of old said: “You gentlemen are expansive in moral cultivation; if anyone in the present age [?] is to be called a commonplace official, who could it be but me?” Was this statement right or wrong? “Literary accomplishment can adorn oneself; administrative service can benefit others”—this statement…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
又是歟非歟今欲槩古人之言行考
聖製以不謬落浮惰獎勤實是必有道諸生服
膺
聖訓飽抱而來不宜遜讓明著于篇以觀所學
問上之求才士之求進其為道一也諸生
知之乎法行而道非盡善弊生而法隨
以隳其為勢一也諸生又知之乎是故
科舉以取之資格以敘之而天下人才
盡在羅籠之中而不能逸矣使上古聖
===
王復生不能舍是以取士使上古賢臣
復生不能外是以進身其勢則然也莫
公於科舉厥後乃有不公之訾莫常於
資格厥後乃有不常之誚昔人有曰古
人行已似不如此又曰爵位品秩一一
稱滿其意將無以役使羣臣語其法如
是而況於徇情者乎風行於上而成於
下道二於此而原於彼試與諸生論之
悉黜請托視私其鄉人者何如不造郡
punctuated:
又是歟非歟？今欲槩古人之言行，考聖製以不謬，落浮惰，獎勤實，是必有道。諸生服膺聖訓，飽抱而來，不宜遜讓，明著于篇，以觀所學。
問：上之求才，士之求進，其為道一也，諸生知之乎？法行而道非盡善，弊生而法隨以隳，其為勢一也，諸生又知之乎？是故科舉以取之，資格以敘之，而天下人才盡在羅籠之中而不能逸矣。使上古聖王復生，不能舍是以取士；使上古賢臣復生，不能外是以進身，其勢則然也。莫公於科舉，厥後乃有不公之訾；莫常於資格，厥後乃有不常之誚。昔人有曰：「古人行已似不如此。」又曰：「爵位品秩，一一稱滿其意，將無以役使羣臣。」語其法如是，而況於徇情者乎？風行於上而成於下，道二於此而原於彼。試與諸生論之：悉黜請托，視私其鄉人者何如？不造郡
translation_en:
…is this statement, too, right or wrong? Now, if we wish to assess the words and deeds of the ancients, examine the imperial composition without error, dismiss the frivolous and indolent, and reward the diligent and conscientious, there must be a way to do so. You candidates take the imperial instructions to heart and have come fully imbued with them [?]. You should not hold back out of modesty: set forth your views clearly in your essays, so that your learning may be seen.
Question: The ruler’s search for talent and the scholar’s pursuit of advancement follow one and the same path. Do you candidates understand this? When regulations are implemented but the way they operate is not wholly sound, abuses arise and the regulations consequently fall into disrepair: this, too, is a consistent tendency. Do you candidates also understand this? Thus, men are selected through the civil-service examinations and ranked according to qualifications and seniority, so that all the talented men of the realm are caught within the net and cannot escape. Were the sage kings of high antiquity to return to life, they could not dispense with this means of selecting scholars; were the worthy ministers of high antiquity to return to life, they could not advance themselves outside it. Such is the force of circumstances. Nothing is more impartial than the examinations, yet subsequently accusations of partiality arose; nothing is more constant than ranking by qualifications and seniority, yet subsequently charges of inconsistency arose. Someone of former times said, “The ancients seem not to have conducted themselves in this way.” Another saying runs, “If noble titles and official ranks satisfy every one of their wishes, there will be no means of directing the service of the assembled ministers.” If this can be said of the regulations themselves, how much more does it apply to those who act out of personal favor? A practice spreads from those above and becomes established among those below; the way diverges here, but has its source there [?]. Let us discuss this with you candidates: how does rejecting all requests for personal intercession compare with favoring one’s fellow townsmen? Not visiting the prefectural …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
齋視投牒求進者何如以舍人而四遷
至五大夫以大僕而三賜至執圭視徒
步數年至封侯一言句月取宰相者何
如科舉不能累人自是人累科舉故殿
前對策者道學自傳進士題名者大成
是集待常才以資待非常之才以望故
有舉處士甚登三事者有舉郡守堪為
宰相者法無不可人則萬殊科舉之行
久矣或有以貫人之行為法累者君子
===
則曰彼無我與也而高見遠識之士抑
有不局於科舉者乎資格之行久矣而
超資越次者亦比比也抑有抱眞蓄大
晦不自售陸沉於下者乎士而不局於
科舉是其所以進身者特施其餘耳而
其所獨到者固非科舉所能累而亦不
累之也士而拘於資格而不得盡其才
展其志則其所能為與其所當為又有
出於仕進之外者矣道有所極至勢有
punctuated: 齋，視投牒求進者何如？以舍人而四遷至五大夫，以大僕而三賜至執圭，視徒步數年至封侯、一言句月取宰相者何如？科舉不能累人，自是人累科舉。故殿前對策者，道學自傳；進士題名者，大成是集。待常才以資，待非常之才以望。故有舉處士甚登三事者，有舉郡守堪為宰相者。法無不可，人則萬殊。科舉之行久矣，或有以貫人之行為法累者，君子則曰：「彼無我與也。」而高見遠識之士，抑有不局於科舉者乎？資格之行久矣，而超資越次者亦比比也。抑有抱眞蓄大、晦不自售、陸沉於下者乎？士而不局於科舉，是其所以進身者特施其餘耳，而其所獨到者固非科舉所能累，而亦不累之也。士而拘於資格，而不得盡其才、展其志，則其所能為與其所當為，又有出於仕進之外者矣。道有所極至，勢有
translation_en:
…the prefectural study: how do such men compare with those who submit petitions seeking advancement? Those who rose from retainer through four promotions to Grandee of the Fifth Rank, or from Grand Coachman through three grants to Holder of the Jade Tablet—how do they compare with men who rose from commoner to enfeoffed marquis within a few years, or obtained the chief ministership through a single utterance in a matter of months [?]? The examination system cannot compromise men; it is men themselves who compromise the examination system. Thus, among those answering policy questions before the throne were men whose Learning of the Way secured their enduring reputation; among those whose names appeared on the lists of metropolitan graduates were men who brought learning to its fullest accomplishment. Ordinary talent is treated according to qualifications, extraordinary talent according to reputation. Thus some recommended scholars living in retirement as fit to ascend to the Three Excellencies [?], while others recommended commandery governors as capable of serving as chief ministers. There is nothing inherently unworkable in the regulations; people, however, differ in countless ways.

The examination system has long been in operation. Some may let people’s conduct bring the regulations into disrepute [?], but the gentleman says: “That has nothing to do with me.” Among men of lofty insight and far-reaching discernment, might there also be some who are not confined by the examinations? The system of qualifications and seniority has long been in operation, yet men who transcend their standing and leap over the prescribed sequence are also found everywhere. Might there also be men who cherish what is true and nurture great capacities, remain obscure without advertising themselves, and languish unnoticed in lowly circumstances?

For a scholar not confined by the examinations, the means by which he advances himself amount merely to putting his spare capacities to use. His distinctive attainments are certainly beyond the examinations’ power to compromise, and neither does he compromise the examinations. If a scholar is constrained by qualifications and seniority and cannot fully employ his talents or realize his aspirations, then what he can do and what he ought to do also extend beyond advancement in office. The Way has its utmost reaches, and circumstances have…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
所不能拘此非分外事予曰盍各言爾
志趙孟曰請七子皆賦以觀鄭志
問今北虜跳梁侵擾三邊烏合星散出沒
無常防此則窺彼備東則寇西聚多則
士卒不充布少則侵軼莫禦誠不可不
慮也夫戎狄之患久矣備禦之畧多矣
諸生能言之乎或陳征伐之謀或立表
餌之說或興和親之議或建農戰之策
或築三城於磧口或建三城於西南或
===
欲蓄之以犬羊或欲移兵於邊郡或欲
之以金幣或假之以封號其利害得失
可得而言歟抑亦有可行於今者歟兩
年以来士不解甲農不停餉而克捷之
功未聞烽燧之警猶急豈將帥之不得
其人歟抑有所牵制而不得展其力歟
將十羊九牧而謀不斷歟抑敗軍者逋
誅逗留者受賞安居者論功死戰者不
録而士卒解體不用命歟將謂進死退
punctuated:
所不能拘，此非分外事。予曰：「盍各言爾志？」趙孟曰：「請七子皆賦，以觀鄭志。」
問：今北虜跳梁，侵擾三邊，烏合星散，出沒無常。防此則窺彼，備東則寇西；聚多則士卒不充，布少則侵軼莫禦，誠不可不慮也。夫戎狄之患久矣，備禦之畧多矣，諸生能言之乎？或陳征伐之謀，或立表餌之說，或興和親之議，或建農戰之策，或築三城於磧口，或建三城於西南，或欲蓄之以犬羊，或欲移兵於邊郡，或欲之以金幣，或假之以封號，其利害得失可得而言歟？抑亦有可行於今者歟？兩年以来，士不解甲，農不停餉，而克捷之功未聞，烽燧之警猶急。豈將帥之不得其人歟？抑有所牵制而不得展其力歟？將十羊九牧而謀不斷歟？抑敗軍者逋誅，逗留者受賞，安居者論功，死戰者不録，而士卒解體不用命歟？將謂進死退
translation_en:
…what circumstances cannot constrain; this is no matter beyond one’s proper duty. I say: “Why does each of you not state your aspirations?” Zhao Meng said: “Let all seven gentlemen recite an ode, so that we may observe the aspirations of Zheng.”
Question: The northern raiders now run rampant, harassing the three frontier regions. They gather like crows and scatter like stars, appearing and disappearing unpredictably. Defend this place, and they spy out opportunities elsewhere; prepare in the east, and they raid the west. Concentrate troops in large numbers, and there are insufficient soldiers to fill the ranks; distribute them in small detachments, and their incursions cannot be checked. This is indeed a matter that demands consideration. The troubles caused by the Rong and Di have long persisted, and many strategies for defense have been devised. Can you candidates discuss them? Some have proposed punitive campaigns; some have advocated displays of strength and material inducements; some have urged peace through marriage alliances; some have proposed combining agriculture with warfare. Some built three fortified cities at Qikou; some established three fortified cities in the southwest. Some wished to rear them like dogs and sheep; some wished to transfer troops to the frontier commanderies; some wished to use gold and silk to [win them over?]; some would grant them titles of enfeoffment. Can you explain the advantages and disadvantages, successes and failures, of these measures? Are any of them practicable today?
For two years, soldiers have not taken off their armor, and farmers have not ceased supplying provisions, yet no achievements in victory have been heard of, and the alarms from the beacon towers remain urgent. Is this because the commanders are not the right men? Or are they constrained in ways that prevent them from exerting their strength? Is it a case of ten sheep with nine shepherds, so that plans never reach a decision? Or do those who lose armies escape execution, those who delay their advance receive rewards, those who remain safely at ease have their merits assessed, and those who fight to the death receive no recognition, so that the soldiers lose cohesion and refuse to obey orders? Or do they say that to advance means death, while to retreat…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
生預有為之所者而一切不戰歟抑士
素不訓練而見敵恐怖歟將謀畧勇銳
之士乏而不足用歟抑有之而不知知
之而不舉舉之而不用用之而不專不
能盡其才力歟昔人有言匈奴之衆不
足當漢之一縣今舉天下之全力以禦
之而反罷於奔命其故何歟將隸籍食
粮之兵半役於拳門在邊聽戰之士多
隱於帥幕而彼衆我寡勢反不敵歟備
===
邊之事前代成敗明驗歷歷可考諸生
行將委質若得當一面則何以哉儒者
於天下事皆合理會而況今日之所甚
急人所共憂者乎其敷陳以成策毋委
曰軍旅之事未之學也
問漕運之不可不講也信矣平時以給京
師有事以餉軍旅至重而最急也我
國家建都上地轉漕東南若江浙之東西淮
湖之南北歲漕數百萬石自儀真至通
punctuated:
生，預有為之所者而一切不戰歟？抑士素不訓練而見敵恐怖歟？將謀畧勇銳之士乏而不足用歟？抑有之而不知，知之而不舉，舉之而不用，用之而不專，不能盡其才力歟？昔人有言：「匈奴之衆不足當漢之一縣。」今舉天下之全力以禦之，而反罷於奔命，其故何歟？將隸籍食粮之兵半役於拳門，在邊聽戰之士多隱於帥幕，而彼衆我寡，勢反不敵歟？備邊之事，前代成敗明驗，歷歷可考。諸生行將委質，若得當一面，則何以哉？儒者於天下事皆合理會，而況今日之所甚急、人所共憂者乎？其敷陳以成策，毋委曰：「軍旅之事，未之學也。」
問：漕運之不可不講也，信矣！平時以給京師，有事以餉軍旅，至重而最急也。我國家建都上地，轉漕東南，若江浙之東西、淮湖之南北，歲漕數百萬石，自儀真至通
translation_en:
…survival, having made arrangements for themselves beforehand [?], and thus refuse to fight altogether? Or is it that the soldiers have never been trained and are terrified at the sight of the enemy? Is there a shortage of men with strategic ability, courage, and vigor, leaving too few to employ? Or are such men available but unrecognized; recognized but not recommended; recommended but not employed; or employed but not entrusted with sole responsibility, so that they cannot fully exercise their talents and abilities? Someone in antiquity said: “The multitudes of the Xiongnu cannot match even a single county of the Han.” Now we muster the full strength of the realm to resist them, yet instead exhaust ourselves rushing to meet their incursions. Why is this? Is it that half the soldiers enrolled on the registers and drawing rations serve in powerful households [?], while many of those stationed on the frontier awaiting battle are concealed in commanders’ headquarters, so that the enemy outnumbers us and we are instead unable to match their strength?
In matters of frontier defense, the clear evidence of successes and failures under previous dynasties can be examined in detail. You students will soon pledge yourselves to government service. If entrusted with responsibility for one region, how would you proceed? A Confucian scholar ought to understand all the affairs of the realm, especially those that are most urgent today and cause universal concern. Set forth your views fully in a policy essay; do not evade the matter by saying: “I have not studied military affairs.”
Question: It is certainly true that grain transport by water must be thoroughly considered! In peacetime it supplies the capital; when trouble arises, it provisions the armies. It is a matter of the greatest importance and utmost urgency. Our dynasty established its capital in the northern region and transports grain from the southeast—from east and west throughout Jiang and Zhe, and north and south throughout Huai and Hu. Each year several million shi of grain are transported by water, from Yizhen to Tong…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
州導善河數千里舟楫往來穩於履陸
北方之粟貢本色者亦由水漕齎糴直
者則由陸路川舟引而達橋陸輦驅而
接軫百數十年上下稱便漕法之善前
代莫及比者玁狁匪茹腥羶疆圉出沒
不時禍心叵測至勤
朝廷命將出師遠駐西鄙相持日久糗餉不
給乃移河南粮一十八萬石往饋榆林
今欲運本色則山路阻遠輦馱無由計
===
數石猶恐不能致一石欲齎糴直則邊
郡被毀內地懼旱縱有可買之處而脚
力亦無所措出不得已多費不恤然今
歲役之民力已殫繼此以往役或再興
則將若之何哉誠不可不預講之也夫
歲漕山東四百萬石止用卒六萬人其
法何居歲漕江淮一百一十萬石無升
斗覆溺者其計何在節級轉般視和糴
三輔河東粟者孰優燒石沃醯視開運
punctuated: 州，導善河數千里，舟楫往來，穩於履陸。北方之粟，貢本色者亦由水漕，齎糴直者則由陸路。川舟引而達橋，陸輦驅而接軫。百數十年，上下稱便，漕法之善，前代莫及。比者玁狁匪茹，腥羶疆圉，出沒不時，禍心叵測，至勤朝廷命將出師，遠駐西鄙，相持日久，糗餉不給，乃移河南粮一十八萬石，往饋榆林。今欲運本色，則山路阻遠，輦馱無由，計數石猶恐不能致一石；欲齎糴直，則邊郡被毀，內地懼旱，縱有可買之處，而脚力亦無所措出。不得已，多費不恤，然今歲役之民力已殫，繼此以往，役或再興，則將若之何哉？誠不可不預講之也。夫歲漕山東四百萬石，止用卒六萬人，其法何居？歲漕江淮一百一十萬石，無升斗覆溺者，其計何在？節級轉般，視和糴三輔河東粟者孰優？燒石沃醯，視開運
translation_en:
…zhou [completing Tongzhou on the preceding page], along several thousand li of managed waterways [?]; boats travel back and forth more securely than one walks on land. Of the grain from the north, that tendered as tribute in kind is likewise conveyed by water, while money carried to purchase grain goes by land. River boats proceed in succession and reach the bridges [?], while carts on land follow so closely that their axle ends meet. For more than a hundred years, those above and below have found this convenient; no previous dynasty has equaled the excellence of this grain-transport system.

Recently, the Xianyun, showing no restraint, have fouled our frontier with their rank presence. They appear and disappear unpredictably, and their evil intentions cannot be fathomed. This has even obliged the court to appoint generals and dispatch armies to distant stations on the western border. The confrontation has lasted so long that provisions have become insufficient, and therefore 180,000 shi of grain from Henan have been diverted to supply Yulin. Now, if we wish to transport grain in kind, the mountain roads are difficult and long, with no practicable way for carts or pack animals to pass: we fear that even several shi expended would not suffice to deliver one shi. If we wish to carry money to purchase grain, the frontier prefectures have suffered devastation and the interior fears drought. Even where grain might be bought, there is no way to procure transport labor. With no alternative, we must disregard the additional expense. Yet this year's service has already exhausted the people's strength. If such service should be demanded again hereafter, what are we to do? We truly must consider the matter in advance.

When four million shi of grain were transported annually by water from Shandong using only sixty thousand soldiers, what method was employed? When 1,100,000 shi were transported annually from the Jiang and Huai regions without so much as a sheng or dou being lost through capsizing or sinking, what arrangements made this possible? How does transport by successive relay stages compare with purchasing grain at negotiated prices in the Three Capital Regions and Hedong—which is superior? How does heating rocks and pouring vinegar over them compare with opening a transport…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
道十八里者孰得致瀕海之粟於河北
何如關中之轉輸運冀州之粟於烏巢
何如祁山之牛馬漕運和糴各有短長
緩急所需難執一說故昔人謂將制國
用當權輕重此其爲說始能不頗也今
醜虜陸梁未即殄滅西陲之運河南之
人殆不能免若措置失宜則恐夷患未
除而腹裏已先擾擾諸生抱策來試而
是役之艱亦既目擊之矣明以告我以
===
觀憂世之志
問省饋餉合兵民固本國威夷狄莫良於
屯田古今皆然也試與諸生言之有田
塞下者有田燉煌者田湟中者羌服田
許下者兵強陳項壽春皆設屯田尋收
混一之功關中諸鎮皆置屯田遂臻治
安之效河北諸路大興營田陝西州軍
亦置屯田一以防寇一以足食此前代
屯田之明驗也我
punctuated:
道十八里者孰得？致瀕海之粟於河北，何如關中之轉輸？運冀州之粟於烏巢，何如祁山之牛馬？漕運、和糴各有短長，緩急所需，難執一說。故昔人謂：「將制國用，當權輕重。」此其爲說始能不頗也。今醜虜陸梁，未即殄滅，西陲之運，河南之人殆不能免。若措置失宜，則恐夷患未除，而腹裏已先擾擾。諸生抱策來試，而是役之艱，亦既目擊之矣。明以告我，以觀憂世之志。

問：省饋餉，合兵民，固本國，威夷狄，莫良於屯田，古今皆然也。試與諸生言之：有田塞下者，有田燉煌者；田湟中者羌服，田許下者兵強。陳、項、壽春皆設屯田，尋收混一之功；關中諸鎮皆置屯田，遂臻治安之效；河北諸路大興營田，陝西州軍亦置屯田，一以防寇，一以足食。此前代屯田之明驗也。我
translation_en:
…a route eighteen li long—which method was more effective? How did bringing grain from the coastal regions to Hebei compare with transport through Guanzhong? How did transporting grain from Jizhou to Wuchao compare with using the wooden oxen and flowing horses at Qishan? Waterborne grain transport and government grain purchases at agreed prices each have strengths and weaknesses; requirements vary with the urgency of circumstances, and it is difficult to insist upon a single approach. Thus a man of former times said: “In regulating state expenditure, one must weigh relative priorities.” Only such an argument can avoid being one-sided. Now the vile enemy runs rampant and has yet to be exterminated. The people of Henan can probably not escape the burden of transporting supplies to the western frontier. If arrangements are mishandled, I fear that before the foreign threat is removed, the interior will already have been thrown into turmoil. You candidates have come to sit the examination with policies to offer, and you have already witnessed the hardships of this service. Explain your views clearly to me, so that I may see your commitment to the troubles of the age.

Question: For reducing the burden of provisioning armies, integrating soldiers and civilians, strengthening the home country, and overawing foreign peoples, nothing is better than agricultural colonies. This has been true in antiquity and remains so today. Let us discuss this with you candidates. Some established farms below the frontier fortifications; others established them at Dunhuang. Those who farmed in Huangzhong brought the Qiang into submission; those who farmed at Xu strengthened their armies. Agricultural colonies were established at Chen, Xiang, and Shouchun, and the achievement of unification soon followed. They were established at the various garrisons in Guanzhong, bringing orderly and peaceful government. In the various circuits of Hebei, agricultural estates were extensively developed; agricultural colonies were also established in the prefectures and military prefectures of Shaanxi, in the one case to guard against raiders and in the other to ensure sufficient food. These are clear demonstrations of the effectiveness of agricultural colonies under earlier dynasties. Our …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
太祖皇帝既定四海設衛以治軍給田以啓屯
大率以二分居守八分務農歲收所入
以給軍食以紓民力
神謨聖猷布在天下我
太宗皇帝尤留
聖慮
詔旨丁寧惟恐弗至此
祖宗之時所以食足兵強以征則勝以守則固
也諸生能知之乎承平日久法制漸弛
===
有屯田之名無屯田之實於是兵餉之
出於民者什常八九而州縣歲入有常
歲用日增財力漸竭顧此失彼兵且日
餒知河南衛所有經年不得支升斗者
諸生又知之乎今塞下之屯地廣矣而
都棄於無用徒貽餉丁綑吏之困苦腹
裏之屯地多矣而槩沒於久假徒勞傒
者有司之交爭茲欲令諸邊之卒各田
其地歟則耒耜方施而突騎已至稼穡
punctuated: 太祖皇帝既定四海，設衛以治軍，給田以啓屯，大率以二分居守，八分務農，歲收所入，以給軍食，以紓民力。神謨聖猷，布在天下。我太宗皇帝尤留聖慮，詔旨丁寧，惟恐弗至。此祖宗之時所以食足兵強，以征則勝，以守則固也。諸生能知之乎？承平日久，法制漸弛，有屯田之名，無屯田之實。於是兵餉之出於民者，什常八九，而州縣歲入有常，歲用日增，財力漸竭，顧此失彼，兵且日餒。知河南衛所有經年不得支升斗者，諸生又知之乎？今塞下之屯地廣矣，而都棄於無用，徒貽餉丁綑吏之困苦；腹裏之屯地多矣，而槩沒於久假，徒勞傒者有司之交爭。茲欲令諸邊之卒各田其地歟？則耒耜方施，而突騎已至，稼穡
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizu, having pacified all within the four seas, established guards to administer the troops and allotted land to establish military agricultural colonies. As a general rule, two tenths of the troops performed garrison duties and eight tenths worked at farming. Each year the produce was collected to provision the troops and ease the burden on the people. His inspired plans and sagely designs were put into practice throughout the realm. Our Emperor Taizong devoted particular attention to this matter, issuing earnest and repeated decrees, fearing only that their implementation might fall short. This explains why, under our imperial ancestors, provisions were abundant and the troops strong: victorious in attack and secure in defense. Do you students understand this?

After many years of peace, the regulations have gradually fallen into neglect. Military agricultural colonies exist in name but not in substance. Consequently, eight or nine tenths of military provisions regularly come from the people. Yet the prefectures and counties have fixed annual revenues, while their yearly expenses increase daily. Financial resources are gradually exhausted; attending to one need means neglecting another, and the troops grow increasingly hungry. It is known that some in Henan’s guards and battalions have gone an entire year without receiving even a sheng or dou of grain. Do you students know this as well?

Today the military colony lands along the frontier are extensive, yet they are all abandoned and unused, merely bringing hardship upon supply laborers and harried clerks [?]. The military colony lands in the interior are numerous, yet they have all disappeared into long-standing loans of land, merely embroiling tenants [?] and the responsible authorities in disputes. Should we now require the soldiers along the frontiers each to cultivate their own land? Their plows and spades would scarcely have begun work before enemy assault cavalry arrived, and the crops…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
甫登而蹂踐即及施何策以防之欲令
腹裏之士各田其地歟則欺隱於奸猾
而智能蔽所司之耳目吞占於強大而
力能沮守臣之覈實用何方以處之始
也有衛必有田今或衛遷而田存始也
有田必有屯今則田在而屯亡苟盡歸
於
朝廷則百姓裕盡收於邊廩則戰士飽夫且
耕且戰以食以守今日急務古先良規
詳陳勿諱試將采焉
punctuated: 甫登而蹂踐即及，施何策以防之？欲令腹裏之士各田其地歟？則欺隱於奸猾，而智能蔽所司之耳目；吞占於強大，而力能沮守臣之覈實，用何方以處之？始也有衛必有田，今或衛遷而田存；始也有田必有屯，今則田在而屯亡。苟盡歸於朝廷，則百姓裕；盡收於邊廩，則戰士飽。夫且耕且戰，以食以守，今日急務，古先良規。詳陳勿諱，試將采焉。
translation_en: …the crops have barely ripened before they are trampled. What measures could prevent this? Should the soldiers in the interior each be made to cultivate their allotted land? Yet cunning men fraudulently conceal it, using their cleverness to blind the responsible officials; powerful men seize and occupy it, using their influence to obstruct the local officials’ investigation of the facts. How should this be dealt with? Originally, wherever there was a guard, there was necessarily land; now, in some cases, the guard has moved while its land remains. Originally, wherever there was land, there was necessarily a military farming settlement; now the land remains, but the settlement has disappeared. If all were restored to the imperial court, the common people would have sufficient means; if all the proceeds were gathered into the frontier granaries, the soldiers would have enough to eat. To farm while also fighting, thereby providing sustenance and defending the realm, is an urgent task today and a sound practice inherited from antiquity. Set forth your views in detail without reserve; we shall consider adopting them.
