title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
當仁不讓於師
何瑭
同考試官訓導張　批　〔場中作者多於當仁處講勇為有戾朱傳唯此作得之是用錄出〕
同考試官學正張　批　〔說出以仁為己任而必為的意思足究心於理者〕
考試官訓導陳　批　〔題出揭書初看似易下筆便難此作說出聖人勉人之意隱然在目〕
===
考試官學正逯　批　〔聖人言語渾然而意思深遠此作發揮殆盡〕
任夫理之在己者不遜人之誨己者蓋仁乃理之在己而師則人之誨己者也今任其理而不遜乎師非的然有見者能如是哉昔聖人勉人為仁其意若曰人有此生即有此仁是乃天之尊爵也人之安宅也若畏縮而不敢當不幾於自棄乎必也寬廣其心骨毅然以為己任而擔
punctuated:
第壹場。
四書。
當仁不讓於師。
何瑭。

同考試官訓導張，批：〔場中作者多於當仁處講勇為，有戾朱傳，唯此作得之，是用錄出。〕
同考試官學正張，批：〔說出以仁為己任而必為的意思，足究心於理者。〕
考試官訓導陳，批：〔題出揭書，初看似易，下筆便難。此作說出聖人勉人之意，隱然在目。〕
考試官學正逯，批：〔聖人言語渾然，而意思深遠，此作發揮殆盡。〕

任夫理之在己者，不遜人之誨己者。蓋仁乃理之在己，而師則人之誨己者也。今任其理而不遜乎師，非的然有見者能如是哉？昔聖人勉人為仁，其意若曰：人有此生，即有此仁，是乃天之尊爵也，人之安宅也。若畏縮而不敢當，不幾於自棄乎？必也寬廣其心骨，毅然以為己任而擔
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When undertaking benevolence, do not yield even to your teacher.”
He Tang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: 〔Most writers in this examination interpreted “undertaking benevolence” as acting boldly, contrary to Zhu Xi’s commentary. This composition alone grasps the meaning; it has therefore been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔It brings out the meaning of taking benevolence as one’s own responsibility and necessarily putting it into practice, showing someone who has closely investigated principle [?].〕

Comment by Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: 〔The topic comes from the posted text [?]. At first glance it seems easy, but once one puts brush to paper it becomes difficult. This composition brings out the Sage’s intention in encouraging others, making it subtly perceptible.〕

Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor: 〔The Sage’s words form a seamless whole, while their meaning is profound and far-reaching. This composition expounds that meaning almost exhaustively.〕

In taking responsibility for the principle inherent in oneself, one does not defer to the person who instructs oneself. For benevolence is the principle inherent in oneself, whereas a teacher is the person who instructs oneself. Now, to take responsibility for that principle without deferring even to one’s teacher—could anyone without clear insight accomplish this? When the Sage of old encouraged people to practice benevolence, his meaning was as though he said: With this life, people possess this benevolence. It is Heaven’s exalted rank and humanity’s secure dwelling. If one shrinks back in fear and dares not undertake it, does this not verge on abandoning oneself? One must broaden one’s spirit, resolutely take it as one’s own responsibility, and shoulder …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
當之不自棄以離吾仁也若退託而不肯任不
幾於自暴乎故必弘大其度量奮然以為已責
而負荷之不自暴以舍吾仁也彼師以傳道鮮
惑為事在所當讓也仁則吾所自有而自為之
非有爭也故當勇往而必為視聽此仁言動此
仁于以尊天之尊爵雖師亦何所讓哉師以進
德脩業為教在所必讓也仁則我所固有而自
行之無所爭也故當身體而力行作止此仁語
默此仁于以居人之安宅雖師又安所讓哉夫
===
然則天之賦於我者以全我之所得於天者以
復人之為仁孰有加於此耶抑嘗因聖人之格
言驗聖門之高弟顏子嘗當仁矣而克己復禮
為之必勇仲弓嘗當仁矣而主敬行恕行之必
力師如孔子大聖尤所當讓當時不聞二子以
仁讓聖人為者得無以自為自有之仁而無所
與讓耶有志於仁者必以二子為的而後可
道也者不可須臾離也可離非道也是故
君子戒慎乎其所不睹恐懼乎其所
punctuated:
當之，不自棄以離吾仁也。若退託而不肯任，不幾於自暴乎？故必弘大其度量，奮然以為已責而負荷之，不自暴以舍吾仁也。彼師以傳道鮮惑為事，在所當讓也；仁則吾所自有而自為之，非有爭也。故當勇往而必為，視聽此仁，言動此仁，于以尊天之尊爵，雖師亦何所讓哉？師以進德脩業為教，在所必讓也；仁則我所固有而自行之，無所爭也。故當身體而力行，作止此仁，語默此仁，于以居人之安宅，雖師又安所讓哉？夫然則天之賦於我者以全，我之所得於天者以復，人之為仁孰有加於此耶？抑嘗因聖人之格言，驗聖門之高弟。顏子嘗當仁矣，而克己復禮，為之必勇；仲弓嘗當仁矣，而主敬行恕，行之必力。師如孔子，大聖尤所當讓，當時不聞二子以仁讓聖人為者，得無以自為自有之仁而無所與讓耶？有志於仁者，必以二子為的而後可。

道也者，不可須臾離也；可離，非道也。是故君子戒慎乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所
translation_en:
…shoulder it, without abandoning oneself and thereby departing from one’s benevolence. If one draws back, making excuses and refusing to undertake it, does this not verge on doing violence to oneself? Thus one must broaden one’s capacity, resolutely regard it as one’s own responsibility, and bear its weight, without doing violence to oneself and thereby forsaking one’s benevolence. A teacher makes transmitting the Way and dispelling doubts [?] his task: in this one ought to defer to him. Benevolence, however, is something one possesses oneself and practices oneself; there is no contention involved. Thus one must advance courageously and resolve to practice it: in seeing and hearing, this benevolence; in speech and action, this benevolence. In this way one honors Heaven’s noble rank. Even to a teacher, what deference could there be in this? A teacher instructs one in advancing virtue and cultivating one’s endeavors: in this one must defer to him. Benevolence, however, is inherent in oneself and is practiced by oneself; there is nothing over which to contend. Thus one must embody it and practice it strenuously: in activity and rest, this benevolence; in speech and silence, this benevolence. In this way one dwells in humanity’s peaceful abode. Even to a teacher, how could one defer in this?

Then what Heaven has endowed in me is preserved whole, and what I have received from Heaven is restored. In practicing benevolence, who could surpass this? Moreover, let us take the sage’s maxim and test it against the outstanding disciples of his school. Yan Zi undertook benevolence: in overcoming himself and returning to ritual propriety, he necessarily acted courageously. Zhonggong undertook benevolence: in making reverence his guiding principle and practicing consideration for others, he necessarily exerted himself. A teacher such as Kong Zi, a great sage, was especially someone to whom they should defer. Yet we do not hear that these two disciples yielded the practice of benevolence to the sage. Was this not because they themselves practiced the benevolence they themselves possessed, leaving no occasion for deference? Those who aspire to benevolence must take these two disciples as their models; only then will they succeed.

The Way cannot be departed from for even an instant. If it could be departed from, it would not be the Way. Thus the gentleman is watchful and cautious concerning what he does not see, and fearful and apprehensive concerning what he…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
不聞莫見乎隱莫顯乎微故君子慎
其獨也喜怒哀樂之未發謂之中發
而皆中節謂之和中也者天下之大
本也和也者天下之達道也
李昇
同考試官訓導談　批〔作長題者病難收拾整齊嚴肅無如此篇〕
同考試官教諭亢　批〔寫出所以道不可離之意蓋玩索理學而有得者〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔道不可離之意融貫會通是故錄之〕
===
考試官學正逯　批〔動靜之功體用之妙宛然在目造道者之言也〕
中庸論道不可離而詳其功必明其不可離之
意焉夫道原於天而備於人其不可離也審矣
中庸詳其功而明其意其示人之意一何至歟
且夫道者日用事物當行之理皆性之德而具
於心充塞乎天地無物而不有不可須臾而離
punctuated:
不聞。莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。喜怒哀樂之未發，謂之中；發而皆中節，謂之和。中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。

李昇

同考試官訓導談　批〔作長題者病難收拾，整齊嚴肅，無如此篇。〕
同考試官教諭亢　批〔寫出所以道不可離之意，蓋玩索理學而有得者。〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔道不可離之意，融貫會通，是故錄之。〕
考試官學正逯　批〔動靜之功，體用之妙，宛然在目，造道者之言也。〕

中庸論道不可離，而詳其功，必明其不可離之意焉。夫道原於天而備於人，其不可離也審矣。中庸詳其功而明其意，其示人之意一何至歟！且夫道者，日用事物當行之理，皆性之德而具於心，充塞乎天地，無物而不有，不可須臾而離
translation_en:
…what he does not hear. Nothing is more visible than what is hidden, and nothing more manifest than what is minute. Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone. Before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise, this is called equilibrium; when they arise and all attain their proper measure, this is called harmony. Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally operative Way of all under Heaven.

Li Sheng 李昇

Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Those writing on long topics suffer from difficulty in bringing everything together. For orderliness and solemnity, none equals this piece.〕
Associate Examiner Kang, Instructor, comments: 〔It expresses the meaning of why the Way cannot be departed from. Its author has evidently gained understanding through pondering and investigating the Learning of Principle.〕
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔It integrates and comprehensively elucidates the meaning of the Way’s inseparability; therefore I have selected it.〕
Examiner Lu, School Instructor, comments: 〔The work of cultivation in activity and stillness, and the subtleties of substance and function, stand vividly before the eyes. These are the words of one who has attained the Way.〕

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the Way cannot be departed from and sets out in detail the work of cultivation; it must thereby clarify what its inseparability means. The Way originates in Heaven and is fully endowed in human beings: that it cannot be departed from is certain. The Doctrine of the Mean details this work and clarifies this meaning. How utterly thorough is its intention to instruct people!

Now, the Way consists of the principles that ought to be followed in the affairs and things of daily life. These are all virtues of our nature, fully present in the mind. It fills Heaven and Earth; there is nothing in which it is not present, and one cannot depart from it even for an instant…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
也使其可離非率性之道矣貫徹乎古今無時
而不然不可頃刻而違也使其可違又豈率性
之道哉夫道不可離如此由教而入之君子嘗
何如用其功耶故於其靜也目雖無所睹亦戒
謹而不敢忽耳雖無所聞亦恐懼而不敢怠存
養如此所以存天理之本然而使斯道不離於
須臾也於其動也幽暗之中人雖不知也而吾
之神明獨知何著見也是以君子雖常戒慎矣
而於此益致其力細微之事人雖不覺也而吾
===
之天君獨覺何明顯也君子雖常恐懼矣而於
此益密其功省察如此所以遏人欲於將萌而
使斯道不離於隱微也然道之所以不可離者
何哉蓋人之一心有喜怒焉有哀樂焉方其未
發也渾然在中無所偏倚不謂之中乎及其已
發也一皆中節無所乖戾不謂之和乎中乃性
之德即天命之謂也而天下之理皆由此出道
之體在是矣非大本而何和乃情之德即率性
之謂也而天下古今之所共由道之用在是矣
punctuated:
也。使其可離，非率性之道矣。貫徹乎古今，無時而不然，不可頃刻而違也。使其可違，又豈率性之道哉？夫道不可離如此，由教而入之君子，嘗何如用其功耶？故於其靜也，目雖無所睹，亦戒謹而不敢忽；耳雖無所聞，亦恐懼而不敢怠。存養如此，所以存天理之本然，而使斯道不離於須臾也。於其動也，幽暗之中，人雖不知也，而吾之神明獨知，何著見也！是以君子雖常戒慎矣，而於此益致其力。細微之事，人雖不覺也，而吾之天君獨覺，何明顯也！君子雖常恐懼矣，而於此益密其功。省察如此，所以遏人欲於將萌，而使斯道不離於隱微也。
然道之所以不可離者，何哉？蓋人之一心，有喜怒焉，有哀樂焉。方其未發也，渾然在中，無所偏倚，不謂之中乎？及其已發也，一皆中節，無所乖戾，不謂之和乎？中乃性之德，即天命之謂也，而天下之理皆由此出，道之體在是矣，非大本而何？和乃情之德，即率性之謂也，而天下古今之所共由，道之用在是矣。
translation_en:
…Were it possible to depart from it, it would not be the Way of following one’s nature. It runs through past and present, with no time at which it is otherwise; one cannot deviate from it even for an instant. Were it possible to deviate from it, how could it be the Way of following one’s nature? Since the Way cannot be departed from in this manner, how does the gentleman who enters it through instruction apply his efforts? Thus, in stillness, although his eyes see nothing, he remains cautious and vigilant, not daring to be negligent; although his ears hear nothing, he remains apprehensive, not daring to slacken. Such preservation and nourishment of the mind preserve heavenly principle as it originally is and ensure that this Way is not departed from even for a moment. In activity, amid darkness and obscurity, although others do not know, my own spiritual awareness alone knows: how manifest it is! Thus, although the gentleman is always cautious and watchful, here he applies himself still more earnestly. In minute matters, although others do not perceive, the sovereign of my mind alone perceives: how clear it is! Although the gentleman is always apprehensive, here he makes his efforts still more meticulous. Such scrutiny checks human desires just as they are about to arise and ensures that this Way is not departed from even in what is hidden and subtle.
Yet why can the Way not be departed from? Within the human mind there are joy and anger, sorrow and pleasure. Before they are aroused, they remain an undivided whole within, inclining to neither side: is this not called equilibrium? Once they are aroused, if each and every one attains its proper measure, with nothing discordant, is this not called harmony? Equilibrium is the virtue of human nature, precisely what is meant by Heaven’s mandate. All principles under Heaven issue from it; here lies the substance of the Way. What could it be but the great foundation? Harmony is the virtue of the feelings, precisely what is meant by following one’s nature. It is what all under Heaven, past and present, follow in common; here lies the functioning of the Way…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
非達道而何是道之體用即吾性情之德也此
其所以不可須臾而離也歟抑洪中庸之書子
思子憂道學之失其傳而作也此章上文言道
之大原出於天而不可易此則言其體備於己
而不可離以及存養省察之要下文則又以聖
神功化之極為言推而論之一篇之中無非此
義文雖簡而義則周體雖微而用則費學者誠
能反求諸身體驗而擴充之則將駸駸乎入於
聖賢之域而斯道不患其無傳矣不然其不流
為異端者幾希有志於斯道者宜於此而潛心
焉
===
易其田疇薄其稅斂民可使富也食之以
時用之以禮財不可勝用也
鄭選
同考試官訓導何　批〔上節既說民可使富下節又以節儉言之必有故也此作得之〕
同考試官教諭曾　批〔足民之政此章盡之是作最善發揮而感慨溢於言外必佳士也〕
punctuated:
非達道而何？是道之體用，即吾性情之德也。此其所以不可須臾而離也歟？抑洪《中庸》之書，子思子憂道學之失其傳而作也。此章上文言道之大原出於天而不可易，此則言其體備於己而不可離，以及存養省察之要；下文則又以聖神功化之極為言。推而論之，一篇之中無非此義。文雖簡而義則周，體雖微而用則費。學者誠能反求諸身，體驗而擴充之，則將駸駸乎入於聖賢之域，而斯道不患其無傳矣。不然，其不流為異端者幾希。有志於斯道者，宜於此而潛心焉。
易其田疇，薄其稅斂，民可使富也；食之以時，用之以禮，財不可勝用也。
鄭選
同考試官訓導何，批〔上節既說民可使富，下節又以節儉言之，必有故也。此作得之。〕
同考試官教諭曾，批〔足民之政，此章盡之。是作最善發揮，而感慨溢於言外，必佳士也。〕
translation_en:
…How could it be anything other than the universally followed Way? The substance and functioning of this Way are precisely the virtues of our nature and feelings. Is this not why it cannot be departed from even for an instant? Moreover [?], Master Zisi wrote the Doctrine of the Mean because he feared that the transmission of the learning of the Way would be lost. The preceding passage of this chapter states that the great source of the Way comes from Heaven and cannot be altered. This passage states that its substance is fully present within oneself and cannot be departed from, and also explains the essentials of nourishing and preserving it and of examining oneself. The following passage speaks further of the utmost achievements and transforming influence of sagely and spiritual power. Extending this reasoning, nothing throughout the entire work lies outside this meaning. Though its wording is brief, its meaning is comprehensive; though its substance is subtle, its functioning is far-reaching. If learners can truly seek it within themselves, experience it personally, and extend it to the full, they will steadily advance into the realm of the sages and worthies, and there will be no fear that this Way will lack transmission. Otherwise, scarcely any will avoid drifting into heterodox teachings. Those committed to this Way should devote their minds deeply to this.
If their fields are put in good order and their taxes and levies lightened, the people can be made prosperous. If resources are consumed at the proper times and used in accordance with ritual propriety, wealth will be more than can be exhausted.
Zheng Xuan.
Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The first section has already explained that the people can be made prosperous; the following section then speaks of frugality. There must be a reason for this. This essay grasps it.〕
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: 〔This chapter fully sets forth the policies for ensuring that the people have enough. This essay excels at elucidating them, and its deeply felt concern overflows beyond the words. Its author must be a fine scholar.〕

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導陳　批〔題目有關世教而此作亦非虛言無補者〕
考試官學正逯　批〔說得孟子之意出是故錄之〕
有所以富民之道有所以足財之道善治天下
者然也蓋民者國之本財者民之心也富民足
財各有其道尚何天下之難治哉昔孟子之意
若曰國以民為本民有不富如治道何有天下
者誠知農事至重使民耕治之而遠邇悉無荒
蕪之田能以民事為急使民經理之而高下塍
===
為禾黍之地是田疇治矣九一而助惟正之供
不橫征以厲民什一而賦常制是取不暴斂以
自奉是稅斂薄矣將見田之所入者多歲之所
收者廣仰足以事父母俯足以畜妻子民豈有
不富哉民以財為心財有不足如治道何有天
下者誠知食不以時民安貴矣如朝焉則饔之
如夕焉則飧之凡飲食之間必嚴妄費之禁非
食之以時而何用不以禮民侈用矣如冠婚之
用截然品節之具存喪祭之行秩乎制度之周
punctuated:
考試官訓導陳　批〔題目有關世教，而此作亦非虛言無補者。〕
考試官學正逯　批〔說得孟子之意出，是故錄之。〕
有所以富民之道，有所以足財之道，善治天下者然也。蓋民者，國之本；財者，民之心也。富民足財，各有其道，尚何天下之難治哉！昔孟子之意若曰：國以民為本，民有不富，如治道何？有天下者誠知農事至重，使民耕治之，而遠邇悉無荒蕪之田；能以民事為急，使民經理之，而高下塍為禾黍之地，是田疇治矣。九一而助，惟正之供，不橫征以厲民；什一而賦，常制是取，不暴斂以自奉，是稅斂薄矣。將見田之所入者多，歲之所收者廣，仰足以事父母，俯足以畜妻子，民豈有不富哉！民以財為心，財有不足，如治道何？有天下者誠知食不以時，民安貴矣。如朝焉則饔之，如夕焉則飧之，凡飲食之間，必嚴妄費之禁，非食之以時而何？用不以禮，民侈用矣。如冠婚之用，截然品節之具存；喪祭之行，秩乎制度之周
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The topic bears on moral instruction in society, and this composition, too, is no mere empty discourse without practical benefit.〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔It brings out Mencius’s meaning; therefore it has been selected for inclusion.〕
There is a way to enrich the people, and there is a way to make their resources sufficient: those who govern the realm well act accordingly. The people are the foundation of the state, and material resources are what the people set their hearts upon. If enriching the people and ensuring sufficient resources each have their proper method, what difficulty can there still be in governing the realm? Mencius’s meaning was as though he had said: The state takes the people as its foundation. If the people are not prosperous, what can be done about good government? If the ruler truly understands the supreme importance of agriculture and has the people cultivate the land, no fields, near or far, will remain waste. If he gives priority to the people’s affairs and has them tend the land, the high and low field ridges will become ground for grain and millet [?]. Thus the fields will be well cultivated. Under the labor-assistance system, one part in nine is devoted to the public field: only the regular contribution is supplied, without arbitrary exactions that harm the people. Under the levy of one part in ten, only the established amount is collected, without oppressive taxation to support the ruler’s own wants. Thus taxation will be light. Then the fields will yield abundantly and the annual harvests will be ample: the people will have enough to support their parents above them and maintain their wives and children below them. How could they fail to prosper?
The people set their hearts upon material resources. If those resources are insufficient, what can be done about good government? If the ruler truly understands that, when food is not consumed at proper times, the people prize ease [?], he will have them take their morning meal in the morning and their evening meal in the evening. In all matters of eating and drinking, prohibitions against wasteful expenditure must be strictly enforced. What is this if not consuming food at proper times? When expenditure does not accord with ritual propriety, the people spend extravagantly. For expenditures on capping ceremonies and weddings, clearly differentiated rules of gradation and restraint are fully provided; in the conduct of funerals and sacrifices, the prescribed arrangements are orderly and comprehensive …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
容凡用度之間必謹侈用之戒非用之以禮而
何殆見民之所用者少家之所積者厚隨所取
而無不給隨所用而無不周財豈可勝用哉吁
既務本以豐財之源又儉約以節財之流爲治
之道孰有加於此耶抑考時至戰國君失厥道
非惟不能教民而反有以厲民者故民皆安於
游惰習於侈靡又甚於横征暴斂無怪乎民窮
而財盡也孟子目擊其弊不忍君民之胥失乃
詳舉聖人治天下之道以諗當世冀其得聞而
用之惜乎蔽固深而不能用使孟子託諸空言
也噫
===
易
勞謙君子萬民服也
鄭選
同考試官訓導何　批　〔發明大臣有勞而不伐殆無餘　藴矣且講萬民服處轉挽可佳〕
同考試官教諭曾　批　〔理明而不鑿詞達而不泛傑作　也是用録出〕
punctuated:
容。凡用度之間，必謹侈用之戒，非用之以禮而何？殆見民之所用者少，家之所積者厚，隨所取而無不給，隨所用而無不周，財豈可勝用哉！吁！既務本以豐財之源，又儉約以節財之流，爲治之道，孰有加於此耶？抑考時至戰國，君失厥道，非惟不能教民，而反有以厲民者，故民皆安於游惰，習於侈靡，又甚於横征暴斂，無怪乎民窮而財盡也。孟子目擊其弊，不忍君民之胥失，乃詳舉聖人治天下之道以諗當世，冀其得聞而用之。惜乎蔽固深而不能用，使孟子託諸空言也。噫！

《易》
勞謙，君子萬民服也。
鄭選

同考試官訓導何　批：〔發明大臣有勞而不伐，殆無餘　藴矣。且講萬民服處，轉挽可佳。〕

同考試官教諭曾　批：〔理明而不鑿，詞達而不泛，傑作　也，是用録出。〕
translation_en:
…in their provisions [?]. In all expenditure, one must scrupulously heed the warning against extravagance. What is this if not spending in accordance with ritual propriety? Then surely the people will spend little and households will accumulate substantial reserves. Whatever they draw upon will suffice; whatever their expenses, all will be covered. How could their wealth ever be exhausted? Ah! By attending to the fundamental occupation of agriculture, one enriches the source of wealth; by frugality and restraint, one regulates its outflow. What method of government could surpass this?

Yet consider the Warring States period, when rulers lost the proper Way. Not only were they unable to instruct the people, but they actually inflicted suffering upon them. Thus the people all became content with idleness and accustomed to extravagance, their plight further aggravated by arbitrary levies and harsh exactions. No wonder the people were impoverished and their resources exhausted. Mencius witnessed these abuses. Unable to bear the failings of rulers and people alike, he set forth in detail the sages’ way of governing the realm to counsel his contemporaries, hoping that they might hear and employ it. Alas, their entrenched blindness was so profound that they could not put it into practice, leaving Mencius to entrust his teachings to empty words. Ah!

Book of Changes
“A gentleman who labors yet remains humble: all the people submit to him.”
Zheng Xuan

Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of how a high minister renders service without boasting leaves almost nothing unexplored. Moreover, the turn of argument in explaining ‘all the people submit’ is admirable.〕

Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: 〔The reasoning is clear without being forced; the language conveys the meaning without becoming diffuse. This is an outstanding work, and for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.〕

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導陳　批　意新辭健逈出衆作置之高選
允協輿情
考試官學正逯　批　化陳爲新佳作也異日建功名于
竹帛之上可以占子之心事矣
功忘于己者人所難人服于心者爲無間此謙
九三之象傳也蓋有功不居非厚德之君子未
易能也而謙九三以之其致人心之歸服也夫
豈有間哉昔謙九三周公繫其爻曰勞謙君子
有終吉夫子象傳申之謂夫九三君子秉剛正
===
之德當大臣之位上焉君所任輸忠悃爲奠安
宗社之謀功業樹建于當時下焉衆所依運心
思爲保固生靈之計政績輝煌于天下有功于
君其心以爲功雖高分所當爲也退處謙冲歛
然不自居其功蓋人情之所難而君子之所養
者見焉有勞于民其心以爲勞雖大職所當盡
也歛歸恬淡寂然不自伐其勞蓋君子之至厚
而淺薄之太露者愧焉謙之九三如此殆見天
道之所益地道之所流者在是鬼神之所福人
punctuated:
考試官訓導陳　批：意新辭健，逈出衆作，置之高選，允協輿情。
考試官學正逯　批：化陳爲新，佳作也。異日建功名于竹帛之上，可以占子之心事矣。
功忘于己者人所難，人服于心者爲無間，此謙九三之象傳也。蓋有功不居，非厚德之君子未易能也，而謙九三以之，其致人心之歸服也，夫豈有間哉！昔謙九三，周公繫其爻曰：「勞謙君子，有終吉。」夫子象傳申之，謂夫九三君子秉剛正之德，當大臣之位，上焉君所任，輸忠悃爲奠安宗社之謀，功業樹建于當時；下焉衆所依，運心思爲保固生靈之計，政績輝煌于天下。有功于君，其心以爲功雖高，分所當爲也，退處謙冲，歛然不自居其功，蓋人情之所難，而君子之所養者見焉。有勞于民，其心以爲勞雖大，職所當盡也，歛歸恬淡，寂然不自伐其勞，蓋君子之至厚，而淺薄之太露者愧焉。謙之九三如此，殆見天道之所益、地道之所流者在是，鬼神之所福、人
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: The ideas are fresh and the language vigorous, far surpassing the other compositions. Placing it among the highest selections fully accords with the general judgment.

Examiner Lu, School Director, comments: It transforms the familiar into something new—a fine composition. From this one can discern your aspirations to establish achievements and a name recorded on bamboo and silk in days to come.

To forget one’s own achievements is difficult for others to do; when people submit in their hearts, their allegiance admits no division. This is the meaning of the Commentary on the Images for the third, yang line of the hexagram Modesty. To have achievements yet claim no credit is not easily within anyone’s power unless he is a gentleman of ample virtue. Yet the third, yang line of Modesty embodies this. How, then, could there be any division in the allegiance it wins from people’s hearts?

Formerly, the Duke of Zhou appended these words to the third, yang line of Modesty: “A gentleman of achievement and modesty brings matters to completion: auspicious.” The Master elaborated upon this in the Commentary on the Images. His meaning is that the gentleman represented by this line possesses firm and upright virtue and occupies the position of a great minister. Above, he is entrusted with responsibility by his ruler: pouring forth his loyalty and sincerity, he devises plans to secure the ancestral temple and the altars of state, establishing meritorious achievements in his age. Below, he is the support of the multitude: applying his mind, he devises measures to protect the people, and his achievements in government shine throughout the realm.

Although he has rendered meritorious service to his ruler, he considers that, however great his achievements, they are merely what his allotted duty requires. He withdraws into modest self-effacement and, restraining himself, claims no credit for his achievements. This is difficult for ordinary human nature, and herein the gentleman’s self-cultivation becomes visible. Although he has labored for the people, he considers that, however great his labors, they are merely what his office requires him to fulfill. He retires into quiet simplicity and, remaining unobtrusive, does not boast of his labors. Such is the gentleman’s utmost depth of virtue; those whose shallowness is all too conspicuous are put to shame by it.

Such is the third, yang line of Modesty. Here, surely, we see what the Way of Heaven augments and what the Way of Earth flows toward; what the spirits bless, and what human …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
道之所好者在是羣黎百姓仰勳勞而起敬者
莫不慕其才而服其謀猷之廣遠庶民小子沐
謙光而興思者莫不薰其德而服其器量之恢
宏上乎于君无功高不賞之嫌所謂生祝其壽
死立其祀者則有之矣是人心之愛戴寧有間
于彼此乎下乎于民无率怠弗協之理所謂君
子親賢小人樂利者則有之矣是人心之悅服
曾有間于遐邇乎若使九三君子一有恃勞矜
功之心則天下鬨然羣起而爭之矣有終之吉
===
奚能保哉周公許其終以示占孔子驗其實以
申象其為有功大臣之戒勸者深矣嘗夫周公
當成王寄托之任輔成王室自古功高未有若
此者而周公亦舄几几非惟不以為功且引以
為罪卒之大風拔木金縢啓而成王悟流言息
而東山歸天地位焉鬼神相焉豈特兆萬民服焉
而已周公以其心事特筆于爻而孔子於象傳
復申明之蓋為萬世功臣之龜鑑也後世猶有
若渾濬之平呉鍾鄧之伐蜀互相爭功至不保
punctuated:
道之所好者在是。羣黎百姓仰勳勞而起敬者，莫不慕其才而服其謀猷之廣遠；庶民小子沐謙光而興思者，莫不薰其德而服其器量之恢宏。上乎于君，无功高不賞之嫌，所謂生祝其壽、死立其祀者，則有之矣。是人心之愛戴，寧有間于彼此乎？下乎于民，无率怠弗協之理，所謂君子親賢、小人樂利者，則有之矣。是人心之悅服，曾有間于遐邇乎？若使九三君子一有恃勞矜功之心，則天下鬨然羣起而爭之矣。有終之吉，奚能保哉？周公許其終以示占，孔子驗其實以申象，其為有功大臣之戒勸者深矣。
嘗夫周公當成王寄托之任，輔成王室，自古功高未有若此者，而周公亦舄几几，非惟不以為功，且引以為罪。卒之大風拔木，金縢啓而成王悟，流言息而東山歸，天地位焉，鬼神相焉，豈特兆萬民服焉而已？周公以其心事特筆于爻，而孔子於象傳復申明之，蓋為萬世功臣之龜鑑也。後世猶有若渾濬之平呉、鍾鄧之伐蜀，互相爭功，至不保
translation_en:
… what the Way of humanity favors is found here. Among the common people who look up to his meritorious service with reverence, none fails to admire his ability and acknowledge the breadth and reach of his designs. Among the ordinary people and humble folk who receive the radiance of his modesty and are moved to reflection, none fails to be imbued with his virtue and acknowledge his expansive generosity of spirit. In his relations with his ruler above, there is no suspicion that his achievements are too great to reward. Rather, there is what is described as praying for his longevity while he lives and establishing sacrifices to him after he dies. Could such heartfelt love and esteem distinguish between one person and another? In his relations with the people below, there is no reason for them to lapse into indolence and discord. Rather, there is what is described as “gentlemen cherishing the worthy, and common people enjoying their benefits.” Could such willing allegiance distinguish between those far away and those nearby? If the gentleman represented by the Nine in the Third Place once entertained the thought of relying on his services and boasting of his achievements, all under Heaven would rise in clamorous contention against him. How could he retain the good fortune of bringing matters to a successful end? The Duke of Zhou promised him a successful end to indicate the divination’s outcome; Confucius examined its actual basis to elaborate the Image. Profound indeed are the admonition and encouragement they offer ministers of great achievement.
Consider [?] how the Duke of Zhou bore the responsibility entrusted to him concerning King Cheng and assisted in securing the royal house. Never since antiquity had anyone’s achievements been so great. Yet the Duke of Zhou remained composed and dignified in his ceremonial shoes: not only did he refrain from claiming credit, he even took blame upon himself. In the end, a great wind uprooted trees; the metal-bound coffer was opened, and King Cheng understood. The rumors ceased, and there was a return from the eastern hills. Heaven and Earth assumed their proper places, and spirits lent their aid. Was it merely that the myriad people submitted to him? The Duke of Zhou gave particular expression to his own intentions and deeds in the line statement, and Confucius further elucidated them in the Commentary on the Images, providing a guide and mirror for meritorious ministers throughout all ages. Yet in later generations there were still men such as Wang Hun and Wang Jun in the pacification of Wu, and Zhong Hui and Deng Ai in the conquest of Shu, who competed with one another for credit, to the point of failing to preserve …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
其身者其亦可慨矣夫
是故蓍之德圓而神卦之德方以知六爻
之義易以貢
焦鵬
同考試官訓導何　批　揭書出題本不計其難易但
作者不失之簡必失之泛惟此作平順通達說理了了塲中絮孚
豈多得耶
同考試官教諭曾　批　連日閱易未有甚可人意者
此作說理通暢其易義中之優者歟
===
考試官訓導陳　批　說得蓍卦爻三者明白可取
考試官學正逯　批　說理妥帖潔浄自精微之義固當
如此
大傳指易之所有而各著其理之所寓焉盖易
之所有蓍卦爻而已而圓神方知易貢之理各
有攸寓易之所以能開物成務冒天下之道也
有以哉今夫易何為者也昔者聖人幽贊神明
而著以生剛柔摩盪而卦爻以立自著之德言
之其策四十有九用于卦畫未成之先分揲而
punctuated:
其身者，其亦可慨矣夫！

是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。
焦鵬

同考試官訓導何批：「揭書出題，本不計其難易，但作者不失之簡，必失之泛。惟此作平順通達，說理了了，塲中絮孚，豈多得耶？」
同考試官教諭曾批：「連日閱易，未有甚可人意者。此作說理通暢，其易義中之優者歟！」
考試官訓導陳批：「說得蓍、卦、爻三者明白，可取。」
考試官學正逯批：「說理妥帖潔浄，自精微之義固當如此。」

大傳指易之所有，而各著其理之所寓焉。盖易之所有，蓍、卦、爻而已，而圓神、方知、易貢之理，各有攸寓。易之所以能開物成務、冒天下之道也，有以哉！今夫易何為者也？昔者聖人幽贊神明，而著以生；剛柔摩盪，而卦爻以立。自著之德言之，其策四十有九，用于卦畫未成之先，分揲而
translation_en:
…their own lives: how lamentable this is!

“Thus the virtue of the milfoil stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and knowing; and the meaning of the six lines is readily disclosed.”
Jiao Peng

Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: “When opening the book to select a topic, one does not initially reckon its difficulty. Yet writers, unless they err through excessive brevity, invariably err through vagueness. This composition alone proceeds smoothly and lucidly, explaining the principles clearly. Amid the examination hall’s ‘xu fu’ [?], how often could one obtain its like?”

Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: “Over several days of reading essays on the Changes, I have found none that was particularly satisfying. This composition explains the principles fluently and clearly. Surely it is among the better essays on the meaning of the Changes!”

Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It explains the three things—milfoil stalks, hexagrams, and lines—clearly, and merits selection.”

Examiner Lu, School Instructor, comments: “Its exposition of principle is apt, clean, and lucid. The subtle meaning itself [?] certainly calls for treatment like this.”

The Great Commentary identifies what the Changes contains and makes clear where each of its principles resides. What the Changes contains is simply milfoil stalks, hexagrams, and lines; and the principles of roundness and numinous efficacy, squareness and knowing, and ready disclosure each have their particular abode. There is indeed a reason why the Changes can reveal things, bring undertakings to completion, and encompass the Way of all under Heaven!

Now, what does the Changes do? In antiquity, the sages mysteriously assisted the spiritual powers, and the milfoil stalks [?] came into being; the hard and the yielding rubbed against and stirred one another, and the hexagrams and lines were established. Speaking of the virtue of the milfoil stalks [?], their number is forty-nine. They are used before the hexagram lines have taken shape, being divided and counted off, and…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
掛扐寓變化于枯梗之中參伍而錯綜寄神妙
于尺櫝之內或一二焉或三四焉進退離合不
可以方體求或七八焉或九六焉陰陽奇偶不
可為典要拘其為德也不亦圓而神乎自卦之
德言之其數六十有四見于蓍變已動之後文
成象定事有一定之理內貞外悔理有一定之
則或健與順或動與止然不移皆有所據而
可求或入與陷或麗與說確然不易皆有所見
而可考其為德也不亦方以知乎至若六爻之
===
義有陽爻百九十二焉而或變為陰有陰爻百
九十二焉而或變為陽位雖有承乘比應之同
也而告人以吉凶之兆則隨其所向所以開狐
疑而決趨避者屢遷無常焉爻雖有遠近貴賤
之等也而曉人以悔吝之萌則指其所之所以
明失得以濟民行者變動靡定焉其為義也又
非易以貢乎是則圓神也方知也易以貢也三
者皆蓍卦爻之理也而聖人體具于心得其理
而不假其物此其所以能明天道察民故興神
punctuated: 掛扐，寓變化于枯梗之中；參伍而錯綜，寄神妙于尺櫝之內。或一二焉，或三四焉，進退離合，不可以方體求；或七八焉，或九六焉，陰陽奇偶，不可為典要拘。其為德也，不亦圓而神乎？自卦之德言之，其數六十有四，見于蓍變已動之後。文成象定，事有一定之理；內貞外悔，理有一定之則。或健與順，或動與止，然不移，皆有所據而可求；或入與陷，或麗與說，確然不易，皆有所見而可考。其為德也，不亦方以知乎？至若六爻之義，有陽爻百九十二焉，而或變為陰；有陰爻百九十二焉，而或變為陽。位雖有承乘比應之同也，而告人以吉凶之兆，則隨其所向，所以開狐疑而決趨避者，屢遷無常焉。爻雖有遠近貴賤之等也，而曉人以悔吝之萌，則指其所之，所以明失得以濟民行者，變動靡定焉。其為義也，又非易以貢乎？是則圓神也，方知也，易以貢也，三者皆蓍卦爻之理也。而聖人體具于心，得其理而不假其物，此其所以能明天道、察民故、興神
translation_en:
…by setting one stalk aside and counting off the remainders, they lodge transformation within dry stems; by grouping and interweaving the counts, they entrust numinous subtlety to a box a foot long. Sometimes the counts are one or two, sometimes three or four: their advance and retreat, separation and combination cannot be understood through fixed forms. Sometimes they are seven or eight, sometimes nine or six: yin and yang, odd and even cannot be confined by fixed rules. Is the virtue of the milfoil stalks not round and numinous? Speaking of the virtue of the hexagrams, they number sixty-four and appear after the transformations of the milfoil have been set in motion. Once their patterns are formed and their images established, affairs have determinate principles. The inner trigram is the primary aspect and the outer trigram the secondary aspect; their principles have determinate rules. Whether strength and compliance, or movement and stillness, they remain unchanging [?], each with a basis that can be sought out. Whether penetration and peril, or attachment and joy, they are firmly unalterable, each with manifestations that can be examined. Is their virtue not square and knowing?
As for the meaning of the six lines, there are 192 yang lines, some of which change into yin, and 192 yin lines, some of which change into yang. Although their positions share the relationships of supporting, riding upon, adjacency, and correspondence, the signs of good or ill fortune that they disclose follow the direction in which they tend. Thus, the means by which they dispel uncertainty and determine what to pursue or avoid repeatedly shift, without constancy. Although the lines have distinctions of distance and proximity, high and low status, in revealing the first signs of regret and distress they point to where they are going. Thus, the means by which they clarify loss and gain and assist the people’s conduct change without fixed limits. Does their meaning not also lie in changing and offering guidance?
Roundness and numinousness, squareness and knowledge, and change that offers guidance: these three are the principles of the milfoil stalks, hexagrams, and lines. Yet the sage embodies them fully in his heart; he grasps their principles without relying on the objects themselves. This is how he can illuminate the Way of Heaven, discern the circumstances of the people, and bring forth numinous…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
物以前民用也哉抑論卦爻者著策之體著策
者卦爻之用徒有卦爻而無著策則法象虛陳
而易道幾乎息矣然易本為衆人作使人皆聖
人焉則心易之理自具知來藏往之妙雖著卦
爻皆可無也奈之何易既作而斯民猶有不知
趨避者此聖人拳拳憂世之心所以不能與民
相忘于無易之表
書
食哉惟時柔遠能邇惇德允元而難任人
===
蠻夷率服
李昇
同考試官訓導談　批〔題本正大塲屋士類能言之〕
〔但佳者絶少理明辭贍而中有作家法度僅見此篇〕
同考試官教諭允　批〔作舊題有新意其氣充然可〕
〔以爲文矣〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔虞廷咨牧之意模寫殆盡豈士之〕
〔傑然者與〕
考試官學正逯　批〔通篇典雅不涉浮誕錄之〕
punctuated:
物以前民用也哉！抑論卦爻者，著策之體；著策者，卦爻之用。徒有卦爻而無著策，則法象虛陳，而易道幾乎息矣。然易本為衆人作，使人皆聖人焉，則心易之理自具，知來藏往之妙，雖著卦爻皆可無也。奈之何易既作，而斯民猶有不知趨避者？此聖人拳拳憂世之心，所以不能與民相忘于無易之表。
書
食哉惟時，柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人，蠻夷率服。
李昇
同考試官訓導談，批〔題本正大，塲屋士類能言之，〕〔但佳者絶少。理明辭贍，而中有作家法度，僅見此篇。〕
同考試官教諭允，批〔作舊題有新意，其氣充然，可〕〔以爲文矣。〕
考試官訓導陳，批〔虞廷咨牧之意，模寫殆盡。豈士之〕〔傑然者與？〕
考試官學正逯，批〔通篇典雅，不涉浮誕，錄之。〕
translation_en:
…objects of spiritual efficacy, thereby guiding the people in their use! Furthermore, the hexagrams and lines constitute the substance embodied in the divining stalks [?]; the divining stalks provide the practical application of the hexagrams and lines. If there were only hexagrams and lines, without divining stalks, the patterns and images would stand idly displayed, and the Way of the Changes would almost cease to operate. Yet the Changes was originally made for ordinary people. If everyone were a sage, the principles of the Changes would naturally be complete within the mind; with the marvelous capacity to know what is to come and to preserve what has passed, even the stalks, hexagrams, and lines could all be dispensed with. How is it, then, that although the Changes has been made, some among the people still do not know what to pursue and what to avoid? This is why the sage, with his earnest concern for the world, cannot forget the people and be forgotten by them in a realm beyond the need for the Changes.
Book of Documents
“Food! Attend to its proper seasons. Deal gently with those afar and be good to those nearby; honor the virtuous and trust the good, but keep flatterers at a distance. Then the Man and Yi peoples will all submit.”
Li Sheng
Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is upright and weighty, and examination candidates can all discuss it. Yet excellent treatments are extremely rare. Only in this essay have I seen clear reasoning and ample expression combined with the discipline of an accomplished writer.”
Associate Examiner Yun [?], Instructor, comments: “He brings fresh ideas to an old topic. Its vigor is abundant: this may indeed be called accomplished writing.”
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He has rendered almost exhaustively the intent of the Yu court’s consultation with the regional governors. Surely he is an outstanding scholar!”
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Classically elegant throughout, without lapsing into frivolity or extravagance. Include it in the record.”

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
惟政治無不宜斯遠人無不服聖君命州牧然
也夫善政之得民心也尚矣苟能處之各得其
宜又何遠人之不服哉史臣記帝舜命十二州
牧之辭有曰為治莫大於遠人之所服遠莫要
於政治之脩彼王政以食為首而農事以時為
先也欲足民食在於民時春耕夏耘使得盡力
於畎畝而役之必乘其隙東作西成使得有事
於田疇而使之必以其暇遠者宜在所略而近
者宜在所詳也欲盡其詳先於其略寬而撫之
===
使四境之外一仁恩之浹洽擾而習之使邦域
之中一德澤之周流若然則重民食一遐邇處
之各得其宜矣以至佩仁服義忠信誠慤有為
君子者焉則惇厚之允信之迪簡在王庭不致
有簡賢侮德之誚懷奸稔惡包藏凶禍有為小
人者焉則疏斥之拒絕之不與同中國不致有
聽讒用邪之譏若然則親君子遠小人處之各
得其道矣夫如是豈徒中國順治而已遠而八
蠻慕王道之蕩蕩相率而來王稽首稱藩蓋不
punctuated: 「惟政治無不宜，斯遠人無不服。」聖君命州牧然也。夫善政之得民心也尚矣！苟能處之各得其宜，又何遠人之不服哉？史臣記帝舜命十二州牧之辭，有曰：為治莫大於遠人之所服，遠莫要於政治之脩。彼王政以食為首，而農事以時為先也。欲足民食，在於民時。春耕夏耘，使得盡力於畎畝，而役之必乘其隙；東作西成，使得有事於田疇，而使之必以其暇。遠者宜在所略，而近者宜在所詳也。欲盡其詳，先於其略。寬而撫之，使四境之外一仁恩之浹洽；擾而習之，使邦域之中一德澤之周流。若然，則重民食、一遐邇，處之各得其宜矣。以至佩仁服義，忠信誠慤，有為君子者焉，則惇厚之，允信之，迪簡在王庭，不致有簡賢侮德之誚；懷奸稔惡，包藏凶禍，有為小人者焉，則疏斥之，拒絕之，不與同中國，不致有聽讒用邪之譏。若然，則親君子、遠小人，處之各得其道矣。夫如是，豈徒中國順治而已？遠而八蠻，慕王道之蕩蕩，相率而來王，稽首稱藩，蓋不
translation_en: “Only when every aspect of government is fitting will all distant peoples submit.” Such was the sage ruler’s charge to the regional governors. Good government has won the people’s hearts from ancient times! If each matter can be handled fittingly, what distant people would fail to submit? The court historian recorded Emperor Shun’s charge to the twelve regional governors as follows: Nothing in governing is greater than securing the submission of distant peoples; for bringing distant peoples to submission [?], nothing is more essential than putting government in good order. In kingly government, food comes first; in agriculture, proper timing takes precedence. To provide the people with sufficient food, one must respect their agricultural seasons. During spring plowing and summer weeding, let them devote their strength fully to the fields, and requisition their labor only in the intervals. During the work of spring and the harvest of autumn, let them attend to their farmland, and employ them only when they have leisure. Distant peoples should be governed with a light touch, while those nearby should receive detailed attention. To attend fully to those nearby, begin with those requiring the lighter touch. Treat them generously and nurture them, so that benevolent kindness may permeate all lands beyond the borders; gently guide and train them, so that the blessings of virtue may circulate throughout the realm. In this way, by valuing the people’s food supply and uniting those far and near, each will be treated fittingly. Furthermore, when there are noble men who clothe themselves in benevolence and righteousness and are loyal, trustworthy, sincere, and honest, treat them generously and trust them sincerely; advance and select them for service at the royal court. Thus there will be no occasion for the reproach that one neglects the worthy and insults the virtuous. When there are petty men who harbor treachery, persist in wrongdoing, and conceal violent and disastrous designs, distance and dismiss them, reject and exclude them, and do not allow them to share the central realm. Thus there will be no occasion for criticism that one listens to slander and employs the wicked. In this way, by drawing close to noble men and keeping petty men at a distance, each will be treated according to the proper way. With matters thus ordered, would the central realm alone enjoy orderly government? Even the distant peoples of the eight Man regions, admiring the vast breadth of the kingly Way, will lead one another to acknowledge the king, bow their heads to the ground, and declare themselves his vassals. Surely this would not …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
特一處爲然也外而蠻夷仰王道之平平相率
而來享傾心向化盖不但一國爲爾也吁内治
既舉外夷自服如此汝十二州牧可不以是而
殫厥心乎抑考蠻狄之爲中國患自古爲然也
特在御之得其道耳蠻夷率服在於内治之修
有苗來格在於干羽之舞後世智不出此而乃
築長城於秦結和親於漢借兵勢於唐甚至稱
子於石晉稱臣於南宋愈趨愈下其不能久安
長治也宜哉有志用世者讀舜典之書當一唱
===
而三歎
克享天心受天明命
同考試官訓導談　批　姚諒
〔此篇講天心主啓迪眷求說受天命處不附有天下享混講殊有定見〕
同考試官教諭允　批
〔題不難作此篇獨善發揚而理自見必佳士也〕
考試官訓導陳　批
〔體貼經傳融會成文取之〕
考試官學正逯　批
〔見之真若其作義自別錄示〕
punctuated:
特一處爲然也。外而蠻夷仰王道之平平，相率而來享，傾心向化，盖不但一國爲爾也。吁！内治既舉，外夷自服如此，汝十二州牧可不以是而殫厥心乎？抑考蠻狄之爲中國患，自古爲然也，特在御之得其道耳。蠻夷率服，在於内治之修；有苗來格，在於干羽之舞。後世智不出此，而乃築長城於秦，結和親於漢，借兵勢於唐，甚至稱子於石晉，稱臣於南宋，愈趨愈下。其不能久安長治也，宜哉！有志用世者，讀《舜典》之書，當一唱而三歎。

克享天心，受天明命。

同考試官訓導談　批　姚諒
〔此篇講天心，主啓迪眷求說；受天命處，不附有天下享混講，殊有定見。〕
同考試官教諭允　批
〔題不難作，此篇獨善發揚，而理自見，必佳士也。〕
考試官訓導陳　批
〔體貼經傳，融會成文，取之。〕
考試官學正逯　批
〔見之真，若其作義自別，錄示。〕
translation_en:
…nor was this so in only one place. Beyond the realm, the Man and Yi peoples look up to the impartiality of the kingly Way and lead one another to present tribute, wholeheartedly embracing its transforming influence. Surely this is not confined to a single country. Ah! Once internal government has been put in order, the peoples beyond submit of their own accord in this way. Can you, the governors of the twelve provinces, fail to devote your utmost attention to this? Yet, considering how the Man and Di have troubled the Central States, this has been so since antiquity. What matters is simply finding the proper way to deal with them. The submission of the Man and Yi depends on cultivating internal government; the Youmiao were brought to submission by a dance with shields and plumes. The wisdom of later ages did not surpass this, yet under the Qin they built the Long Wall, under the Han they contracted marriage alliances, and under the Tang they borrowed military strength. They even went so far as to profess themselves sons under the Shi family's Jin dynasty and subjects under the Southern Song, descending ever lower. It is no wonder that they could not secure enduring peace and lasting order! Those who aspire to serve the world should read the Canon of Shun and respond to a single recitation with three sighs.

“Be able to satisfy Heaven's heart and receive Heaven's luminous mandate.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor. Author: Yao Liang 姚諒.
〔In discussing Heaven's heart, this essay chiefly follows the interpretation concerning Heaven's enlightening guidance and solicitous search. In its treatment of receiving Heaven's mandate, it does not conflate this with possessing All-under-Heaven [?]. It shows a notably firm interpretive judgment.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Yun, Instructor.
〔The topic is not difficult to write on, but this essay is exceptionally good at developing it, so that the principle becomes apparent of itself. Its author must be an excellent scholar.〕

Comment by Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor.
〔It closely apprehends the classics and their commentaries, integrating them into a coherent composition. Accept it.〕

Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor.
〔Its understanding is true; the way it develops the meaning is distinctive [?]. Copy it out for display.〕

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
求學
能當乎天心大膺乎天眷君臣一德所致也蓋
惟德可以動天也有商君臣咸有一德豈不能
當天心而膺天眷哉昔伊尹將告歸而陳戒於
太甲莫意謂夫莫難當者天之心莫難受者天
之命是故監于萬方啓迪有命天嘗有心而求
其人矣天下之大其能仰承天心者誰歟惟尹
暨湯咸有一德而能當乎天之心焉眷求一德
俾作神主天嘗有意而求其主矣四海之廣其
===
能上當天心者疇歟惟湯及尹皆有一德而能
承乎天之意焉然天心既當則天命斯受矣由
是天命雖無常也則面稽天若而有以膺之眷
命用懋中命用休于以荷天之休百祿是遒受
明命於昭昭之中而仰焉之無愧也昔之保佑
於桀者今則舍桀而歸湯矣天命於此難諶也則
克配上帝而有以受之自天申之保佑命之于
以荷天之寵百祿是總受休命於蒼蒼之表而
俯焉之無怍也向之純佑於夏者今則舍夏而
punctuated:
求學

能當乎天心，大膺乎天眷，君臣一德所致也。蓋惟德可以動天也。有商君臣咸有一德，豈不能當天心而膺天眷哉？昔伊尹將告歸而陳戒於太甲，莫意謂夫莫難當者天之心，莫難受者天之命。是故監于萬方，啓迪有命，天嘗有心而求其人矣。天下之大，其能仰承天心者誰歟？惟尹暨湯咸有一德，而能當乎天之心焉。眷求一德，俾作神主，天嘗有意而求其主矣。四海之廣，其能上當天心者疇歟？惟湯及尹皆有一德，而能承乎天之意焉。然天心既當，則天命斯受矣。由是天命雖無常也，則面稽天若而有以膺之。眷命用懋，中命用休，于以荷天之休，百祿是遒，受明命於昭昭之中，而仰焉之無愧也。昔之保佑於桀者，今則舍桀而歸湯矣。天命於此難諶也，則克配上帝而有以受之。自天申之，保佑命之，于以荷天之寵，百祿是總，受休命於蒼蒼之表，而俯焉之無怍也。向之純佑於夏者，今則舍夏而
translation_en:
Seeking Learning

Being able to accord with Heaven’s heart and abundantly receive Heaven’s favor results from ruler and minister sharing a single virtue. For only virtue can move Heaven. Since the ruler and minister of Shang both possessed a single virtue, how could they fail to accord with Heaven’s heart and receive its favor? Formerly, when Yi Yin was about to retire and presented his admonitions to Tai Jia, his meaning was [?] that nothing is harder to accord with than Heaven’s heart, and nothing harder to receive than Heaven’s mandate. Thus, “surveying the myriad regions and guiding those destined to receive the mandate,” Heaven had an intention and sought the right person. In all the vastness of the world, who could reverently respond to Heaven’s heart? Only Yin and Tang, both possessing a single virtue, could accord with Heaven’s heart. “Favorably seeking one of single virtue, to make him lord of the spirits,” Heaven had a purpose and sought the right sovereign. Throughout the broad expanse within the Four Seas, who could accord with Heaven’s heart above? Only Tang and Yin, both possessing a single virtue, could fulfill Heaven’s intention.

Once they accorded with Heaven’s heart, they received Heaven’s mandate. Thus, although Heaven’s mandate is not constant, they examined Heaven’s ways directly and followed them, thereby becoming worthy to receive it. Heaven’s gracious charge encouraged them; its central charge brought blessings [?]. Thus they bore Heaven’s blessings, and the hundred blessings gathered upon them. They received the illustrious mandate amid Heaven’s radiant brightness and could look upward without shame. The protection formerly bestowed upon Jie now abandoned Jie and turned to Tang. Heaven’s mandate was in this respect difficult to trust; yet they could match the Supreme Lord in virtue and thereby receive it. From Heaven came repeated favor, protection, and the mandate. Thus they bore Heaven’s favor, and the hundred blessings were gathered together. They received the auspicious mandate from beyond the azure heavens and could look downward without shame. title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之商矣吁天心未易享也而能享之天命未易
受也而能受之皆本於君臣之一德如此今王
可不純一其德享天心以永天命哉抑有一代
之君必有一代之臣雲龍風虎之相從水濕火
燥之相就此固理也亦勢也天生勇智之湯而
必有元聖之伊尹明良相逢一德相協故能當
天之心受天之命而成弔伐之功伊尹告老將
歸恐太甲德不純一乃作誥而以成湯之所以
得天命者告之惟欲其常厥德而保天命於無
窮大臣之用心固宜如此也史臣詳而記之所
以曉天下後世立乎人之本朝者
詩
賔之初筵左右秩秩籩豆有楚殽核維旅
酒既和旨飲酒孔偕鍾鼓既設舉醻
逸逸大侯既抗弓矢斯張射夫既同
獻爾發功發彼有的以祈爾爵
===
同考試官訓導張 批
何瑭
揭書出此題頭緒頗多難於
punctuated:
之商矣。吁！天心未易享也，而能享之；天命未易受也，而能受之，皆本於君臣之一德如此。今王可不純一其德，享天心以永天命哉？抑有一代之君，必有一代之臣。雲龍風虎之相從，水濕火燥之相就，此固理也，亦勢也。天生勇智之湯，而必有元聖之伊尹，明良相逢，一德相協，故能當天之心，受天之命，而成弔伐之功。伊尹告老將歸，恐太甲德不純一，乃作誥，而以成湯之所以得天命者告之，惟欲其常厥德，而保天命於無窮。大臣之用心，固宜如此也。史臣詳而記之，所以曉天下後世立乎人之本朝者。

詩
賔之初筵，左右秩秩。籩豆有楚，殽核維旅。酒既和旨，飲酒孔偕。鍾鼓既設，舉醻逸逸。大侯既抗，弓矢斯張。射夫既同，獻爾發功。發彼有的，以祈爾爵。

同考試官訓導張，批。
何瑭
揭書出此題，頭緒頗多，難於
translation_en:
…and gone over to Shang. Ah! Heaven’s favor is not easily won, yet they won it; Heaven’s mandate is not easily received, yet they received it. All this was rooted in the shared virtue of ruler and minister. Can the present king fail to make his virtue pure and undivided, winning Heaven’s favor so as to perpetuate Heaven’s mandate? Moreover, for every age’s ruler there must be that age’s minister. Clouds follow the dragon, and winds the tiger; water flows toward damp places, and fire takes to dry things. This is both a principle and a natural tendency. When Heaven produced Tang, brave and wise, there necessarily appeared Yi Yin, the great sage. An enlightened ruler and a worthy minister met, united in a single virtue. Thus they could accord with Heaven’s heart, receive Heaven’s mandate, and accomplish their work of consoling the afflicted and punishing the guilty. When Yi Yin requested retirement on grounds of age and was about to withdraw, he feared that Tai Jia’s virtue might not remain pure and undivided. He therefore composed an admonition explaining how Cheng Tang had obtained Heaven’s mandate. His sole desire was that Tai Jia remain constant in his virtue and preserve Heaven’s mandate forever. Such indeed should be the concern of a great minister. The court historian recorded this in detail to instruct those throughout the realm and in later generations who serve at their sovereign’s court.

Book of Odes
When the guests first take their places at the feast,
Those to left and right are orderly.
The bamboo baskets and wooden vessels stand neatly arranged;
Meats and fruits are set out.
The wine is well blended and delicious;
The drinkers are in perfect harmony.
Bells and drums have been set in place;
They raise their cups in reciprocal toasts with easy grace.
The great archery target has been raised;
Bows and arrows are made ready.
The archers have assembled:
Display your skill in shooting!
Shoot at that target’s center,
To seek your cup of wine.
