title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
措詞是篇斂煩就簡且筆力雄健必熟於飽經者宜置前列
同考試官學正張　批　此題亦敘事體能發揮親切而
不悔不冗者僅見此篇
考試官訓導陳　批　事不遺〻文條暢可佳
考試官學正逯　批　鋪敘燕射禮儀之盛宛然在目是宜
錄之
古人因射而飲禮儀極其盛焉甚矣古人飲酒
之不苟也茲因射而飲其禮儀之盛如此又何
過舉之有哉是詩衛武公飲酒悔過而作也此
===
言因射而飲者始時禮儀之盛謂夫當射禮未
行之先適迎賓即席之始有列於筵之左者秩
秩乎其不紊有列於筵之右者秩秩乎其不雜
籩豆所以盛殽核楚然羅列之整齊殽核所以
實籩豆旅然陳設之俱備清酒在罇味調而氣
馨也飲此酧矣酧一而不亂也迨夫將射也樂
賓之鍾鼓先陳於堂上者司樂之屬則遷設於
下以避射位焉飲賓之醻爵已奠於席前者執
事之人則舉而行之往來有序焉射有大侯也
punctuated:
措詞。是篇斂煩就簡，且筆力雄健，必熟於飽經者，宜置前列。
同考試官學正張批：此題亦敘事體，能發揮親切而不悔不冗者，僅見此篇。
考試官訓導陳批：事不遺〻，文條暢，可佳。
考試官學正逯批：鋪敘燕射禮儀之盛，宛然在目，是宜錄之。
古人因射而飲，禮儀極其盛焉。甚矣，古人飲酒之不苟也！茲因射而飲，其禮儀之盛如此，又何過舉之有哉？是詩衛武公飲酒悔過而作也。此言因射而飲者始時禮儀之盛，謂夫當射禮未行之先，適迎賓即席之始，有列於筵之左者，秩秩乎其不紊；有列於筵之右者，秩秩乎其不雜。籩豆所以盛殽核，楚然羅列之整齊；殽核所以實籩豆，旅然陳設之俱備。清酒在罇，味調而氣馨也；飲此酧矣，酧一而不亂也。迨夫將射也，樂賓之鍾鼓先陳於堂上者，司樂之屬則遷設於下，以避射位焉；飲賓之醻爵已奠於席前者，執事之人則舉而行之，往來有序焉。射有大侯也。
translation_en:
…to formulate the wording. This essay reduces complexity to simplicity, and its writing is vigorous and forceful. Its author must be thoroughly versed in the classics [?]; it deserves a place among the leading essays.
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: This topic likewise calls for a narrative treatment. This is the only essay I have seen that develops it aptly and closely, without obscurity [?] or prolixity.
Examiner Chen, an Assistant Instructor, comments: No detail is omitted [?], and the writing is well ordered and fluent. Commendable.
Examiner Lu, an Instructor, comments: Its full account of the splendid ceremonial of banqueting and archery brings the scene vividly before our eyes. It certainly merits inclusion.
The ancients drank in connection with archery, and their ceremonial was magnificent in the utmost. How scrupulous the ancients were in their drinking! Here they drank in connection with archery, with ceremonial of such magnificence: what misconduct could there have been? This poem was composed by Duke Wu of Wei in repentance for his faults in drinking. This passage describes the magnificence of the ceremonial at the outset, when drinking accompanied archery. It means that, before the archery rite began, just as the guests were welcomed and took their places, those arrayed to the left of the mats were orderly and undisturbed; those arrayed to the right were orderly and without confusion. The bamboo and wooden vessels held the dishes and fruits, neatly arrayed in orderly ranks; the dishes and fruits filled those vessels, all set out in a complete display. The clear wine stood in the wine jars, its flavor balanced and its aroma fragrant. They drank these reciprocal toasts, conducting them uniformly and without disorder [?]. When the archery was about to begin, the bells and drums used to entertain the guests, which had first been arrayed above in the hall, were moved below by the music officials’ subordinates, to clear the positions for archery. The cups for reciprocal toasts with the guests, already placed before their mats, were raised and passed by the attendants, moving back and forth in due order. For the archery there was a great target…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
始焉掩柬令也繫其下綱而既抗矣射有弓矢
也始焉戴橐令也亦既出之而斯張矣有三耦
焉亦既比也獻夫發矢之功有衆耦焉亦既同
也奏夫舍矢之績於是各心競云我非徒發也
正欲發彼有的以祈豐上之爵而飲乎汝焉我
非徒射也惟欲中彼大侯以祈豐上之觶而飲
乎爾焉夫一射飲之間禮儀之盛如此是無過
之可舉矣武公悔過而以此為言非篤於自脩
者能如是哉抑論之酒之為物郊祀之所必先
===
燕饗之所必用誠不可缺者也但飲之而不節
則内有以喪其德外有以喪其儀甚則釀成家
國之禍者有矣故武王於康叔嘗作酒誥以訓
之今武公飲酒悔過自作此詩以戒焉一篇之
中丁寧反覆極言飲者常始乎治而卒乎亂匪
徒自戒所以戒人也匪徒戒人所以戒後世也
若武公者可謂能守武王康叔之家法者歟世
之酗酒怠政者尚其鑒之
穆穆文王於緝熙敬止假哉天命
punctuated:
始焉掩柬，令也；繫其下綱，而既抗矣。射有弓矢也，始焉戴橐，令也；亦既出之，而斯張矣。有三耦焉，亦既比也，獻夫發矢之功；有衆耦焉，亦既同也，奏夫舍矢之績。於是各心競云：「我非徒發也，正欲發彼有的，以祈豐上之爵，而飲乎汝焉；我非徒射也，惟欲中彼大侯，以祈豐上之觶，而飲乎爾焉。」夫一射飲之間，禮儀之盛如此，是無過之可舉矣。武公悔過而以此為言，非篤於自脩者能如是哉？抑論之，酒之為物，郊祀之所必先，燕饗之所必用，誠不可缺者也。但飲之而不節，則内有以喪其德，外有以喪其儀，甚則釀成家國之禍者有矣。故武王於康叔嘗作《酒誥》以訓之。今武公飲酒悔過，自作此詩以戒焉。一篇之中，丁寧反覆，極言飲者常始乎治而卒乎亂。匪徒自戒，所以戒人也；匪徒戒人，所以戒後世也。若武公者，可謂能守武王、康叔之家法者歟？世之酗酒怠政者，尚其鑒之！
穆穆文王，於緝熙敬止，假哉天命！
translation_en:
…At first, the target was gathered up [?], as prescribed; its lower cords were then fastened, and it was raised. For the archery there were bows and arrows. At first, these were kept in their cases [?], as prescribed; they were then taken out, and the bows were drawn. The three pairs of archers had been matched, and displayed their skill in discharging arrows; the other pairs had likewise assembled, and demonstrated their accomplishment in shooting. Each, inwardly competing, said: “I do not merely discharge an arrow: I aim to hit that marked target, to obtain the cup on the feng cupstand and make you drink. I do not merely shoot: I aim to hit that great target, to obtain the goblet on the feng cupstand and make you drink.” Within this single occasion of archery and drinking, ritual observance was so splendid that no fault could be cited. Duke Wu regretted his faults and spoke of this: could anyone who was not deeply committed to cultivating himself have done so?
To discuss it further, wine is something that must take precedence in the suburban sacrifices and must be used at banquets; it is indeed indispensable. Yet drinking without restraint causes one inwardly to lose one’s virtue and outwardly to lose one’s decorum. In extreme cases, it has even brewed calamities for families and states. Thus King Wu once composed the “Announcement on Wine” to instruct Kang Shu. Now Duke Wu, regretting his faults in drinking, himself composed this poem as a warning. Throughout the piece, he earnestly reiterates his admonitions, explaining fully how drinkers commonly begin in order and end in disorder. He was not merely warning himself, but also warning others; not merely warning others, but also warning later generations. Could one such as Duke Wu be said to have upheld the ancestral precepts of King Wu and Kang Shu? May those in this world who drink to excess and neglect government take warning from him!
“Solemn and majestic was King Wen; ah, he continued in brightness and abided in reverence. Great indeed is Heaven’s Mandate!”

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
李紳
同考試官訓導張　批〔寫出周公告戒之忠溢於言表當是作手〕
同考試官學正張　批〔緝熙敬止文王之所以爲聖者盡在是矣非學力有得者能如此作乎敬羨敬羨〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔此三句正所謂非周公不能作者子能盡發於筆端其亦知周公之言者歟〕
考試官學正逯　批〔講天人處親切有味〕
惟聖德純乎敬故天命所由集夫德者得天之
===
本也今聖德深遠而不已其敬如此則夫大哉
天命豈能舍之而他往哉昔周公追述文王之
德以戒成王及此謂夫我有周受命而興也豈
偶然哉良由我文王幽然而深聲色之不大淵
淵其淵探之無涯涘也玄然而遠形迹之不露
浩浩其天測之無限量也夫德之深遠敬之不
已耳遂嘆美之以爲我文王也一敬常存而繼
續光明有如一元流通貫四時而無端何有於
窮已乎一敬不雜而連屬昭著有如二曜循環
punctuated:
李紳

同考試官訓導張　批〔寫出周公告戒之忠，溢於言表，當是作手。〕
同考試官學正張　批〔緝熙敬止，文王之所以爲聖者盡在是矣。非學力有得者能如此作乎？敬羨，敬羨！〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔此三句正所謂非周公不能作者，子能盡發於筆端，其亦知周公之言者歟？〕
考試官學正逯　批〔講天人處，親切有味。〕

惟聖德純乎敬，故天命所由集。夫德者，得天之本也。今聖德深遠而不已，其敬如此，則夫大哉天命，豈能舍之而他往哉？昔周公追述文王之德以戒成王，及此，謂夫我有周受命而興也，豈偶然哉？良由我文王幽然而深，聲色之不大，淵淵其淵，探之無涯涘也；玄然而遠，形迹之不露，浩浩其天，測之無限量也。夫德之深遠，敬之不已耳。遂嘆美之，以爲我文王也，一敬常存而繼續光明，有如一元流通，貫四時而無端，何有於窮已乎？一敬不雜而連屬昭著，有如二曜循環……
translation_en:
Li Shen

Associate Examiner Zhang, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The Duke of Zhou’s loyal concern in issuing his admonition is conveyed beyond the words themselves. Surely this is an accomplished writer.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: 〔“Continuing in brightness and abiding in reverence”: all that made King Wen a sage lies in these words. Could anyone write like this without real attainment through study? Admiration and respect, admiration and respect!〕
Examiner Chen, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔These three phrases truly exemplify what is meant by saying that only the Duke of Zhou could have composed them. You have brought out their full meaning through your brush: surely you, too, understand the Duke of Zhou’s words!〕
Examiner Lu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of Heaven and humanity is incisive and rich in meaning.〕

Only because sagely virtue is pure in its reverence does Heaven’s Mandate converge upon it. Virtue is the foundation for winning Heaven’s favor. Now, when sagely virtue is profound and far-reaching, and its reverence unceasing in this way, how could the great Mandate of Heaven abandon it and go elsewhere? Formerly, the Duke of Zhou recalled King Wen’s virtue to admonish King Cheng. Coming to this point, he meant: “Could it have been by chance that our Zhou received the Mandate and rose to power? It was truly because our King Wen was inwardly profound, making no great display in voice or countenance. Deep indeed was his abyss: probe it, and there was no shore or limit. Mysterious and far-reaching, he left no outward traces. Vast indeed was his heaven: measure it, and there was no bound.” The profundity and far-reaching scope of his virtue were simply his unceasing reverence. Thus the Duke sighed in admiration and praised him, saying that our King Wen’s single-minded reverence was ever present, continually shining forth, like the primal vital force flowing through all four seasons without beginning or end. How could it ever be exhausted or cease? His single-minded reverence was unmixed, continuously manifest in brightness, like the sun and moon revolving in their courses …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
運晝夜而無窮何有於止息乎夫以文王之敬
純一不已如此是以上帝着之而不易之峻命
惟周是集有以成三分有二之鴻圖本宗百世
為天子者於是乎肇基矣彼蒼眷顧而大哉之
天命惟周是歸有以垂九年未集之大統支庶
百世為諸侯者於此乎託始矣夫文王德盛而
得天命如此此我周所以受命而代商也為嗣
王者可不知所自哉大抵源深則流自長德盛
則澤自遠惟文王也生而緝熙其敬沒而於昭
===
于天是以子孫蒙其福澤而君有天下焉周公
推本所自以告成王者亦惟欲其致勉於此敬
耳厥後成王果為有周之令主而致雍熙泰和
之盛治實有自於勉敬中來也噫若周公者可
謂善道其君者矣
春秋
公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍新
城　楚人圍許諸侯遂救許〔俱僖公〕
六年會王人晉人宋人齊人陳人蔡
punctuated:
運晝夜而無窮，何有於止息乎？夫以文王之敬，純一不已如此，是以上帝着之而不易之，峻命惟周是集，有以成三分有二之鴻圖，本宗百世為天子者於是乎肇基矣。彼蒼眷顧，而大哉之天命惟周是歸，有以垂九年未集之大統，支庶百世為諸侯者於此乎託始矣。夫文王德盛而得天命如此，此我周所以受命而代商也。為嗣王者，可不知所自哉？大抵源深則流自長，德盛則澤自遠。惟文王也，生而緝熙其敬，沒而於昭于天，是以子孫蒙其福澤而君有天下焉。周公推本所自以告成王者，亦惟欲其致勉於此敬耳。厥後成王果為有周之令主，而致雍熙泰和之盛治，實有自於勉敬中來也。噫！若周公者，可謂善道其君者矣。

春秋

公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許。〔俱僖公〕六年。會王人、晉人、宋人、齊人、陳人、蔡
translation_en:
…moving through day and night without end—how could there be any cessation? King Wen’s reverence was thus pure, undivided, and unceasing. Therefore the Lord on High made it manifest and did not alter it; the august Mandate gathered upon Zhou alone. This enabled him to establish the grand design of possessing two of the realm’s three parts, laying the foundation for the principal lineage to hold the position of Son of Heaven for a hundred generations. Azure Heaven looked upon him with favor, and its great Mandate devolved upon Zhou alone. Thus he could bequeath the great succession whose work remained unfinished after nine years, establishing the beginnings from which collateral branches would become regional lords for a hundred generations. Such was the abundance of King Wen’s virtue and his receipt of Heaven’s Mandate: this is why our Zhou received the Mandate and replaced Shang. Could a succeeding king fail to understand its source?

In general, when the source is deep, the stream naturally flows far; when virtue abounds, its blessings naturally extend into the distant future. King Wen continually brightened his reverence while alive and shone gloriously in Heaven after death. Thus his descendants enjoyed his blessings and ruled all under Heaven. When the Duke of Zhou traced this back to its source and instructed King Cheng, he wished only that the king should exert himself in this reverence. Thereafter King Cheng indeed became an excellent ruler of Zhou and brought about a flourishing government of harmony, prosperity, and profound peace. This truly arose from his diligent cultivation of reverence. Ah! Someone like the Duke of Zhou may indeed be said to have guided his ruler well.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao to attack Zheng and besiege Xincheng. Men of Chu besieged Xu; the regional lords thereupon went to Xu’s rescue. [Both entries concern Duke Xi’s sixth year; the transcription separates the year from the annotation irregularly.]

Met with a representative of the king and men of Jin, Song, Qi, Chen, and Cai …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
人秦人盟于翟泉〔僖公二十九年 狄〕
侵齊　晋人秦人圍鄭〔俱僖公三十〕
年
朱㷷
同考試官教諭劉　批〔此題傳意自明不費臆說場中 多牽强不合獨此逈出衆作是用錄出〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔春秋屬詞比事此作得之〕
考試官學正逯　批〔理明詞正得春秋謹嚴體〕
春秋紀二伯有事於貳國有美其因外患而能
===
移師以恤之者有譏其因外侮不能移師以却
之者此齊桓能移圍鄭之師以救許晋文不能
移圍鄭之師以却狄春秋備書其予奪之意見
矣且夫我僖六年齊桓主伯因鄭逃首止翼戴
儲君之盟遂合列國伐鄭而圍新造之邑聲其
無王之非而罪著于上聞其即夷之故而討顯
于下禁於是時興師圍許盖欲攻所必救以釋
鄭也使桓公不移圍鄭之師以救之則攘夷安
夏之義失矣幸而有見乎此即解新密之圍以
punctuated:
人、秦人盟于翟泉〔僖公二十九年 狄〕。侵齊。晋人、秦人圍鄭〔俱僖公三十〕年。
朱㷷
同考試官教諭劉批〔此題傳意自明，不費臆說。場中多牽强不合，獨此逈出衆作，是用錄出。〕
考試官訓導陳批〔春秋屬詞比事，此作得之。〕
考試官學正逯批〔理明詞正，得春秋謹嚴體。〕
春秋紀二伯有事於貳國，有美其因外患而能移師以恤之者，有譏其因外侮不能移師以却之者。此齊桓能移圍鄭之師以救許，晋文不能移圍鄭之師以却狄，春秋備書，其予奪之意見矣。且夫我僖六年，齊桓主伯，因鄭逃首止翼戴儲君之盟，遂合列國伐鄭，而圍新造之邑，聲其無王之非，而罪著于上；聞其即夷之故，而討顯于下。禁於是時興師圍許，盖欲攻所必救以釋鄭也。使桓公不移圍鄭之師以救之，則攘夷安夏之義失矣。幸而有見乎此，即解新密之圍以
translation_en:
…men and the men of Qin made a covenant at Diquan. 〔The twenty-ninth year of Duke Xi; Di [?].〕 Invaded Qi. The men of Jin and Qin besieged Zheng. 〔Both in Duke Xi’s thirtieth〕 year. [The transcription appears to have displaced “Di,” the subject of “invaded Qi,” into the preceding annotation.]
Zhu Juan [?] 朱㷷
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning conveyed by the commentaries on this topic is clear in itself and requires no speculative explanation. Most candidates forced interpretations that did not fit. This answer alone stands far above the others; hence its selection for inclusion.〕
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The Spring and Autumn Annals links expressions and juxtaposes events; this essay grasps that method.〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Its reasoning is clear and its language correct. It captures the careful and rigorous manner of the Spring and Autumn Annals.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals records two hegemons undertaking military action against a state of divided allegiance. In one case it praises a hegemon who, when an external threat arose, could redirect his army to bring relief; in the other it censures a hegemon who, when an external invasion occurred, could not redirect his army to repel it. Thus Duke Huan of Qi could redirect the army besieging Zheng to rescue Xu, whereas Duke Wen of Jin could not redirect the army besieging Zheng to repel the Di. By recording these matters fully, the Spring and Autumn Annals makes its approval and disapproval apparent.
Now, in the sixth year of our Duke Xi, Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony. Because Zheng had withdrawn from the covenant at Shouzhi to support and uphold the heir apparent, he assembled the various states to attack Zheng and besiege its newly built town. He proclaimed its offense of disregarding the king, making its guilt manifest before the sovereign above; he made known its adherence to the barbarians, making the grounds for punishment evident to those below. At this time, [Chu?] raised an army and besieged Xu, presumably intending to attack a place that had to be rescued and thereby relieve Zheng. Had Duke Huan failed to redirect the army besieging Zheng to rescue Xu, he would have forfeited the principle of repelling the barbarians and securing the Xia states. Fortunately, he understood this and lifted the siege of Xinmi in order to…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
赴許人之難緩不急之討而舉拯焚救溺之義
隳垂成之功以慰嘉穀霖雨之望禦彼門庭之
冦䘏此倒懸之民下視晉文之行事不啻若天
淵之懸絶矣春秋於伐鄭之後書齊人圍許諸
侯遂救許者所以著其為善之尤也詩曰豈不
懷歸畏此簡書桓公有見於此與馴至我僖季
世晉文繼伯首因鄭人背叛不禮既盟翟泉以
謀之繼欲觀其可攻與否又提師旅以伐之載
書共讀於壇坫之上戎馬蹂踐乎溱洧之區狄
===
於斯時潛師侵齊蓋闞晉有鄭虞欲以侮晉也
使文公能移圍鄭之師以伐之則方伯連師之
職脩矣夫何不此之顧乃偕西戎之秦同舉圍
鄭之兵徒知夙夕睚眦之怨在所必報不知夷
狄豺狼之人尤不可厭舍大敵而計小怨縱遠
夷以陵中國回視齊桓之所行不啻若氷炭之
相反矣故春秋於翟泉之後書狄侵齊晉人秦
人圍鄭直書其事以貶之也詩曰戎狄是膺荊
舒是懲文公誠有昧於此矣噫此齊桓之伯所
punctuated: 赴許人之難，緩不急之討，而舉拯焚救溺之義；隳垂成之功，以慰嘉穀霖雨之望。禦彼門庭之冦，䘏此倒懸之民，下視晉文之行事，不啻若天淵之懸絶矣。《春秋》於伐鄭之後書「齊人圍許，諸侯遂救許」者，所以著其為善之尤也。《詩》曰：「豈不懷歸？畏此簡書。」桓公有見於此與！馴至我僖季世，晉文繼伯，首因鄭人背叛不禮，既盟翟泉以謀之；繼欲觀其可攻與否，又提師旅以伐之。載書共讀於壇坫之上，戎馬蹂踐乎溱洧之區。狄於斯時潛師侵齊，蓋闞晉有鄭虞，欲以侮晉也。使文公能移圍鄭之師以伐之，則方伯連師之職脩矣。夫何不此之顧，乃偕西戎之秦，同舉圍鄭之兵？徒知夙夕睚眦之怨在所必報，不知夷狄豺狼之人尤不可厭。舍大敵而計小怨，縱遠夷以陵中國，回視齊桓之所行，不啻若氷炭之相反矣。故《春秋》於翟泉之後書「狄侵齊，晉人、秦人圍鄭」，直書其事以貶之也。《詩》曰：「戎狄是膺，荊舒是懲。」文公誠有昧於此矣。噫！此齊桓之伯所
translation_en:
…to rush to the aid of the people of Xu in their distress, postponing a punitive expedition that was not urgent and fulfilling the righteous duty of rescuing people from fire and drowning. He abandoned an achievement nearing completion to satisfy their longing for deliverance, like good grain awaiting soaking rain. He repelled the raiders at their gates and relieved the people in their desperate plight. Looking down upon Duke Wen of Jin’s conduct by comparison, the gulf was indeed as great as that between heaven and the depths. That the Spring and Autumn Annals, after recording the attack on Zheng, writes, “The men of Qi [?] besieged Xu; the assembled lords thereupon rescued Xu,” serves to make manifest his exceptional goodness. The Book of Odes says: “Do I not long to return? I stand in awe of this written summons.” Duke Huan understood this, did he not!

In time, toward the end of the reign of our Duke Xi, Duke Wen of Jin succeeded as hegemon. Because the people of Zheng had betrayed him and treated him discourteously, he first made a covenant at Diquan to plan action against them. Then, wishing to see whether Zheng could be attacked, he again led an army against it. The covenant text was read together upon the ceremonial platform, while warhorses trampled the lands of the Zhen and Wei rivers. At this time, the Di secretly sent troops to invade Qi. Seeing that Jin was preoccupied with Zheng, they sought to take advantage of Jin. Had Duke Wen been able to redirect the army besieging Zheng to attack them, he would have fulfilled his duties as regional overlord and leader of the allied lords. Why did he disregard this and instead join Qin, a state of the western Rong, in raising troops to besiege Zheng? He knew only that the resentments he brooded over day and night, arising from the slightest affronts, must be avenged; he did not know that the wolfish peoples of the Yi and Di were especially impossible to satisfy. Abandoning a great enemy to reckon with a petty grievance, he allowed distant barbarians to overrun the central states. Compared with Duke Huan of Qi’s conduct, his actions were as opposed as ice and burning charcoal.

Thus, after the entry concerning Diquan, the Spring and Autumn Annals writes, “The Di invaded Qi; the men of Jin and the men of Qin besieged Zheng.” It records the events directly in order to censure him. The Book of Odes says: “The Rong and Di were struck down; Jing and Shu were chastised.” Duke Wen was truly blind to this. Alas! The reason Duke Huan of Qi’s hegemony…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
以為賢有非晉文所可比者良以此耳不特是
為然桓公得江黄而不用於伐楚文公謂非致
秦則不可與楚爭楚抑而秦興桓公會則不適
三川盟則不加王人文公會畿內則抗矣盟子
虎則悖矣桓公寧不得鄭不納子華懼其獎臣
抑君不可以訓文公為元咺而執君窮經歷數
無施不然否則仲尼稱其一匡孟子與其為盛
何為而不及文公哉此又讀經者之所當知
閏月不告月猶朝于廟〔文公六年〕
===
同考試官教諭劉　批〔此題場中作者皆以閏月不告月為惜其禮之廢與幸字相對甚矣傳意此篇得之是宜錄出〕　吳道純
考試官訓導陳　批〔寫出聖人愛禮之意非明於經者不能也〕
考試官學正逯　批〔詞嚴理正得春秋法〕
春秋之於望國紀其禮之不當廢幸其禮之不
盡廢夫禮之係於人也大矣春秋既紀魯文之
不告朔而又幸其朝廟斯可見焉且閏月雖為
非月之正然唐典以是而定時成歲周制以之
punctuated:
以為賢，有非晉文所可比者，良以此耳。不特是為然，桓公得江、黄而不用於伐楚，文公謂非致秦則不可與楚爭，楚抑而秦興。桓公會則不適三川，盟則不加王人；文公會畿內則抗矣，盟子虎則悖矣。桓公寧不得鄭，不納子華，懼其獎臣抑君，不可以訓；文公為元咺而執君。窮經歷數，無施不然。否則，仲尼稱其一匡，孟子與其為盛，何為而不及文公哉？此又讀經者之所當知。

閏月不告月，猶朝于廟。〔文公六年〕

同考試官教諭劉　批〔此題場中作者皆以閏月不告月為惜其禮之廢，與幸字相對。甚矣傳意，此篇得之，是宜錄出。〕　吳道純
考試官訓導陳　批〔寫出聖人愛禮之意，非明於經者不能也。〕
考試官學正逯　批〔詞嚴理正，得春秋法。〕

春秋之於望國，紀其禮之不當廢，幸其禮之不盡廢。夫禮之係於人也大矣！春秋既紀魯文之不告朔，而又幸其朝廟，斯可見焉。且閏月雖為非月之正，然唐典以是而定時成歲，周制以之
translation_en:
…This is precisely why Duke Huan of Qi’s hegemony is judged worthy in ways that Duke Wen of Jin’s cannot match. Nor is this the only instance. Duke Huan secured the allegiance of Jiang and Huang but did not employ them in attacking Chu. Duke Wen held that without bringing Qin into the alliance he could not contend with Chu: Chu was checked, but Qin rose. When Duke Huan convened meetings, he did not go to Sanchuan; in covenants, he did not place himself above the king’s representatives. Duke Wen, however, showed insubordination by convening a meeting within the royal domain, and violated proper order by binding Zihu to a covenant. Duke Huan preferred to forgo Zheng’s allegiance rather than accept Zihua’s proposal, fearing that encouraging a minister while suppressing his ruler would set an unacceptable precedent. Duke Wen, by contrast, arrested a ruler on Yuan Xuan’s behalf. Exhaustively examine the Classic and enumerate the cases: the same holds throughout. Otherwise, why would Zhongni praise Duke Huan for once setting the world right, and Mencius acknowledge the preeminence of his achievements, without extending such praise to Duke Wen? This too is something readers of the Classic should understand.

“In the intercalary month, the announcement of the month was not performed; yet he still paid his respects at the ancestral temple.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Wen.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The candidates who addressed this topic in the examination hall all understood “in the intercalary month, the announcement of the month was not performed” as expressing regret at the abandonment of the rite, in contrast to the word “fortunately.” The meaning of the commentary is profound [?]; this essay has grasped it and therefore deserves inclusion.〕 The essay is by Wu Daochun.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: 〔It conveys the Sage’s concern for ritual—something impossible for anyone who does not understand the Classic.〕
Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor: 〔Its language is rigorous and its reasoning correct; it captures the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals.〕

In its treatment of the eminent state [?], the Spring and Autumn Annals records that its rites ought not to have been abandoned and expresses relief that they had not been abandoned entirely. How great is the importance of ritual to human life! This is evident in the Annals’ recording that Duke Wen of Lu failed to perform the announcement of the new moon, while also expressing relief that he paid his respects at the ancestral temple. Moreover, although an intercalary month is not a regular month, the Canon of Tang uses it to fix the seasons and complete the year, and the institutions of Zhou use it to…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而詔王居門終月是古者天子班告朔於邦國
未嘗以為附月之餘而弗之數也奈何春秋中
葉魯文在位當夫閏月之臨不行告朔之禮昏
庸怠惰上不稟夫君親之命況溺宴安下不授
夫萬民之時徒知此為非月之正禮可殺也而
不知節氣分數之所關徒知此為附月之餘禮
可簡也而不知朝野政事之所係今魯文公執
一己之偏見蔑天下之通禮安知後世不因此
循襲效尤而亦廢此閏月之禮邪春秋紀之者
===
以此孔子曰周公其衰矣觀此益信其然當是
時也使魯文迷而不悟後先一轍則尤可憾也
幸而舉行故事猶朝于廟冠服楚楚趨進於廟
庭之中環佩鏘鏘躬拜乎堂階之下雖曰大典
既失而禮義之天未泯雖曰舊章已壞而君親
之念猶存夫以魯文前過固不可贖一節猶有
可取安知後世不由此而因名求實以復此閏
月之禮邪春秋幸之者以此孔子曰我愛其禮
觀此亦可以釋憾矣噫魯號儒書秉禮之邦今
punctuated:
而詔王居門終月。是古者天子班告朔於邦國，未嘗以為附月之餘而弗之數也。奈何春秋中葉，魯文在位，當夫閏月之臨，不行告朔之禮？昏庸怠惰，上不稟夫君親之命；況溺宴安，下不授夫萬民之時。徒知此為非月之正，禮可殺也，而不知節氣分數之所關；徒知此為附月之餘，禮可簡也，而不知朝野政事之所係。今魯文公執一己之偏見，蔑天下之通禮，安知後世不因此循襲效尤，而亦廢此閏月之禮邪？春秋紀之者以此。孔子曰：「周公其衰矣！」觀此，益信其然。

當是時也，使魯文迷而不悟，後先一轍，則尤可憾也。幸而舉行故事，猶朝于廟，冠服楚楚，趨進於廟庭之中；環佩鏘鏘，躬拜乎堂階之下。雖曰大典既失，而禮義之天未泯；雖曰舊章已壞，而君親之念猶存。夫以魯文前過，固不可贖，一節猶有可取，安知後世不由此而因名求實，以復此閏月之禮邪？春秋幸之者以此。孔子曰：「我愛其禮。」觀此，亦可以釋憾矣。

噫！魯號儒書秉禮之邦，今
translation_en:
…and instructed the king to remain at the gate for the entire month. Thus, when the Son of Heaven in antiquity distributed the calendar to the states for the announcement of each new moon, he never regarded the intercalary month as a mere surplus appended to another month and left it uncounted. How, then, could Duke Wen of Lu, reigning in the middle of the Spring and Autumn period, fail to perform the rite of announcing the new moon when an intercalary month arrived? Benighted and indolent, he failed in his obligations above to receive the commands of his sovereign and forebears; sunk in ease and pleasure [?], he failed in his obligations below to communicate the seasons to the myriad people. He knew only that this was not a regular month and that its rites could be curtailed, but did not understand its bearing on the solar terms and calendrical fractions. He knew only that this was a surplus appended to another month and that its rites could be simplified, but did not understand its connection with the affairs of government at court and throughout the land. Now Duke Wen of Lu clung to his own partial view and slighted the rites universally observed throughout the realm. Who could know whether later generations might follow this precedent, imitate his fault, and likewise abolish the rites for the intercalary month? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded it. Confucius said, “How the legacy of the Duke of Zhou has declined!” Seeing this makes one all the more convinced that it was so.

At that time, had Duke Wen of Lu persisted in his delusion without awakening, continuing just as before, there would have been still greater cause for regret. Fortunately, he carried out the established observance and still paid homage at the ancestral temple. His cap and robes were immaculate as he advanced with quick steps into the temple courtyard; his pendant jades rang out as he bowed below the steps of the hall. Though the great ceremony had already been lost, his Heaven-endowed sense of ritual and righteousness had not been extinguished. Though the old ordinances had already been impaired, his regard for his sovereign and forebears remained. Duke Wen’s earlier fault could certainly not be redeemed, yet this one aspect of his conduct was still commendable. Who could know whether later generations might take this as their starting point, seek the substance through the surviving name, and thereby restore the rites for the intercalary month? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals expressed relief at it. Confucius said, “I cherish the rite.” Seeing this, one may also find relief from regret.

Alas! Lu was reputed to be a state of Confucian learning [?] that upheld ritual. Now…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
文公名不稱情如此良可嘅夫大抵周公制禮
作樂欲傳之天下後世豈意數傳而至文公之
子孫如是不執耶不特是也觀其以練祭則緩
於作主以宗廟則大室屋壞以賦政則四不視
朔以邦交則三不會盟其尊王事伯之禮事神
治民之道俱失矣先儒謂魯國之衰自文公始
詎不諒哉
禮記
禮義以爲器故事行有考也
===
許浚達
同考試官教諭朱　批〔此篇用前章事入講渾然一露〕
圭角初若不經意者宜取以冠本房
考試官訓導陳　批〔典實〕
考試官學正逯　批〔圓融可嘉〕
聖人以道而爲治則治功有所成矣蓋道不外
乎禮義也能用禮義如成器則事之所行豈有
不得其成者哉昔記禮運者意謂聖人之作則
也於凡天下之事惟其制之也有道故其行之
punctuated:
文公名不稱情如此，良可嘅夫！大抵周公制禮作樂，欲傳之天下後世，豈意數傳而至文公之子孫，如是不執耶？不特是也，觀其以練祭則緩於作主，以宗廟則大室屋壞，以賦政則四不視朔，以邦交則三不會盟，其尊王事伯之禮、事神治民之道俱失矣。先儒謂魯國之衰自文公始，詎不諒哉！

禮記
禮義以爲器，故事行有考也。

許浚達
同考試官教諭朱，批〔此篇用前章事入講，渾然一露〕圭角，初若不經意者，宜取以冠本房。
考試官訓導陳，批〔典實〕
考試官學正逯，批〔圓融可嘉〕

聖人以道而爲治，則治功有所成矣。蓋道不外乎禮義也，能用禮義如成器，則事之所行，豈有不得其成者哉？昔記禮運者，意謂聖人之作則也，於凡天下之事，惟其制之也有道，故其行之
translation_en:
…Duke Wen’s reputation was so far from matching the reality: truly lamentable! When the Duke of Zhou established rites and created music, he intended to transmit them throughout the world and to later generations. How could he have imagined that, after only a few generations, Duke Wen and his descendants would fail so utterly to uphold them? Nor was this all. In connection with the first-anniversary mourning sacrifice, he delayed making the spirit tablet; in the ancestral temple, the roof of the Grand Chamber collapsed; in administering government, he failed four times to attend the first-day-of-the-month observance; and in relations with other states, he failed three times to attend covenant assemblies. The rites of honoring the king and serving the hegemon, and the ways of serving the spirits and governing the people, were all abandoned. Earlier Confucian scholars said that the decline of Lu began with Duke Wen. Is this not indeed true?

Record of Rites
“Ritual and righteousness are used as instruments; thus undertakings, when carried out, yield accomplishments.”

Xu Junda
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “This essay draws on matters from the preceding section to open its exposition. Its integration is seamless, [without?] exposing sharp edges [?], and at first it seems uncontrived. It should be selected to rank first among the papers in this examining room.”
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial.”
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Admirably rounded and coherent.”

When the sage governs by the Way, his work of government achieves results. For the Way lies nowhere beyond ritual and righteousness. If he can employ ritual and righteousness as finished instruments, how could any undertaking he carries out fail to reach completion? The author who recorded the “Evolution of Ritual” meant that, when the sage establishes standards for all the affairs of the world, it is precisely because he regulates them according to the Way that, when he puts them into practice …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
也有成何則禮者原於天道之昇降衷所均賦
也聖人因而脩之以為制事之器則夫綱維世
變防範人心者自不能舍之而他圖義者本於
天德之利秉彝所共有也聖人因而達之以為
處事之具則夫裁制人情權輿事理者自不能
違之而遠取如君臣父子固有親義之理矣豈
能徇情而自盡哉必以禮義而正之篤之不啻
持權衡以較輕重焉兄弟夫婦固有別序之理
矣豈能率意而自行哉必以禮義而睦之和之
===
不啻以規矩而正方圓焉夫聖人用禮義如成
器如此吾知禮一立而萬事序自無紊亂錯雜
之弊加於身而錯於前若無不得其宜也義一
行而百度舉自無混淆倒置之非發乎邇而見
乎遠者罔不得其當也如正君臣篤父子則因
正極其義而尊卑之分定因篤極其親而慈孝
之愛隆事之不底於成者何有乎睦兄弟和夫
婦則因睦極其序而塤篪之奏協因和極其別
而關雎之化行事之不逮於考者何有乎吁治
punctuated:
也有成。何則？禮者原於天道之昇降，衷所均賦也。聖人因而脩之，以為制事之器，則夫綱維世變、防範人心者，自不能舍之而他圖。義者本於天德之利，秉彝所共有也。聖人因而達之，以為處事之具，則夫裁制人情、權輿事理者，自不能違之而遠取。如君臣父子，固有親義之理矣，豈能徇情而自盡哉？必以禮義而正之、篤之，不啻持權衡以較輕重焉。兄弟夫婦，固有別序之理矣，豈能率意而自行哉？必以禮義而睦之、和之，不啻以規矩而正方圓焉。
夫聖人用禮義如成器如此，吾知禮一立而萬事序，自無紊亂錯雜之弊，加於身而錯於前，若無不得其宜也。義一行而百度舉，自無混淆倒置之非，發乎邇而見乎遠者，罔不得其當也。如正君臣、篤父子，則因正極其義，而尊卑之分定；因篤極其親，而慈孝之愛隆。事之不底於成者，何有乎？睦兄弟、和夫婦，則因睦極其序，而塤篪之奏協；因和極其別，而關雎之化行。事之不逮於考者，何有乎？吁！治
translation_en:
…also achieves completion. Why is this so? Ritual originates in the ascending and descending movements of the Way of Heaven, in the inner moral nature imparted equally to all [?]. The sage accordingly cultivates it, making it an instrument for regulating affairs. Thus, in maintaining order amid worldly changes and restraining the human heart, one cannot abandon it and devise some other means. Righteousness is rooted in the beneficence of Heaven’s virtue and is shared by all who possess the constant moral nature. The sage accordingly extends it, making it a means for handling affairs. Thus, in regulating human feelings and establishing the principles of affairs, one cannot depart from it and seek elsewhere. Between ruler and minister, and father and son, there are inherently principles of righteousness and affection. Yet how could people simply follow their feelings and fully discharge these relationships? They must use ritual and righteousness to rectify the former relationship and deepen the latter, just as one uses a balance to compare weights. Between elder and younger brothers, and husband and wife, there are inherently principles of precedence and distinction. Yet how could people simply act as they please? They must use ritual and righteousness to bring concord to the former relationship and harmony to the latter, just as one uses compass and square to make circles and squares true.
Such is the sage’s use of ritual and righteousness as finished instruments. I know that once ritual is established, all affairs fall into order, naturally free from the defects of disorder and confusion. Whatever concerns one’s person or is set before one seems invariably to find its proper place. Once righteousness is put into practice, all institutions function, naturally free from the errors of confusion and inversion. Whatever begins nearby and manifests itself far away invariably attains what is fitting. Thus, in rectifying the relationship between ruler and minister and deepening that between father and son, rectification brings righteousness to its fullest realization, establishing the distinctions between superior and inferior; deepening brings affection to its fullest realization, enriching the love expressed in parental kindness and filial devotion. What affair could then fail to reach completion? In bringing concord to brothers and harmony to husband and wife, concord brings precedence to its fullest realization, so that the earthen ocarina and bamboo flute sound in harmony; harmony brings distinction to its fullest realization, so that the transforming influence of “The Ospreys” takes effect. What affair could then fail to attain accomplishment? Ah! Governance…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
道既盡治功自成聖人之作則有如是夫擲論
此章言聖人作則者凡十條無非致治之良法
也而終之曰四靈以為畜何哉蓋天地萬物本
吾一體聖人克盡治道於已而其效至於孚格
鳥獸固其宜矣周子曰聖王脩禮法明教化三
綱正九疇敘百姓太和鳥獸魚鱉咸若亦此意
也噫為政而欲求治效之隆盍於其所自圖之
是故清明象天廣大象地終始象四時周
還象風雨五色成文而不亂八風從
律而不姦百度得數而有常小大相
成終始相生倡和清濁迭相為經故
樂行而倫清耳目聰明血氣和平移
風易俗天下皆寧
盧盤
同考試官教諭朱　批〔作長題難於整潔此篇法度森嚴詞理順當錄之以式來學〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔體格自別〕
考試官學正逯　批〔得聖人作樂之本意〕
punctuated:
道既盡，治功自成，聖人之作則有如是夫！擲論，此章言聖人作則者凡十條，無非致治之良法也，而終之曰「四靈以為畜」，何哉？蓋天地萬物，本吾一體。聖人克盡治道於已，而其效至於孚格鳥獸，固其宜矣。周子曰：「聖王脩禮法，明教化，三綱正，九疇敘，百姓太和，鳥獸魚鱉咸若。」亦此意也。噫！為政而欲求治效之隆，盍於其所自圖之？
是故清明象天，廣大象地，終始象四時，周還象風雨。五色成文而不亂，八風從律而不姦，百度得數而有常，小大相成，終始相生，倡和清濁，迭相為經。故樂行而倫清，耳目聰明，血氣和平，移風易俗，天下皆寧。
盧盤
同考試官教諭朱　批〔作長題難於整潔，此篇法度森嚴，詞理順當，錄之以式來學。〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔體格自別。〕
考試官學正逯　批〔得聖人作樂之本意。〕
translation_en:
…once the Way of government has been fully realized, the accomplishments of government follow naturally. Such is the sage’s establishment of standards! To discuss this [?]: this chapter lists ten instances of the sage’s establishment of standards, all of them excellent methods for achieving good government. Why, then, does it conclude by saying, “The four numinous creatures are kept as domestic animals”? Heaven, earth, and the myriad things are fundamentally one body with us. When the sage fully realizes the Way of government within himself, it is only fitting that its effects should reach even birds and beasts and win their trust. Master Zhou said: “The sage king cultivates ritual and laws and makes instruction and moral transformation clear. The Three Bonds are set right, the Nine Categories put in order, and the people attain supreme harmony; birds, beasts, fish, and turtles all flourish in accordance with their natures.” This expresses the same idea. Ah! Those who govern and wish to achieve splendid results—why do they not direct their efforts to the source from which these results arise?
Thus, its purity and brightness model Heaven; its breadth and greatness model Earth; its endings and beginnings model the four seasons; and its cyclical movement models wind and rain. The five colors form patterns without disorder; the winds of the eight directions follow the pitch standards without deviation. The hundred measures attain their proper numbers and possess constancy. The small and the great complete one another; endings and beginnings give rise to one another. Leading and responding, high and low tones alternately serve as the guiding thread. Thus, when music is practiced, human relationships become clear, ears and eyes become perceptive, the blood and vital energies become harmonious and balanced, customs and usages are transformed, and all under Heaven is at peace.
Lu Pan.
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔“When writing on a long topic, it is difficult to achieve an orderly and polished composition. This essay is rigorously structured, and its language and reasoning are fitting and coherent. It is recorded here as a model for future students.”〕
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“Its form and style are distinctive.”〕
Examiner Lu 逯, Instructor, comments: 〔“It grasps the sage’s original intention in creating music.”〕

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
樂之作也備法制之詳樂之數也極功效之大
甚矣樂觀其深也然非備法制之詳安能致功
效之大若是哉想昔樂記之意謂夫君子之作
樂也原諸性情之德極夫感通之妙是故天道
本清明也樂聲之清明廉而無疵皦而不雜者
寧不有以象天乎地道本廣大也樂體之廣大
備乎道器貫乎精粗者寧不有以象地乎終於
仲呂之上六始於黃鍾之初九其與春而夏秋
而冬序相肖焉曲直繁瘠之有倫俯仰詘伸之
===
有度其與散而風潤而雨節相似焉聲有五矣
配乎五行之色則各成文而不亂音有八矣配
乎八卦之風則各從律而不姦度有百矣自一
度衍之而至於百則百度豈不各得其數而有
常乎以至樂有小大也宮羽錯雜而小大之相
成樂有終始也律呂調和而終始之相生一唱
一和迭相為經纍纍乎如貫珠或清或濁還相
為主洋洋乎其盈耳夫樂之作如此由是樂教
敷行人心感格將見親疎貴賤之倫因之以清
punctuated: 樂之作也，備法制之詳；樂之數也，極功效之大。甚矣，樂觀其深也！然非備法制之詳，安能致功效之大若是哉？想昔《樂記》之意，謂夫君子之作樂也，原諸性情之德，極夫感通之妙。是故天道本清明也，樂聲之清明，廉而無疵，皦而不雜者，寧不有以象天乎？地道本廣大也，樂體之廣大，備乎道器，貫乎精粗者，寧不有以象地乎？終於仲呂之上六，始於黃鍾之初九，其與春而夏、秋而冬，序相肖焉。曲直繁瘠之有倫，俯仰詘伸之有度，其與散而風、潤而雨，節相似焉。聲有五矣，配乎五行之色，則各成文而不亂。音有八矣，配乎八卦之風，則各從律而不姦。度有百矣，自一度衍之而至於百，則百度豈不各得其數而有常乎？以至樂有小大也，宮羽錯雜而小大之相成；樂有終始也，律呂調和而終始之相生。一唱一和，迭相為經，纍纍乎如貫珠；或清或濁，還相為主，洋洋乎其盈耳。夫樂之作如此，由是樂教敷行，人心感格，將見親疎貴賤之倫因之以清
translation_en:
The creation of music encompasses the full detail of its rules and institutions; its numerical ordering brings its efficacy to the utmost greatness. How profound is the contemplation of music [?]! Yet without completeness in the details of its rules and institutions, how could it achieve effects so great? Reflecting on the meaning of the ancient Record of Music, we may say that the gentleman, in creating music, roots it in the virtue of human nature and feelings and fully realizes the subtle workings of sympathetic response.

Thus, the Way of Heaven is inherently clear and bright. Musical sound is clear and bright, distinct and without blemish, lucid and unmixed: does it not thereby image Heaven? The Way of Earth is inherently broad and great. The constitution of music is broad and great, encompassing both the Way and its concrete embodiments and extending through the refined and the coarse: does it not thereby image Earth? Ending with the topmost six of Zhonglü and beginning with the initial nine of Huangzhong, its sequence resembles the passage from spring to summer and from autumn to winter. Its curved and straight, elaborate and spare movements have their proper order; its bending and rising, contracting and extending have their proper measure. Its rhythms resemble the wind that disperses and the rain that moistens.

There are five notes. Matched with the colors of the Five Phases, each forms a pattern without disorder. There are eight kinds of musical sound. Matched with the winds of the Eight Trigrams, each follows the pitch standards without transgression. There are a hundred measures. When one measure is extended to a hundred, does not each of the hundred acquire its proper numerical value and constancy? Moreover, music has lesser and greater elements: the gong and yu notes interweave, and the lesser and greater complete one another. Music has endings and beginnings: the yang and yin pitch standards harmonize, and endings and beginnings generate one another. One leads and another responds, each in turn providing the guiding thread, linked together like strung pearls. Now high and clear, now low and deep, each in turn takes the lead, abundantly filling the ears.

Such is the creation of music. Through it, musical instruction spreads widely, and human hearts are moved and transformed. We shall then see the relationships between close and distant kin, and between noble and humble, become clear through it…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
明長幼男女之理賴之以宣著姦聲不留亂色
不雜耳目以之聰明也剛氣不怒柔氣不懾血
氣以之和平也君上所化之風移未淳者而復
之淳民下所習之俗易未美者而歸之美暴民
不作諸侯賓服雍雍乎至治之流通兵革不試
五刑不用熙熙乎太和之融液其天下皆寧也
何如哉吁備法制於作樂之初獲功效於樂行
之後君子於樂是豈徒為者耶雖然樂之作有
本有文德者樂之本也器者樂之文也君子反
===
情和志比類成行則樂之本立矣然後發以聲
音飾以羽旄而樂之文備焉噫德性蘊諸中而
數從於外有相乎之實無襲取之弊此功效之
大所以至於移風易俗天下皆寧也歟作樂君
子尚當致察於斯
第貳場
論
王者至大至正
何塘
punctuated:
明，長幼男女之理賴之以宣著。姦聲不留，亂色不雜，耳目以之聰明也；剛氣不怒，柔氣不懾，血氣以之和平也。君上所化之風，移未淳者而復之淳；民下所習之俗，易未美者而歸之美。暴民不作，諸侯賓服，雍雍乎至治之流通；兵革不試，五刑不用，熙熙乎太和之融液。其天下皆寧也，何如哉！吁！備法制於作樂之初，獲功效於樂行之後，君子於樂，是豈徒為者耶？雖然，樂之作有本有文。德者，樂之本也；器者，樂之文也。君子反情和志，比類成行，則樂之本立矣。然後發以聲音，飾以羽旄，而樂之文備焉。噫！德性蘊諸中，而數從於外，有相乎之實，無襲取之弊，此功效之大所以至於移風易俗、天下皆寧也歟！作樂君子，尚當致察於斯。

第貳場

論

王者至大至正

何塘
translation_en:
…made clear, and the principles governing relations between older and younger, men and women, depend upon it to become manifest. Corrupt sounds do not linger, and disorderly sights do not intrude; through this, hearing and sight become acute. Firm dispositions do not turn angry, and yielding dispositions do not become fearful; through this, the vital energies become peaceful and balanced. The prevailing ways shaped by the ruler are transformed from impurity and restored to purity; the customs practiced by the people are changed from what is unworthy and brought to what is good. Violent people do not rise up, and the regional lords submit: harmonious indeed is the unimpeded operation of perfect government! Arms are not put to use, and the five punishments are not employed: joyous indeed is the pervasive influence of supreme harmony! How remarkable it is that all under Heaven should thus enjoy peace!

Ah! To establish the full system of rules when instituting music, and to reap its benefits after music has been put into practice—can the gentleman’s undertaking in music possibly be purposeless? Nevertheless, the making of music has both a foundation and an outward form. Virtue is its foundation; instruments are its outward form. When the gentleman examines his feelings, harmonizes his intentions, and orders things by their kinds into proper ranks, the foundation of music is established. Only then does he express it through sounds and embellish it with feather and yak-tail dance pennons, bringing its outward form to completion. Ah! Virtuous character is stored within, and numerical measures follow without; there is genuine mutual correspondence [?], without the defect of merely borrowing outward forms. Is this not why its great efficacy extends to transforming prevailing ways and customs and bringing peace to all under Heaven? Gentlemen who institute music should give this careful consideration.

Second Session

Discourse

The True King Is Supremely Great and Supremely Upright

He Tang

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導張　批〔論能化陳腐爲高古當非專〕
事舉業者
同考試官學正張　批〔論場多以四時五行日月霜露〕
等語分裂對待千篇一律殊爲可厭此作說理渾淪精到而詞能力去卑弱
可賀可賀
考試官訓導陳　批〔能以古作爲時文而詞不險怪說理〕
又有源委其邃於文者乎
考試官學正逯　批〔此篇說大字正字原於易已自得之文〕
法而通篇皆高古雄偉無一字踏襲況初考通暢稱是將理學詞章俱成者不
===
獻矣
圖科場有子也可
論曰舉天之所以爲天者而全有之於已
王者所以父天天也大天之所以爲天者穆
焉浩浩無所倚著難乎其同哉而覆載之
中乃有一人全其道焉是能繼天之志述
天之事克負荷而不墜者也乾之稱父也
孰不同乎而不克肖焉則不可以爲子丹
朱不可以爲堯之子商均不可以爲舜之
punctuated:
同考試官訓導張批〔論能化陳腐爲高古，當非專〕事舉業者。

同考試官學正張批〔論場多以四時五行日月霜露〕等語分裂對待，千篇一律，殊爲可厭。此作說理渾淪精到，而詞能力去卑弱，可賀，可賀！

考試官訓導陳批〔能以古作爲時文，而詞不險怪，說理〕又有源委，其邃於文者乎！

考試官學正逯批〔此篇說大字正字，原於易，已自得之文〕法，而通篇皆高古雄偉，無一字踏襲。況初考通暢稱是，將理學詞章俱成者不獻矣。圖科場有子也可。

論曰：舉天之所以爲天者，而全有之於已，王者所以父天天也。大天之所以爲天者，穆焉浩浩，無所倚著，難乎其同哉！而覆載之中，乃有一人全其道焉，是能繼天之志、述天之事，克負荷而不墜者也。乾之稱父也，孰不同乎？而不克肖焉，則不可以爲子。丹朱不可以爲堯之子，商均不可以爲舜之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “This discourse transforms the stale and commonplace into something lofty and antique. Its author surely does more than devote himself exclusively to examination composition.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “In the discourse section, candidates commonly take expressions such as the four seasons, the five phases, the sun and moon, and frost and dew, and divide them into contrasting pairs. Thousands of essays follow the same pattern: truly tiresome. This composition expounds its principles comprehensively and precisely, and its language succeeds in avoiding baseness and weakness. Congratulations, congratulations!”

Examiner Chen, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “He can turn ancient writing into contemporary examination prose without making his language strained or bizarre. His exposition of principles also traces their sources and ramifications. Surely he has a profound understanding of writing!”

Examiner Lu, an Instructor, comments: “This essay’s explanation of the words ‘great’ and ‘correct’ derives from the Book of Changes, and he has already developed a method of composition of his own. The entire piece is lofty, antique, powerful, and imposing, without a single word of slavish imitation. Moreover, his first examination composition is fluent and worthy of this one. He looks likely to attain accomplishment in both the learning of principle and literary composition [the concluding wording is garbled: 不獻矣。圖科場有子也可, ?].”

The discourse states: To take everything by which Heaven is Heaven and possess it fully within oneself—this is how the king takes Heaven as his father [?]. That by which great Heaven is Heaven is solemn and boundlessly vast, depending upon nothing: how difficult it is to equal it! Yet within the world that Heaven covers and Earth bears, there is one person who embodies its Way completely. He can carry on Heaven’s intent and continue Heaven’s work, shouldering this responsibility without letting it fall.

As for calling Qian ‘father,’ who does not share this relationship? Yet one who cannot resemble his father cannot count as his son. Danzhu cannot count as Yao’s son; Shangjun cannot count as Shun’s …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
子以其不肖也啓爲禹之子而肖禹武王
爲文王之子而肖文王王者肖天所以爲
天之子也天之所以爲天者何如也大之
至也正之至也聖人之所以爲聖人者何
如也大之至也正之至也大與正一道也
大不出乎正之外止實行於大之中非大
則正者狹矣非正則大者偏矣至則各極
其至而無以復加也道具於天而全付於
聖人之身聖人全受之而惟肖焉譬之父
===
子其幹蠱肖堂者歟聖人者先天而天弗
違後天而奉天時所謂震爲長男所謂大
君者吾父母宗子者也先儒胡仁仲曰王
者至大至正請申之無外之謂大不偏之
謂正易曰大哉乾元天之大也利見大人
聖人之大也剛健中正天之正也龍德正
中聖人之正也臨之大亨以正天之道無
妄之大亨以正天之命而聖人同之也聖
人作易而於天與聖人一則曰大一則曰
punctuated: 子，以其不肖也。啓爲禹之子而肖禹，武王爲文王之子而肖文王。王者肖天，所以爲天之子也。天之所以爲天者何如也？大之至也，正之至也。聖人之所以爲聖人者何如也？大之至也，正之至也。大與正，一道也。大不出乎正之外，止實行於大之中。非大則正者狹矣，非正則大者偏矣。至則各極其至，而無以復加也。道具於天，而全付於聖人之身，聖人全受之而惟肖焉。譬之父子，其幹蠱肖堂者歟？聖人者，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。所謂震爲長男，所謂大君者，吾父母宗子者也。先儒胡仁仲曰：「王者至大至正。」請申之：無外之謂大，不偏之謂正。《易》曰：「大哉乾元！」天之大也。「利見大人」，聖人之大也。「剛健中正」，天之正也。「龍德正中」，聖人之正也。臨之大亨以正，天之道；無妄之大亨以正，天之命，而聖人同之也。聖人作《易》，而於天與聖人，一則曰大，一則曰
translation_en:
…sons, because they did not resemble their fathers in virtue. Qi was Yu’s son and resembled Yu; King Wu was King Wen’s son and resembled King Wen. The king resembles Heaven: this is why he is Heaven’s son. What makes Heaven Heaven? The utmost greatness and the utmost rectitude. What makes the sage a sage? The utmost greatness and the utmost rectitude. Greatness and rectitude constitute a single Way. Greatness does not extend beyond rectitude, and rectitude [?] is put into practice within greatness. Without greatness, rectitude would be narrow; without rectitude, greatness would be partial. At their utmost, each reaches its fullest extent, beyond which nothing can be added. The Way is complete in Heaven and is entrusted in its entirety to the person of the sage. The sage receives it entire and faithfully resembles Heaven. To compare this to father and son, is he not the son who sets his father’s affairs in order and carries on the household’s work [?]?

The sage acts before Heaven, and Heaven does not oppose him; he acts after Heaven and observes Heaven’s seasons. This is what is meant by “Zhen is the eldest son,” and by “the great sovereign is the principal heir of our parents.” The earlier Confucian scholar Hu Renzhong said: “The king possesses the utmost greatness and the utmost rectitude.” Allow me to expand upon this. Having nothing outside oneself is called greatness; inclining to neither side is called rectitude. The Book of Changes says: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian!” This is Heaven’s greatness. “It is beneficial to see the great man”: this is the sage’s greatness. “Firm, vigorous, central, and correct”: this is Heaven’s rectitude. “Dragon virtue, correct and central”: this is the sage’s rectitude. The great success through correctness of the hexagram Lin (Approach) is Heaven’s Way; the great success through correctness of Wuwang (Without Falsehood) is Heaven’s mandate. The sage accords with both. In composing the Book of Changes, the sage spoke of Heaven and the sage, on the one hand calling them great, and on the other calling them…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
正誠以大與正盡乎天與聖人之道而況
於至者乎天與聖人一體也天之於聖人
也其用意亦勤矣形之以其氣性之以其
理自其蒼蒼冥冥而保佑之申命之誘其
衷而聖之六龍以御之九重以居之皇極
以建之百官萬民以下之萬幾以憂之為
之去其害而安之出告以仁愛之昌其運
以久之凡父之所以為其子謀者天皆施
之於王者焉天之於王者其用意亦勤矣
===
王者何以得此於天哉惟克肖之耳天與
王者一氣之流通也親不異於父子勢不
殊於一家使王者之所存所行而一不合
乎天則獲罪於天矣天其子之乎孟子曰
不順乎親不可以為子曾子曰為人子止
於孝然則為天之子者其所以順焉而止
其所者果何如哉天有是道而王者亦有
焉則父子一道矣是故乾道變化各正性
命此天道之所以至大而無不正也王者
punctuated: 正，誠以大與正盡乎天與聖人之道，而況於至者乎？天與聖人一體也。天之於聖人也，其用意亦勤矣。形之以其氣，性之以其理，自其蒼蒼冥冥而保佑之、申命之，誘其衷而聖之，六龍以御之，九重以居之，皇極以建之，百官萬民以下之，萬幾以憂之，為之去其害而安之，出告以仁愛之，昌其運以久之。凡父之所以為其子謀者，天皆施之於王者焉。天之於王者，其用意亦勤矣。王者何以得此於天哉？惟克肖之耳。天與王者，一氣之流通也，親不異於父子，勢不殊於一家。使王者之所存所行而一不合乎天，則獲罪於天矣，天其子之乎？孟子曰：「不順乎親，不可以為子。」曾子曰：「為人子，止於孝。」然則為天之子者，其所以順焉而止其所者，果何如哉？天有是道，而王者亦有焉，則父子一道矣。是故乾道變化，各正性命，此天道之所以至大而無不正也。王者
translation_en: …“correct”—truly because greatness and correctness encompass the Way of Heaven and the sage. How much more so when these qualities reach their utmost! Heaven and the sage form one body. Heaven’s care for the sage is indeed assiduous. It gives him form through its vital energy and nature through its principle. From its azure heights and hidden depths, it protects him and repeatedly charges him with its mandate; it guides his inner heart and makes him a sage. It gives him the six dragons to ride, the ninefold palace to inhabit, and the August Ultimate to establish. It places the hundred officials and myriad people beneath him, and burdens him with concern for the myriad affairs of government. It removes dangers for him and brings him security; it issues admonitions to show him benevolent love, and makes his fortunes flourish so that they endure. Everything a father does to plan for his son, Heaven does for the king. Heaven’s care for the king is indeed assiduous. How does the king obtain all this from Heaven? Only by being able to resemble it. Heaven and the king are linked by the circulation of a single vital energy. Their intimacy is no different from that of father and son; their relationship is no different from that within a single family. If anything in the king’s intentions or conduct fails to accord with Heaven, he incurs guilt before Heaven. Would Heaven then regard him as its son? Mengzi said: “One who does not act in accord with his parents cannot be a son.” Zengzi said: “As a son, one rests in filial devotion.” How, then, should one who is Heaven’s son act in accord with it and rest in his proper place? Heaven possesses this Way, and the king possesses it too: thus father and son share a single Way. Hence, “The Way of Qian changes and transforms, and each thing receives its proper nature and destiny.” This is why Heaven’s Way is supremely great, with nothing in it that is not correct. The king…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之首出庶物萬國咸寧者以之於穆不已
繼善成性此天道之所以至大而無不正
也王者之富有日新裁成輔相者以之天
下為度萬物皆我即天之無不覆幬體物
不遺者也不偏不黨王道平平即天之栽
培傾覆虧盈益謙者也帝德廣運與上帝
降衷者同一致表正萬邦與並育並行者
同一揆今夫天之於物也鼓之以雷霆潤
之以風雨日月運行一寒一暑而天下之
===
物形者自形色者自色榮悴者自榮悴中
國自中國四夷自四夷也天何嘗限之以
遠近偏之以彼此哉一至大至正之道耳
王者奉行天道擴一心之大以包天下之
大操一心之正以正天下之不正井田以
養之學校以教之綏之動之予之奪之刑
之賞之宮中府中俱為一體王國邦國各
施其道而天下之衣者衣食者食枉者直
邪者正善者勸惡者懼中國以治四夷以
punctuated:
之首出庶物、萬國咸寧者，以之。於穆不已，繼善成性，此天道之所以至大而無不正也；王者之富有日新、裁成輔相者，以之。天下為度，萬物皆我，即天之無不覆幬、體物不遺者也。不偏不黨，王道平平，即天之栽培傾覆、虧盈益謙者也。帝德廣運，與上帝降衷者同一致；表正萬邦，與並育並行者同一揆。

今夫天之於物也，鼓之以雷霆，潤之以風雨，日月運行，一寒一暑，而天下之物，形者自形，色者自色，榮悴者自榮悴，中國自中國，四夷自四夷也。天何嘗限之以遠近、偏之以彼此哉？一至大至正之道耳。王者奉行天道，擴一心之大以包天下之大，操一心之正以正天下之不正。井田以養之，學校以教之，綏之，動之，予之，奪之，刑之，賞之。宮中府中，俱為一體；王國邦國，各施其道。而天下之衣者衣，食者食，枉者直，邪者正，善者勸，惡者懼，中國以治，四夷以
translation_en:
…it is through this that the true king stands foremost among all beings and the myriad states enjoy peace. Profound and unceasing, continuing in goodness and bringing nature to completion: this is why the Way of Heaven is supremely great and nowhere fails to be correct. It is through this that the true king possesses all in abundance, renews himself daily, and shapes and assists the processes of transformation. Taking all under Heaven as his measure and regarding the myriad things as himself accords with Heaven’s sheltering everything and embodying itself in all things without omission. Without partiality or faction, the kingly Way is level and even: this accords with Heaven’s nurturing what stands upright and overthrowing what leans, diminishing the full and augmenting the humble. The sovereign’s virtue, broad and far-reaching, has the same purport as the Supreme Lord’s bestowal of the moral mean upon humanity; setting an upright example for the myriad states follows the same standard as all things growing together and all courses proceeding together without conflict.

Now, in its dealings with things, Heaven rouses them with thunder and lightning and moistens them with wind and rain. The sun and moon revolve; cold and heat alternate. Thus, among all things under Heaven, those that take form do so of themselves; those that assume color do so of themselves; those that flourish or wither do so of themselves. The Central States are themselves, and the peoples of the four quarters are themselves. When has Heaven ever set limits according to distance, or shown partiality toward one rather than another? There is only the one supremely great and supremely correct Way. The true king carries out the Way of Heaven, extending the greatness of his own heart to embrace the vastness of all under Heaven, and holding fast to its rectitude to correct whatever is not upright in the world. He sustains the people through the well-field system and teaches them through schools; he settles them and sets them in motion, gives to them and takes from them, punishes them and rewards them. The palace and the government offices form a single body; in the royal domain and the various states, he applies the appropriate Way to each. Thus, throughout the world, those who need clothing are clothed, those who need food are fed, the crooked are made straight, the wayward are corrected, the good are encouraged, and the wicked are made fearful. Thereby the Central States are brought to order, and the peoples of the four quarters …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
服也王者何嘗施彼而遺此擇其一而慳
其二哉一至大至正之道耳大之所以為
大者皆中正仁義之理正之所以為正者
皆光大高明之事大之外別無大極其大
之至矣正之外別無正極其正之至矣天
得是而為父王者得是而為子至是而王
者與天為一矣至是而王者之盛德大業
無以復加矣然天之道天自有之而無假
於外王者之道得之於天而措之德業之
===
盛不可以不保之也故伊尹以惟天無親
克敬惟親戒太甲傳說以惟天聰明惟聖
時憲戒高宗夫二君者皆至大至正者也
而伊尹傳說猶拳拳焉豈非欲其保天命
於悠久哉人君一心攻之者衆苟不知所
以持之則其所已能者或有所移易而況
能至乎敬焉憲焉持之之方也敬則不敢
怠違憲則不敢褻慢察之日用之間防之
隱微之際勿褊狹以小之勿邪詖以頗之
punctuated:
服也。王者何嘗施彼而遺此，擇其一而慳其二哉？一至大至正之道耳。大之所以為大者，皆中正仁義之理；正之所以為正者，皆光大高明之事。大之外別無大，極其大之至矣；正之外別無正，極其正之至矣。天得是而為父，王者得是而為子。至是而王者與天為一矣，至是而王者之盛德大業無以復加矣。然天之道，天自有之而無假於外；王者之道，得之於天而措之。德業之盛，不可以不保之也。
故伊尹以「惟天無親，克敬惟親」戒太甲，傳說以「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲」戒高宗。夫二君者，皆至大至正者也，而伊尹、傳說猶拳拳焉，豈非欲其保天命於悠久哉？人君一心，攻之者衆，苟不知所以持之，則其所已能者或有所移易，而況能至乎？敬焉，憲焉，持之之方也。敬則不敢怠違，憲則不敢褻慢。察之日用之間，防之隱微之際。勿褊狹以小之，勿邪詖以頗之。
translation_en:
…submit. When has a true king ever bestowed his care on those while neglecting these, chosen to favor one while begrudging another? There is only the Way of utmost greatness and utmost rectitude. What makes greatness great consists entirely of the principles of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness; what makes rectitude upright consists entirely of deeds that are expansive, luminous, lofty, and discerning. Beyond this greatness there is no other greatness: it reaches the very utmost of greatness. Beyond this rectitude there is no other rectitude: it reaches the very utmost of rectitude. Heaven possesses this and thereby becomes the father; the king possesses this and thereby becomes the son. At this point the king and Heaven become one. At this point nothing can further augment the king’s flourishing virtue and great achievements. Yet Heaven’s Way is inherently its own and depends on nothing external; the king’s Way is received from Heaven and put into practice. The flourishing of his virtue and achievements must therefore be preserved.
Thus Yi Yin admonished Tai Jia with the words, “Heaven has no favorites; it favors only those capable of reverence.” Fu Yue admonished Gaozong with the words, “Heaven is keen of hearing and clear of sight; the sage takes this as his model.” Both these rulers possessed utmost greatness and utmost rectitude, yet Yi Yin and Fu Yue remained earnestly solicitous. Was this not because they wished them to preserve Heaven’s mandate for all time? The ruler has but one heart, and many things assail it. If he does not know how to maintain it, even the capacities he already possesses may change or be lost; how much less can he reach the utmost? Reverence and taking Heaven as his model are the means of maintaining it. Through reverence he dares not be negligent or disobedient; through taking Heaven as his model he dares not be disrespectful or heedless. He must examine his heart amid daily activities and guard it where its workings are hidden and subtle. Do not diminish it through narrow-mindedness; do not skew it through perversity and bias…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
勿聲色貨利遊畋以伐之勿土木以荒之
勿優柔不斷以弱之勿異端以惑之勿溺
於私昵嬖幸以敗之勿智術以欺之勿昏
昏以淆之勿察察以苛之而凡行於家施
於邦國天下者久如是暫如是中心無爲
以守之則天之所以子之者亦鑒厥恒久
將子孫萬世無窮矣雖然用功之方亦有
其要焉曰格物曰致知曰誠意正心是爲
論
===
表
擬宋加韓琦尚書右僕射謝表〔治平元年〕
何瑭
同考試官訓導張　批〔富麗可取〕
同考試官學正張　批〔表佳〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔表得體〕
考試官學正逯　批〔其詞麗而能括當時事不覺其煩〕
臣
臣琦伏承
聖恩加臣尚書右僕射稱謝者臣琦誠惶誠恐
punctuated:
勿聲色貨利遊畋以伐之，勿土木以荒之，勿優柔不斷以弱之，勿異端以惑之，勿溺於私昵嬖幸以敗之，勿智術以欺之，勿昏昏以淆之，勿察察以苛之。而凡行於家、施於邦國天下者，久如是，暫如是，中心無爲以守之，則天之所以子之者，亦鑒厥恒久，將子孫萬世無窮矣。雖然，用功之方亦有其要焉：曰格物，曰致知，曰誠意正心。是爲論。
表
擬宋加韓琦尚書右僕射謝表〔治平元年〕
何瑭
同考試官訓導張批〔富麗可取〕
同考試官學正張批〔表佳〕
考試官訓導陳批〔表得體〕
考試官學正逯批〔其詞麗而能括當時事不覺其煩〕
臣，臣琦伏承聖恩，加臣尚書右僕射，稱謝者。臣琦誠惶誠恐
translation_en:
…Do not let sensual pleasures, wealth and profit, excursions and hunting injure it; do not let building projects lay it waste; do not let indecision weaken it; do not let heterodox teachings confuse it; do not let indulgence in private intimates and favored courtiers ruin it; do not let clever stratagems deceive it; do not let muddleheadedness cloud it; and do not let excessive scrutiny make it harsh. In everything practiced within the family and extended to the state and all under Heaven, remain thus over long periods and brief moments alike, preserving it inwardly without contrived action. Then Heaven, which regards the ruler as its son, will also perceive his constancy, and his descendants will continue without end for ten thousand generations. Nevertheless, there are also essentials to the methods of applying oneself: investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind. This concludes the discourse.
Memorial
A Memorial of Thanks Composed in the Voice of Han Qi of the Song upon His Appointment as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs 〔First year of Zhiping [1064]〕
He Tang
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Rich and elegant; worthy of acceptance.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔A fine memorial.〕
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The memorial is appropriate to its form.〕

Your servant [?]—Your servant Qi has humbly received your sagely favor, appointing me Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and submits this expression of thanks. Your servant Qi, in profound trepidation and fear…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
稽首頓首上言伏以峻秩崇階匪才德而
焉授
特恩異典何衰薄之遽加虛濫叵居滿盈合懼
茲蓋伏遇
○○○○
鳳姿日耀
龍德淵潛
上帝篤生默定神人之主
先皇簡在入符中外之心恢纘
===
洪休光胥
駿命南向而讓西向而讓
盛節高於漢文見堯於牆見堯於羹
大孝齊乎虞舜昔緝熙之正始欲亮陰以無言
道合上玄
德超邃古臣民仰戴
天地維持初
運啓握符巳卜無疆之壽乃疾稱勿藥果從有
喜之祥
punctuated:
稽首頓首上言：伏以峻秩崇階，匪才德而焉授？特恩異典，何衰薄之遽加？虛濫叵居，滿盈合懼。
茲蓋伏遇○○○○，鳳姿日耀，龍德淵潛。上帝篤生，默定神人之主；先皇簡在，入符中外之心。恢纘洪休，光胥駿命。南向而讓，西向而讓，盛節高於漢文；見堯於牆，見堯於羹，大孝齊乎虞舜。昔緝熙之正始，欲亮陰以無言。道合上玄，德超邃古。臣民仰戴，天地維持。初運啓握符，巳卜無疆之壽；乃疾稱勿藥，果從有喜之祥。
translation_en:
…I bow my head to the ground and repeatedly kowtow, submitting these words: I humbly consider that lofty rank and exalted station should be conferred only upon those possessed of ability and virtue. Why, then, have exceptional favor and extraordinary honors suddenly been bestowed upon one so decrepit and unworthy? I cannot occupy this post under false pretenses and without qualification; such overflowing good fortune rightly inspires fear.
This is surely because I have humbly encountered ○○○○ [honorific text unclear], whose phoenix-like bearing shines like the sun and whose dragon-like virtue lies hidden in the depths. The Lord on High brought you into being with abundant favor, silently appointing you sovereign over spirits and men. The late emperor chose you in his heart, and your accession accorded with the wishes of those within and beyond the court. You carried forward his vast blessings and gloriously upheld the great mandate. Facing south, you declined; facing west, you declined: your sublime integrity surpassed that of Emperor Wen of Han. You saw Yao upon the wall and saw Yao in your broth: your great filial devotion equaled that of Shun of Yu. At the very beginning of your illustrious rule, you wished to remain silent in mourning. Your Way accorded with highest Heaven; your virtue surpassed remote antiquity. Your servants and people looked up to you with reverence, and Heaven and Earth sustained you. When your reign began and you took up the token of sovereign authority, a boundless lifespan was already foretold. Then, when illness came, it was pronounced one requiring no medicine; indeed, the auspicious promise of joy was fulfilled.

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
孝感神明
誠孚上下
慈闈知可付託大政遂以歸還聽斷萬幾儀刑
百辟代玄功而造物協神化以開祥九譯
承風八紘受朔方登才良而黜偷惰仍念
故舊而奬老成顧尚書北斗之司官尊省
閣而右弼上台之秩職專平章鼎鉉望高
調陰陽而贊化巖廊地密本政事以經邦
宜畀德以優賢亦循名而責實伏念臣百
===
年遭際一介迂凡歷翰苑軍州職無補於
毫末在封疆郡府才每愧於駑駘北虜司
虞未能奠枕西戎稽討無為軫心荷
先皇以愚直
賜知密勿踰於五稔蒙
陛下以勤勞過
念
寵遇首於羣僚每慚應辨非崇敢謂重厚同勃
中台獨晦共看宿緯之光
punctuated:
孝感神明，誠孚上下。慈闈知可付託，大政遂以歸還。聽斷萬幾，儀刑百辟；代玄功而造物，協神化以開祥。九譯承風，八紘受朔。方登才良而黜偷惰，仍念故舊而奬老成。顧尚書北斗之司，官尊省閣；而右弼上台之秩，職專平章。鼎鉉望高，調陰陽而贊化；巖廊地密，本政事以經邦。宜畀德以優賢，亦循名而責實。
伏念臣百年遭際，一介迂凡。歷翰苑軍州，職無補於毫末；在封疆郡府，才每愧於駑駘。北虜司虞，未能奠枕；西戎稽討，無為軫心。荷先皇以愚直賜知，密勿踰於五稔；蒙陛下以勤勞過念，寵遇首於羣僚。每慚應辨非崇，敢謂重厚同勃？中台獨晦，共看宿緯之光。
translation_en:
…Your filial devotion moved the spirits, and your sincerity won the trust of high and low. The Empress Dowager knew that you could be entrusted with responsibility, and so returned the great affairs of government to you. You hear and decide the myriad affairs of state and serve as a model for all officials. You carry out Heaven’s mysterious work in nurturing creation and accord with its spiritual transformations to usher in auspicious signs. Peoples requiring nine successive interpreters receive your civilizing influence; the eight reaches of the world accept your calendar. Even as you promote the talented and worthy and dismiss the negligent and idle, you remember old servants and reward mature experience.
Consider the office of Minister, likened to the Northern Dipper: its standing is exalted among the departments and halls of government. The rank of the assisting minister, corresponding to the upper celestial terrace, carries particular responsibility for deliberating on government. Lofty is the prestige of those who bear the state’s tripod: they harmonize yin and yang and assist the work of transformation. Intimate is their position in the palace halls: they take governmental affairs as the foundation for ordering the realm. It is fitting to entrust office to the virtuous and favor the worthy, while also requiring actual performance commensurate with their titles.
I humbly reflect that, despite the opportunities afforded me in this lifetime, I am but one impractical, ordinary man. I have served in the Hanlin Academy and in military and local administrations, yet my service has contributed not the slightest benefit. In frontier territories and prefectural offices, my abilities have constantly left me ashamed, like an inferior horse. In watching against danger from the northern tribes [?], I could not secure untroubled repose; in the delayed campaigns against the western Rong, I accomplished nothing to relieve imperial concern [?]. The late emperor graciously recognized my simple honesty, and I served diligently in confidential affairs for more than five years. Your Majesty has shown excessive regard for my toil, bestowing favor upon me above all my colleagues. I am ever ashamed that my readiness in responding is no match for Chong’s [?]; dare I claim that my gravity and integrity equal those of Bo? Alone, my star in the central celestial terrace is dim, while all behold the radiance of the other stars…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
元首自明何賴股肱之力惟鈞石之難任將骸
骨之乞歸豈謂
恩私重加敘進舊班不改
新命愈尊伏
彤廷而懇辭自
紫霄以申錫戰競以次誶受皇駭將覆餗之是
憂何匪服而不欿臣敢不委拚殘喘策勵
初心益殫犬馬之勞用答
乾坤之造伏望
===
孝心純篤
聖母以安
九廟之靈仁澤敷流洽民物以衍萬年之慶臣
下情無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated:
元首自明，何賴股肱之力？惟鈞石之難任，將骸骨之乞歸。豈謂恩私重加，敘進舊班不改，新命愈尊。伏彤廷而懇辭，自紫霄以申錫。戰競以次誶受，皇駭將覆餗之是憂，何匪服而不欿。臣敢不委拚殘喘，策勵初心，益殫犬馬之勞，用答乾坤之造。
伏望孝心純篤聖母，以安九廟之靈；仁澤敷流洽民物，以衍萬年之慶。臣下情無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…The sovereign is himself enlightened: what need has he of the strength of his ministers, his limbs? Knowing how difficult it is to bear this weighty charge, I was about to beg leave to retire. How could I have expected your personal favor to be bestowed anew, advancing me without altering my former standing, and granting a new appointment still more exalted? Prostrate in the vermilion court, I earnestly declined; from the purple heavens, the grant was renewed. Trembling, I received it in due order [?]; terrified, I fear overturning the cauldron’s food—that is, failing in my charge. How could I accept honors beyond my fitness without misgiving? Dare I, your servant, fail to devote the breath remaining to me, spur myself to fulfill my original resolve, and exhaust still further my humble efforts as a dog or horse, to repay the nurturing bounty of Heaven and Earth?
I humbly hope that Your Majesty’s filial devotion toward the Sagely Mother will be pure and profound, bringing peace to the spirits of the nine ancestral temples; and that your benevolent bounty will spread to all the people and living things, extending the blessings of your reign for ten thousand years. Looking up to Heaven and reverently toward Your Sagely Majesty, I cannot contain my deeply stirred feelings and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第叁場
策〔五道〕
第一問
同考試官訓導張　批〔有考據有歸宿是能服膺〕
聖訓而企仰先正者
同考試官學正張　批〔詞贍而徤當是策手〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔識出〕
聖祖懲胡元以吏為治之弊而警飭士子以勤自勉以惰自戒以古人自矜式意思明盡是能
===
服膺
聖訓者允宜録出
考試官學正逯　批〔第一款答問能簡徤其語而歸宿於崇勤戒惰浮惰將非事虛文者况五策皆稱而初場二場亦通宜〕
宜首多士
對克艱厥臣虞廷陳謨敬爾在公周家鳌
成古先哲王知為臣之道在於勤故所以
陳於廷與所以戒其臣下者一惟艱難敬
慎云耳夫艱與敬勤之謂也惰之反也我
punctuated:
第叁場
策〔五道〕
第一問
同考試官訓導張批〔有考據，有歸宿，是能服膺〕聖訓而企仰先正者。
同考試官學正張批〔詞贍而徤，當是策手。〕
考試官訓導陳批〔識出〕聖祖懲胡元以吏為治之弊，而警飭士子以勤自勉，以惰自戒，以古人自矜式，意思明盡，是能服膺聖訓者，允宜録出。
考試官學正逯批〔第一款答問，能簡徤其語，而歸宿於崇勤戒惰。浮惰，將非事虛文者？况五策皆稱，而初場二場亦通，宜〕宜首多士。
對：克艱厥臣，虞廷陳謨；敬爾在公，周家鳌成。古先哲王知為臣之道在於勤，故所以陳於廷與所以戒其臣下者，一惟艱難敬慎云耳。夫艱與敬，勤之謂也，惰之反也。我
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays (five questions)
First Question

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “There is supporting evidence and a definite conclusion. This is someone who takes the Sacred Instructions to heart and looks up to the worthy predecessors.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The language is ample and vigorous; surely an accomplished writer of policy essays.”

The Sacred Progenitor took warning from the abuses of government through clerks under the non-Chinese Yuan dynasty and admonished scholars to encourage themselves through diligence, guard themselves against indolence, and take the ancients as their models. The meaning is clear and fully expressed. This is someone who takes the Sacred Instructions to heart, and the essay certainly deserves selection for inclusion.”

Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “In answering the first question, he makes his language concise and vigorous, concluding with the promotion of diligence and the rejection of indolence. Frivolity and indolence—would these not amount to attending to empty formalities [?]? Moreover, all five policy essays are fitting, and his work in the first and second sessions is also sound. He should—” He should be placed first among the candidates.

The sage kings of antiquity knew that the way of serving as a minister lay in diligence.
