title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝勉羣臣以親理職事而戒其袖手
高坐者其諸克艱敬爾之謂歟請詳言之
昔我
聖祖以天縱不世之資乘胡元瀆濁之餘握乾
符而起淮甸揮江漢以洗腥羶天下既定
法制既立猶謂臣民之或慢于法也乃制
大誥三編以昭示之使知所趨避
聖訓流布家傳人誦
聖子神孫率由靡愆愚也幸生
===
聖世沐
聖化嘗伏讀
官親起稿一章有曰自周至于漢晋唐宋當
時賢人君子受任方隅所任之事必躬親理
之胡元制治一章有曰臨政之時袖手高坐
謀由吏出縱是文章之士不異胡人愚於是
有以知
聖祖之意蓋深懲胡元以吏為源之弊而警飭
臣工以勤自勵以惰自戒以古之賢人君
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝勉羣臣以親理職事，而戒其袖手高坐者，其諸克艱敬爾之謂歟？請詳言之。昔我聖祖以天縱不世之資，乘胡元瀆濁之餘，握乾符而起淮甸，揮江漢以洗腥羶。天下既定，法制既立，猶謂臣民之或慢于法也，乃制《大誥》三編以昭示之，使知所趨避。聖訓流布，家傳人誦，聖子神孫率由靡愆。愚也幸生聖世，沐聖化，嘗伏讀《官親起稿》一章，有曰：「自周至于漢晋唐宋，當時賢人君子受任方隅，所任之事必躬親理之。」《胡元制治》一章，有曰：「臨政之時，袖手高坐，謀由吏出，縱是文章之士，不異胡人。」愚於是有以知聖祖之意，蓋深懲胡元以吏為源之弊，而警飭臣工，以勤自勵，以惰自戒，以古之賢人君
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, urged his assembled ministers to attend personally to their official duties and warned them against sitting aloof with their hands tucked in their sleeves. Was this not precisely the meaning of “meeting the difficulties” and “be reverent”? Allow me to explain in detail.

Formerly, our sagely founder, endowed by Heaven with talents unmatched in his age, arose in the Huai region bearing Heaven’s mandate amid the lingering corruption of the barbarian Yuan. He wielded the waters of the Yangzi and Han to wash away their rank and fetid taint. Once the realm was settled and laws and institutions established, he still considered that officials and commoners might treat the law lightly. He therefore composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) to instruct them clearly, so that they would know what to pursue and what to avoid. These sagely instructions circulated widely: households transmitted them and individuals recited them. His sagely sons and divine grandsons followed them without transgression.

Fortunate to have been born in this sagely age and to have received its transforming influence, I have reverently read the chapter “Officials Personally Draft Documents.” It says: “From the Zhou through the Han, Jin, Tang, and Song, the worthy men and gentlemen of those times who received appointments in the regions invariably attended personally to the affairs entrusted to them.” The chapter “The Governance of the Barbarian Yuan” says: “When administering affairs, they sat aloof with their hands tucked in their sleeves, leaving the devising of plans to clerks. Even men of literary accomplishment were no different from the barbarians.” From this I have come to understand the intention of our sagely founder. Taking deeply to heart the abuses of the barbarian Yuan, which made clerks the source of authority [?], he admonished his officials to spur themselves on through diligence, guard against indolence, and take as their models the worthy men and gentle…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
子自矜式也夫歷代方隅之臣多矣實六
經考諸史姑舉一二焉以周言之王事靡
盬朝夕從事有北山之大夫賦政于外夙
夜匪懈有城齊之山甫以漢言之賢否盡
知各有記籍東海尹翁歸其人也精力推
行不辭米鹽潁川黃霸其人也陶侃之在
荊州惜分陰而總攝庶務劉弘之在荊襄勤
勸課而絕縱衡是在晉方隅之臣乎政尚
清毅文不敢犯廣州都督有宋璟焉數陳
===
剖判下筆如流忠州別駕有陸贄焉非在
唐方隅之臣乎若濂溪之在廣州洗雪冤
滯不憚瘴癘韓忠獻之在相州簿書文檄
檢察必親此則宋之賢人君子任方隅之
責者也噫綜核名實漢道以興清虛相尚
晉轍不洛此我
聖祖之訓所以諄諄切切勉羣臣以躬親職務
而戒其袖手若尸也昔阮孚謂卞壼曰君
常無閑泰如含瓦石不亦勞乎壼曰諸公
punctuated: 子自矜式也。夫歷代方隅之臣多矣，實六經，考諸史，姑舉一二焉。以周言之，王事靡盬，朝夕從事，有北山之大夫；賦政于外，夙夜匪懈，有城齊之山甫。以漢言之，賢否盡知，各有記籍，東海尹翁歸其人也；精力推行，不辭米鹽，潁川黃霸其人也。陶侃之在荊州，惜分陰而總攝庶務；劉弘之在荊襄，勤勸課而絕縱衡，是在晉方隅之臣乎？政尚清毅，文不敢犯，廣州都督有宋璟焉；數陳剖判，下筆如流，忠州別駕有陸贄焉。非在唐方隅之臣乎？若濂溪之在廣州，洗雪冤滯，不憚瘴癘；韓忠獻之在相州，簿書文檄，檢察必親，此則宋之賢人君子任方隅之責者也。噫！綜核名實，漢道以興；清虛相尚，晉轍不洛。此我聖祖之訓所以諄諄切切勉羣臣以躬親職務，而戒其袖手若尸也。昔阮孚謂卞壼曰：「君常無閑泰，如含瓦石，不亦勞乎？」壼曰：「諸公
translation_en:
…gentlemen of antiquity as their own models. There have been many officials entrusted with regional responsibilities throughout the dynasties. Consulting the Six Classics [?] and examining the histories, let us cite just a few. In the Zhou, there was the officer in “Northern Mountain,” who attended to the king’s unceasing business morning and evening; and there was Shanfu, who fortified Qi [?], administering government abroad and remaining diligent day and night. In the Han, Yin Wenggui of Donghai knew fully which men were worthy and which were not, keeping records of each. Huang Ba of Yingchuan energetically carried out his duties, not shrinking even from the minutiae of rice and salt. When Tao Kan was in Jingzhou, he treasured every fraction of an hour and supervised all affairs. When Liu Hong was in the Jingzhou and Xiangyang region, he diligently encouraged and assessed performance and put an end to political maneuvering. Were these not regional officials of the Jin? Song Jing, Area Commander of Guangzhou, prized integrity and firmness in government, so that civil officials dared not transgress [?]. Lu Zhi, Aide in Zhongzhou, analyzed and adjudicated numerous submissions [?], his writing flowing freely. Were these not regional officials of the Tang? As for Lianxi in Guangzhou, he redressed injustices and long-unresolved cases, undeterred by pestilential miasmas. Han Zhongxian in Xiangzhou invariably inspected registers, documents, and official dispatches personally. These were worthy gentlemen of the Song who bore responsibility for regional administration.

Alas! By comprehensively checking names against actual performance, the Han's governance flourished; through mutual admiration for purity and vacuity, the Jin's course went awry [?]. This is why the instructions of our Sagely Progenitor so earnestly and insistently urge all officials to attend personally to their duties, warning them against sitting with folded hands like ceremonial personators of the dead. Once Ruan Fu said to Bian Kun: “You are never at ease, as though you held tiles and stones in your mouth. Is that not exhausting?” Kun replied: “You gentlemen …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
道德恢弘風流相尚執鄙吝者非我而何
歐陽脩曰文章可以潤身政事可以及物
蓋晉是時方以清談為高以勤政務為俗
吏壼深嫉其壞天下脩以文章名當世而
尤勤於吏事不欲以彼妨此故其言如是
觀數子之所行究二子之所言皆尚勤實
戒浮惰者也考諸
聖製可以不謬傳之今日宜為法則若夫近來
之弊誠有如明問所以落之獎之
之機則在上而不在下愚何敢言
===
第二問
同考試官訓導張　批〔策能欵答而要其歸於弗也〕
張伊
非外重而內輕者錄之以為訓
同考試官學正張　批〔題欲觀士子趨向若是作庶幾〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔策能言其志當是學者〕
考試官學正逯　批〔說學者自有一等至到去處非科〕
舉資格所能奪甚明白而考據不差文彩爛然必通古今而能不失
punctuated:
道德恢弘，風流相尚，執鄙吝者，非我而何？」歐陽脩曰：「文章可以潤身，政事可以及物。」蓋晉是時，方以清談為高，以勤政務為俗吏，壼深嫉其壞天下；脩以文章名當世，而尤勤於吏事，不欲以彼妨此，故其言如是。觀數子之所行，究二子之所言，皆尚勤實、戒浮惰者也。考諸聖製，可以不謬；傳之今日，宜為法則。若夫近來之弊，誠有如明問，所以落之、獎之之機，則在上而不在下，愚何敢言？

第二問

同考試官訓導張，批〔策能欵答，而要其歸於弗也〕

張伊

非外重而內輕者，錄之以為訓。

同考試官學正張，批〔題欲觀士子趨向，若是作，庶幾〕

考試官訓導陳，批〔策能言其志，當是學者〕

考試官學正逯，批〔說學者自有一等至到去處，非科〕舉資格所能奪，甚明白，而考據不差，文彩爛然，必通古今而能不失
translation_en:
…“You gentlemen are expansive in virtue and esteem one another’s cultivated elegance; who but I, then, should cling to narrow-mindedness?” Ouyang Xiu said: “Literary composition can adorn oneself; government service can benefit others.” At that time under the Jin, pure conversation was esteemed as lofty, while those diligent in government business were regarded as vulgar officials. Bian Kun deeply resented its ruinous effects on the realm. Xiu was renowned in his day for literary composition, yet was especially diligent in administrative affairs, unwilling to let the former interfere with the latter. Hence their statements. If we examine the conduct of the several men discussed and probe the words of these two, all prized diligence and practical accomplishment and warned against frivolity and indolence. Tested against the imperial composition, these principles cannot be mistaken; transmitted to the present, they should serve as a standard. As for recent abuses, they are indeed as your discerning question describes. The power to dismiss or reward rests with those above, not those below. How would I, in my ignorance, dare to speak?

Second Question

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The policy essay answers sincerely, but its essential conclusion lies in “not” [?].〕

Zhang Yi

He is not one who gives weight to externals while slighting what is within. This is selected to serve as an instructive example. [The placement of this passage in relation to the preceding comment is uncertain.]

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The question seeks to discern the candidates’ inclinations. A composition such as this comes close to the ideal.〕

Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The policy essay can express his aspirations; he must be a man devoted to learning.〕

Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔It explains that those devoted to learning have a particular ultimate attainment of their own, which the qualifications conferred by the civil-service〕 examinations cannot take away. This is very clear; its evidential references are accurate, and its literary brilliance shines forth. He must be conversant with antiquity and the present and able not to lose …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
其所守者取之
對至重者道也至輕者勢也夫道有所極
至知其所在而求其止焉則道重而勢輕
矣是故君子弗勢也請因明問而陳其道
之所以重勢之所以輕可乎出於天者道
也制於人者勢也上必求賢以致其理士
必求進以致其用天理之所在也故曰其
為道一也法立而時為之低昂道在而人
為之二三時政之所制也故曰其為勢一
===
也夫科舉資格所以羅籠奔走天下之人
才者至矣使上古聖王復生不能外是以
取士使上古賢臣復生不能外是以進身
其為法不可易也然楊龜山曰古人得已
似不如此謂科舉使人輕於進也司馬光
曰爵祿品秩一一稱滿其意將無以役使
羣臣謂當時資格之不守也不究理致而
惟程式是拘不思國體而惟人情是徇風
行於上而成於下道二於此而原於彼於
punctuated:
其所守者，取之。

對：至重者，道也；至輕者，勢也。夫道有所極至，知其所在而求其止焉，則道重而勢輕矣。是故君子弗勢也。請因明問而陳其道之所以重、勢之所以輕，可乎？出於天者，道也；制於人者，勢也。上必求賢以致其理，士必求進以致其用，天理之所在也，故曰其為道一也。法立而時為之低昂，道在而人為之二三，時政之所制也，故曰其為勢一也。夫科舉資格，所以羅籠奔走天下之人才者至矣。使上古聖王復生，不能外是以取士；使上古賢臣復生，不能外是以進身。其為法不可易也。然楊龜山曰：「古人得已，似不如此。」謂科舉使人輕於進也。司馬光曰：「爵祿品秩，一一稱滿其意，將無以役使羣臣。」謂當時資格之不守也。不究理致而惟程式是拘，不思國體而惟人情是徇，風行於上而成於下，道二於此而原於彼，於
translation_en:
…one who holds fast to his principles. Select him.

In reply: What carries the greatest weight is the Way; what carries the least is circumstance. The Way has an ultimate point of perfection. If one knows where it lies and seeks to abide there, the Way will carry weight and circumstance will count for little. Thus the gentleman does not yield to circumstance [?]. May I take your illuminating question as the occasion to explain why the Way carries weight and circumstance counts for little?

What issues from Heaven is the Way; what is controlled by men is circumstance. Those above must seek worthy men to bring about good government; scholars must seek advancement to put their abilities to use. This is where heavenly principle resides. Thus it is said that, as a matter of the Way, they are one. Laws are established, yet the times cause them to rise or fall in importance; the Way exists, yet men waver in their adherence to it. These things are determined by the government of the time. Thus it is said that, as a matter of circumstance, they are one.

The examinations and rules of eligibility have reached the utmost effectiveness in drawing in the talented men of the realm and setting them to work. Were the sage kings of high antiquity to return to life, they could not select scholars outside this system; were the worthy ministers of high antiquity to return to life, they could not advance themselves outside it. As a system, it cannot be changed. Yet Yang Guishan said: “The ancients, if they could have avoided it, seemingly would not have acted thus.” He meant that the examinations made men too ready to seek advancement. Sima Guang said: “If titles, stipends, grades, and ranks satisfy their wishes in every particular, there will be no means of putting the assembled ministers to work.” He meant that the rules of eligibility were not being observed at the time.

Without investigating the full implications of principle, men confine themselves solely to prescribed forms; without considering the proper ordering of the state, they cater solely to personal feelings. A tendency spreads among those above and becomes established among those below. The Way becomes divided here, yet the source lies there [?]. Thereupon…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
是乎有不公之謂有不常之訾李昂司考
悉黜請托是矣而楊大年之私其鄉人何
哉司空圖應舉不造郡齋似矣而盧多遜
之投牒求進何哉科舉果皆至公乎樊噲
以舍人而四遷至五大夫夏侯嬰以大僕
而三賜至執圭公孫弘徒步數年至封侯
田千秋一言句片取宰相資格果皆有常
乎殿前對策不妨程伯子之倡道學進士
題名不妨朱晦翁之集大成曾何科舉之
===
足累乎徐穉處士也陳蕃薦登三事張柬
之郡守也狄仁傑薦爲宰相又何資格之
必拘乎法無不可人則萬務令科舉之行
久矣彼以罔人之行爲法累者君子弗與
焉而高見遠識之士固不薄之而不就亦
不局之而自畀也資格之行久矣彼才望
之超資越次者蓋比比然而抱眞蓄大拘
格陸沉者抑或不能無也士而不局於科
舉是其志有所在學有所到日尋向上思
punctuated: 是乎有不公之謂，有不常之訾。李昂司考，悉黜請托，是矣；而楊大年之私其鄉人，何哉？司空圖應舉，不造郡齋，似矣；而盧多遜之投牒求進，何哉？科舉果皆至公乎？樊噲以舍人而四遷至五大夫，夏侯嬰以大僕而三賜至執圭，公孫弘徒步數年至封侯，田千秋一言句片取宰相，資格果皆有常乎？殿前對策，不妨程伯子之倡道學；進士題名，不妨朱晦翁之集大成。曾何科舉之足累乎？徐穉，處士也，陳蕃薦登三事；張柬之，郡守也，狄仁傑薦爲宰相。又何資格之必拘乎？法無不可，人則萬務。令科舉之行久矣，彼以罔人之行爲法累者，君子弗與焉。而高見遠識之士，固不薄之而不就，亦不局之而自畀也。資格之行久矣，彼才望之超資越次者，蓋比比然；而抱眞蓄大、拘格陸沉者，抑或不能無也。士而不局於科舉，是其志有所在，學有所到，日尋向上，思
translation_en:
…thus there are allegations of unfairness and criticisms of inconsistency. When Li Ang served as Examiner, he rejected all who sought advancement through personal intercession: this was right. Yet why did Yang Danian favor men from his own home region? When Sikong Tu sat the examination, he did not visit the prefect’s residence: this seems proper. Yet why did Lu Duoxun submit a written petition seeking advancement? Were the examinations indeed invariably impartial? Fan Kuai rose from attendant to Grandee of the Fifth Order through four promotions; Xiahou Ying, as Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud, received three successive grants, culminating in the rank of Jade Tablet Bearer. Gongsun Hong rose from commoner to enfeoffed marquis within a few years, while Tian Qianqiu obtained the chief ministership with a single brief utterance [?]. Were the rules governing qualifications and seniority indeed always consistent? Answering policy questions before the palace did not prevent Cheng Bozi from championing the Learning of the Way; having his name inscribed among the metropolitan graduates did not prevent Zhu Huiweng from bringing that learning to its fullest synthesis. How, then, could the examinations constitute an encumbrance? Xu Zhi was a scholar who held no office, yet Chen Fan recommended him for appointment among the Three Excellencies. Zhang Jianzhi was a prefect, yet Di Renjie recommended him as chief minister. Why, then, must qualifications and seniority invariably constrain appointments?

There is nothing inherently unworkable in the rules; as for people, there are myriad affairs [?]. Now [?], the examination system has long been practiced. The gentleman does not approve of those whose deceitful conduct brings discredit upon its rules. Men of elevated insight and far-reaching understanding certainly do not disdain it and refuse to participate, but neither do they confine themselves to it and surrender themselves to its bounds. The system of qualifications and seniority has long been practiced. Those whose talent and reputation have enabled them to advance beyond their formal qualifications and leap over the prescribed sequence are indeed numerous. Yet there may also be men who cherish what is true and harbor great capacities, but remain submerged in obscurity because they are constrained by these rules. When a scholar is not confined by the examinations, his aspirations have an object and his learning has attained something: daily he seeks to advance higher and aspires…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
齊古人而不為時文之所奪矣士而拘於
資格則其所以撿察其身與所以推明理
道以垂不朽者固其所當為抑所能為也
又焉肯以世俗耳目役其心哉道至是而
始道勢至是而始不勢雖然士之自處固
當如是然二者實方今取士之途用人之
法不可不慎也惟主司之至明宰執之至
公使楚無獻玉之泣齊無吹竽之濫然後
為得其道也謹對
===
第三問
同考試官訓導談　批〔兵不可易言此欲責任將帥〕
同考試官教諭允　批〔事核而文其有抱者乎〕
〔是得其文武者執此以往屬不足平矣〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔能言禦戎之方〕
考試官學正逯　批〔詳陳今日之弊如指諸掌知非腐〕
〔儒可薦〕
對自古及今有不能禦戎之將而無不可
punctuated:
齊古人，而不為時文之所奪矣。士而拘於資格，則其所以撿察其身，與所以推明理道以垂不朽者，固其所當為，抑所能為也。又焉肯以世俗耳目役其心哉？道至是而始道，勢至是而始不勢。雖然，士之自處固當如是，然二者實方今取士之途、用人之法，不可不慎也。惟主司之至明、宰執之至公，使楚無獻玉之泣，齊無吹竽之濫，然後為得其道也。謹對。

第三問

同考試官訓導談，批〔兵不可易言，此欲責任將帥。〕
同考試官教諭允，批〔事核而文，其有抱者乎？〕〔是得其文武者，執此以往，屬不足平矣。〕
考試官訓導陳，批〔能言禦戎之方。〕
考試官學正逯，批〔詳陳今日之弊，如指諸掌，知非腐〕〔儒，可薦。〕

對：自古及今，有不能禦戎之將，而無不可
translation_en:
…to equal the ancients, without allowing contemporary examination prose to divert him. If a scholar is constrained by formal qualifications, examining his own conduct and elucidating principles and the Way so as to leave an enduring legacy are assuredly what he ought to do, and also what he can do. How, then, could he let worldly perceptions enslave his mind? Only at this point does the Way truly become the Way, and worldly power cease to exercise its sway. Nevertheless, although this is indeed how scholars should conduct themselves, these two institutions are the present means of selecting scholars and employing men, and must be handled with care. Only when those presiding over selection are utterly discerning and the chief councillors utterly impartial—so that in Chu no presenter of jade need weep, and in Qi no unqualified player may pass himself off among the yu musicians—will the proper way have been attained. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Third Question

Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Military affairs cannot be discussed lightly. This answer seeks to hold commanders accountable.〕
Associate Examiner Yun, Instructor, comments: 〔Substantial in its treatment of affairs and accomplished in its writing: does its author have aspirations?〕〔This is one who has attained both civil and military accomplishments. Proceeding on this basis, there would be nothing that could not be pacified [?].〕
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He can explain methods for resisting the Rong.〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔He sets out the present abuses in detail, as clearly as pointing to something in his palm. Clearly he is no pedantic〕〔scholar, and may be recommended.〕

Reply: From antiquity to the present, there have been generals incapable of resisting the Rong, but there have never been any who could not be…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
禦之戎有不能備邊之兵而無不可備之
邊選將訓兵以戰則勝以守則固矣我
國家西自岷洮東盡遼海逶迴萬里控扼諸
邊河山險阻盡為我有使得將以馭兵有
兵以衛將則何戎狄之難禦邊塞之難備
哉請因明問所陳之戎狄之為中國患也
尚矣漢有匈奴唐有回紇吐蕃宋有契丹
女直而其備禦之方若王恢陳征伐之謀
賈誼立表餌之說婁敬興和親之義晁錯
===
建農戰之策張仁愿築受降三城於朔方
李德裕建仗義保佛柔遠三城於西南白
居易欲畜之以人爭郭子儀欲務兵於邊
郡宋人以金幣啖胡人以封號予元昊論
其利害得失則王恢失之貪賈誼失之疎
婁敬失之弱而晁錯張仁愿李德裕郭子
儀之策揆之於今得若人焉皆有可施行
者而不得其人則徒擾無益耳白居易欲
禦其來捨其去是亦確論宋人勢弱反媚
punctuated: 禦之戎，有不能備邊之兵，而無不可備之邊。選將訓兵，以戰則勝，以守則固矣。我國家西自岷洮，東盡遼海，逶迴萬里，控扼諸邊，河山險阻盡為我有。使得將以馭兵，有兵以衛將，則何戎狄之難禦、邊塞之難備哉？請因明問所陳之。戎狄之為中國患也尚矣。漢有匈奴，唐有回紇、吐蕃，宋有契丹、女直。而其備禦之方，若王恢陳征伐之謀，賈誼立表餌之說，婁敬興和親之義，晁錯建農戰之策，張仁愿築受降三城於朔方，李德裕建仗義、保佛、柔遠三城於西南，白居易欲畜之以人爭，郭子儀欲務兵於邊郡，宋人以金幣啖胡人，以封號予元昊。論其利害得失，則王恢失之貪，賈誼失之疎，婁敬失之弱，而晁錯、張仁愿、李德裕、郭子儀之策，揆之於今，得若人焉，皆有可施行者；而不得其人，則徒擾無益耳。白居易欲禦其來，捨其去，是亦確論。宋人勢弱，反媚
translation_en:
…barbarians who cannot be repelled. There are troops incapable of defending the frontier, but no frontier that cannot be defended. Select commanders and train the troops: in battle they will win, and in defense they will stand firm. Our realm extends from Min and Tao in the west to Liaohai in the east, winding for ten thousand li and commanding the strategic points along its frontiers. The natural barriers of rivers and mountains are all in our possession. If we obtain commanders capable of directing the troops, and troops capable of protecting their commanders, what difficulty could there be in repelling the barbarians or defending the frontier? Allow me to set this forth in response to your enlightened question.

The barbarians have troubled the Central Kingdom since remote antiquity. The Han faced the Xiongnu; the Tang, the Huihe and Tufan; and the Song, the Qidan and Nüzhi. As for methods of defense against them, Wang Hui proposed punitive campaigns; Jia Yi advanced his theory of displays and inducements; Lou Jing advocated peace through marriage alliances; and Chao Cuo proposed combining farming with warfare. Zhang Renyuan built the three Shouxiang fortresses in Shuofang, and Li Deyu built the three fortresses of Zhangyi, Baofo, and Rouyuan in the southwest. Bai Juyi wished to restrain them through human contention [?], while Guo Ziyi wished to concentrate military efforts in the frontier commanderies. The Song used gold and silks to entice the northern peoples and bestowed titles upon Yuanhao.

Considering the advantages and disadvantages, successes and failures of these policies, Wang Hui erred through greed, Jia Yi through impracticality, and Lou Jing through weakness. Yet, measured against present circumstances, the policies of Chao Cuo, Zhang Renyuan, Li Deyu, and Guo Ziyi all contain measures that could be put into practice, provided we obtain men of their caliber. Without the right men, however, they would merely cause disruption without benefit. Bai Juyi wished to repel them when they came and let them go when they withdrew; this too is a sound judgment. The Song, being weak, instead sought to flatter…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
夷狄無足取者今北虜不恭寇我疆埸窺
我之宣府挑我之大同入我神木縣擄我
黃河套時去時來或聚或散備東則擾西
防此則奔彼二年于茲迄無休息
朝廷徒有出師之勞塞上不聞克敵之實揄
林之師老而無功寧夏之卒困而不出今
日報某縣被掠男女幾百明日報某鎮被
掠牛羊幾千而鎮帥若無聞也以有數之
男女有盡之牛羊供其無窮之掠而我曾
===
不敢出一卒發一矢以加之戎有不生心
者哉昔人有言匈奴之衆不足當漢之一
縣今舉天下之全力以當之而不能制其
命是必有其由矣古者用兵號令出於一
人士卒受其指麾令朝出而朝行報夕至
而夕發信賞必罰人思自奮今十羊九牧
而計畫不協彼此牵制而從違靡定遲回
不決而緩不及事敗軍者逋誅逗留者苟
免安居者論功死戰者不錄偏裨各有倚
punctuated: 夷狄，無足取者。今北虜不恭，寇我疆埸，窺我之宣府，挑我之大同，入我神木縣，擄我黃河套，時去時來，或聚或散，備東則擾西，防此則奔彼。二年于茲，迄無休息。朝廷徒有出師之勞，塞上不聞克敵之實。揄林之師老而無功，寧夏之卒困而不出。今日報某縣被掠男女幾百，明日報某鎮被掠牛羊幾千，而鎮帥若無聞也。以有數之男女、有盡之牛羊，供其無窮之掠，而我曾不敢出一卒、發一矢以加之，戎有不生心者哉？昔人有言：「匈奴之衆不足當漢之一縣。」今舉天下之全力以當之，而不能制其命，是必有其由矣。古者用兵，號令出於一人，士卒受其指麾，令朝出而朝行，報夕至而夕發，信賞必罰，人思自奮。今十羊九牧，而計畫不協；彼此牵制，而從違靡定；遲回不決，而緩不及事。敗軍者逋誅，逗留者苟免，安居者論功，死戰者不錄，偏裨各有倚
translation_en:
…the barbarians—an approach with nothing to commend it. Now the northern foes are insubordinate: they raid our frontiers, watch for an opening at our Xuanfu, challenge our Datong, enter our Shenmu County, and plunder our territory in the Yellow River bend. They come and go, now gathering, now scattering. When we prepare in the east, they harass the west; when we defend here, they rush there. This has continued for two years without respite. The court incurs only the toil of dispatching armies, while no actual victories over the enemy are reported from the frontier. The army at Yulin [?] has grown weary without achieving results, and the troops at Ningxia are hard pressed and do not venture out. Today comes a report that several hundred men and women have been carried off from some county; tomorrow, that several thousand cattle and sheep have been plundered from some garrison. Yet the garrison commanders act as though they have heard nothing. We supply their endless plundering with our finite numbers of men and women and our exhaustible stocks of cattle and sheep, yet dare not send out a single soldier or loose a single arrow against them. How could the enemy fail to develop further ambitions?

Someone in antiquity said: “The multitude of the Xiongnu is not enough to withstand a single county of the Han.” Now we bring the entire strength of the realm against them, yet cannot control their fate. There must be a reason for this. In ancient warfare, commands issued from one man, and the soldiers accepted his direction. An order issued in the morning was carried out that morning; a report arriving in the evening prompted action that evening. Rewards were reliable and punishments certain, and every man sought to exert himself. Now there are nine shepherds for ten sheep, and their plans are uncoordinated. They constrain one another, leaving it uncertain whether orders will be obeyed or disregarded. They hesitate without deciding, and their delays make timely action impossible. Those who lose armies evade execution; those who linger instead of advancing escape punishment through expediency. Those who remain safely at ease are credited with merit, while those who fight to the death go unrecorded. The subordinate commanders each have someone on whom they rely…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
靠每懷不戰之心士卒素不訓練先存退
怯之意行伍之下豈無智謀勇鋭之士其
如不用何哉况各邊軍士寡弱倉廩空虛
人無鬬志彼此觀望此其所以不能制勝
也爲今之計誠在慎擇總兵廵撫專其委
任責其成功而嚴以勸懲使將帥監司各
得其人則謀畫協一賞罰明信智勇並用
士卒訓練倉廩充實而守無不固戰無不
勝若李牧之在趙李廣之在漢而匈奴不
===
敢近邊韓范二公之在宋而西賊寒膽又
何慮慮之足慮哉愚也草茅賤士芹藻迂生
抱悃款以無施懷奮激而長默伏承明問
發其狂言進退之惟命
第四問
同考試官訓導何　批〔能言古能適時誰謂科舉而不可得豪傑士乎若此非耶〕
鄭　選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔論國用惟陸贄最不煩此篇〕
punctuated:
靠，每懷不戰之心；士卒素不訓練，先存退怯之意。行伍之下，豈無智謀勇鋭之士？其如不用何哉！况各邊軍士寡弱，倉廩空虛，人無鬬志，彼此觀望，此其所以不能制勝也。爲今之計，誠在慎擇總兵、廵撫，專其委任，責其成功，而嚴以勸懲。使將帥、監司各得其人，則謀畫協一，賞罰明信，智勇並用，士卒訓練，倉廩充實，而守無不固，戰無不勝。若李牧之在趙，李廣之在漢，而匈奴不敢近邊；韓范二公之在宋，而西賊寒膽，又何慮慮之足慮哉！愚也，草茅賤士，芹藻迂生，抱悃款以無施，懷奮激而長默。伏承明問，發其狂言，進退之惟命。

第四問

同考試官訓導何　批〔能言古，能適時，誰謂科舉而不可得豪傑士乎？若此非耶？〕

鄭　選

同考試官教諭曾　批〔論國用，惟陸贄最不煩，此篇〕
translation_en:
…support from patrons, each habitually intending to avoid battle; the soldiers, ordinarily untrained, already harbor thoughts of retreat and fear. Surely there are men of intelligence, resourcefulness, courage, and spirit in the ranks? Yet what can be done if they are not employed? Moreover, troops along the various frontiers are few and weak, the granaries are empty, and the men have no will to fight; each watches the others and waits. These are the reasons they cannot secure victory.

The policy for the present truly lies in carefully choosing regional commanders and grand coordinators, giving them undivided authority, holding them responsible for success, and rigorously administering encouragement and punishment. If suitable men fill the posts of commanders and surveillance officials, their plans will be coordinated, rewards and punishments clear and trustworthy, and intelligence and courage both put to use. The soldiers will be trained and the granaries well supplied; every defense will be secure and every battle victorious. When Li Mu served Zhao and Li Guang served the Han, the Xiongnu dared not approach the frontier; when the two lords Han and Fan served the Song, the western rebels trembled with fear. What further cause for anxiety would there be? [The transcription repeats 慮 here.]

I am but a humble scholar from obscurity, an impractical student of the schools. I harbor sincerity but have no means to put it into practice; I cherish an impassioned resolve but have long remained silent. Humbly receiving your discerning question, I have ventured these rash words. Whether to advance or dismiss me rests entirely with your command.

Fourth Question

Associate Examiner He, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He can discuss antiquity and adapt to the needs of the times. Who says that the examinations cannot discover outstanding men? Is this not such a man?”

Zheng Xuan

Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: “In discussing state expenditure, none was more concise than Lu Zhi. This essay…”

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
知之
考試官訓導陳　批〔處置餉邊有法當是學者〕
考試官學正逯　批〔餉邊今日急務書生能言之非泥〕
〔古而不通今者進而用之〕
對轉漕於國家無事之日其事雖難而差
緩轉漕於軍旅方興之時其事既難而尤
亟緩者日征月邁勞息以時而事無不濟
亟者風催火促一日後期則功隨以墮此
餉軍之漕所以又重於無事之日也請因
===
明問所及而陳之昔者漢唐皆都關中漢
武帝時鄭當時㵎山東粟四百萬石止用
卒六萬人唐肅宗時劉晏漕江淮粟一百
一十萬石無升斗覆溺皆由河入渭經底
柱之險而卒收成效以任用得人也裴耀
卿於三門東西各置倉漕舟輸其東陸運
輸其西節級轉般復由舟以達京師雖能
避底柱之險終不若耿壽昌和糴三輔近
郡之為優也李齊物門底柱以通漕道山
punctuated:
知之。
考試官訓導陳　批〔處置餉邊有法，當是學者。〕
考試官學正逯　批〔餉邊今日急務，書生能言之，非泥〕〔古而不通今者，進而用之。〕
對：轉漕於國家無事之日，其事雖難而差緩；轉漕於軍旅方興之時，其事既難而尤亟。緩者日征月邁，勞息以時，而事無不濟；亟者風催火促，一日後期，則功隨以墮。此餉軍之漕所以又重於無事之日也。請因明問所及而陳之。昔者漢唐皆都關中。漢武帝時，鄭當時㵎山東粟四百萬石，止用卒六萬人；唐肅宗時，劉晏漕江淮粟一百一十萬石，無升斗覆溺。皆由河入渭，經底柱之險，而卒收成效，以任用得人也。裴耀卿於三門東西各置倉，漕舟輸其東，陸運輸其西，節級轉般，復由舟以達京師。雖能避底柱之險，終不若耿壽昌和糴三輔近郡之為優也。李齊物門底柱以通漕道，山
translation_en:
…understands this.
Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He has sound methods for managing provisions for the frontier; he must be a man of learning.〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Supplying the frontier is an urgent task today. This scholar can discuss it; he is not someone who clings〕〔to antiquity without understanding the present. Promote him and employ him.〕
Response: Transporting grain by water when the state is at peace is difficult, but comparatively unhurried; transporting it when military operations are just beginning is both difficult and especially urgent. When there is no hurry, the journey proceeds day after day and month after month, with work and rest at proper intervals, and everything can be accomplished. When there is urgency, one is driven as by wind and pressed as by fire: a single day’s delay brings the enterprise to ruin. This is why transporting grain to provision armies is even more consequential than doing so in peaceful times. Allow me to explain in light of the matters raised in your discerning question.
Formerly, both the Han and the Tang established their capitals in Guanzhong. Under Emperor Wu of the Han, Zheng Dangshi transported [?] four million shi of grain from Shandong, employing only sixty thousand soldiers. Under Emperor Suzong of the Tang, Liu Yan transported 1,100,000 shi of grain by water from the Jiang–Huai region, without losing so much as a sheng or a dou through capsizing or sinking. Both routes passed from the Yellow River into the Wei River and through the dangerous waters at Dizhu. Their eventual success resulted from appointing the right men.
Pei Yaoqing established granaries to both the east and west of Sanmen. Grain boats delivered their cargoes to the eastern granaries, and overland transport carried the grain to the western ones. It was transferred stage by stage and then conveyed again by boat to the capital. Although this avoided the dangers of Dizhu, it was ultimately inferior to Geng Shouchang’s purchase of grain at agreed prices in the Three Capital Districts and nearby commanderies. Li Qiwu cut a passage through Dizhu to open a route for grain transport; the mountain…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
巔以通輓燒石沃醯而鑿之然棄石於河
激水湍怒舟不能入新門終不若李泌開
運道十八里者之為得也秦人致瀕海之
粟於河北求給運冀州之粟於烏巢其心
侈矣烏得而不亡蕭何漕關中以給擊楚
之兵孔明置木馬以便祁山之運其策良
矣烏得而不濟噫關中之地阻山帶河歷
代之漕遡河入渭或直達或轉般或和糴
或給京師或餉軍旅各因其時皆能濟事
===
我
國家建都上地轉漕東南若江浙之東西淮
湖之南北歲漕數百萬石自儀真至通州
導善河數千里舟楫往來穩於履陸一夫
牽輓優於六騾北方之粟貢本色者亦由
水漕齊糴直者則由陸路百數十年上下
稱便漕法之善前代莫及比者獵犹匪茹
腥羶疆圉出沒不時禍心叵測至勤
朝廷命將出師遠駐西鄙相持日久粮餉不
punctuated:
巔以通輓，燒石沃醯而鑿之，然棄石於河，激水湍怒，舟不能入新門，終不若李泌開運道十八里者之為得也。秦人致瀕海之粟於河北，求給運冀州之粟於烏巢，其心侈矣，烏得而不亡？蕭何漕關中以給擊楚之兵，孔明置木馬以便祁山之運，其策良矣，烏得而不濟？噫！關中之地，阻山帶河，歷代之漕，遡河入渭，或直達，或轉般，或和糴，或給京師，或餉軍旅，各因其時，皆能濟事。
我國家建都上地，轉漕東南，若江浙之東西、淮湖之南北，歲漕數百萬石。自儀真至通州，導善河數千里，舟楫往來，穩於履陸；一夫牽輓，優於六騾。北方之粟，貢本色者，亦由水漕；齊糴直者，則由陸路。百數十年，上下稱便，漕法之善，前代莫及。比者獵犹匪茹，腥羶疆圉，出沒不時，禍心叵測，至勤朝廷命將出師，遠駐西鄙，相持日久，粮餉不
translation_en:
…at the summit to permit towing; the rock was heated by fire, doused with vinegar, and then cut through. Yet the discarded stone was thrown into the river, making the current surge so violently that boats could not enter the new opening. Ultimately, this was less effective than Li Mi’s opening of an eighteen-li transport route. The men of Qin brought grain from the coast to the region north of the Yellow River; [the text is unclear here] transported grain from Jizhou to Wuchao [?]. Their ambitions were extravagant: how could they escape destruction? Xiao He shipped grain from Guanzhong to supply the troops fighting Chu; Kongming provided wooden horses to facilitate transport to Qishan. Their plans were sound: how could they fail to succeed? Ah! Guanzhong is protected by mountains and girdled by rivers. In successive dynasties, grain shipments went upstream along the Yellow River into the Wei River, sometimes proceeding directly, sometimes being transferred in stages, and sometimes supplied through purchases at agreed prices. Whether provisioning the capital or feeding armies, each method suited its circumstances and accomplished its purpose.
Our dynasty established its capital in a superior location and transports grain by water from the southeast—from the eastern and western parts of Jiang and Zhe and the northern and southern parts of Huai and Hu [?]—shipping several million shi annually. From Yizhen to Tongzhou, the river route has been opened and improved over several thousand li [?]. Boats travel to and fro more safely than one walks on land, and a single man towing a boat accomplishes more than six mules. Northern grain submitted as tribute in kind likewise travels by water; money remitted for grain purchases [?] travels overland. For more than a hundred years, both officials and people have found these arrangements convenient. No previous dynasty has equaled the excellence of this grain-transport system. Recently, however, savage enemies, refusing to yield [?], have befouled the frontier with their rank presence, appearing and disappearing unpredictably, their malicious intentions unfathomable. They have even obliged the court to appoint commanders and dispatch armies to distant stations on the western frontier. The confrontation has continued for many days, and grain and provisions have not…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
給乃移河南粮一十八萬石往饋榆林山
路阻遠輦馱無由欲運本色則脚價幾倍
欲齎糴直則易買無所出不得已多費不
恤然此虜不滅用兵不已西運之役或至
再興苟無善處之術必有内困之弊且如
漢唐漕運皆由三門以給關中今河渭無
常漕之道陝西非常運之所轉般和糴優
於直達緩急所需難持一說陸贄有言欲
制國用當夲輕重令日之事惟視歲之豐
===
歉與事之緩急何如耳歲豐而事緩則齎
糴直而行和糴之法或投糴直可也歲歉
而事急則運本色而行轉般之法或即直
達亦可也惟民不擾而兵不饑斯為得策
耳管子曰粟行五百里衆有饑色孫子曰
千里餽粮士有饑色今各邊粮料勢所難
必内地人民理所當恤若操畸盈者別有
轉移通融之術使近邊千里五百里以内
郡縣專實邊廩而免令内地轉輸尤為良
punctuated: 給，乃移河南粮一十八萬石往饋榆林。山路阻遠，輦馱無由。欲運本色，則脚價幾倍；欲齎糴直，則易買無所出。不得已，多費不恤。然此虜不滅，用兵不已，西運之役或至再興。苟無善處之術，必有内困之弊。且如漢唐漕運，皆由三門以給關中。今河渭無常漕之道，陝西非常運之所。轉般、和糴優於直達，緩急所需，難持一說。陸贄有言：「欲制國用，當夲輕重。」令日之事，惟視歲之豐歉與事之緩急何如耳。歲豐而事緩，則齎糴直而行和糴之法，或投糴直可也；歲歉而事急，則運本色而行轉般之法，或即直達亦可也。惟民不擾而兵不饑，斯為得策耳。管子曰：「粟行五百里，衆有饑色。」孫子曰：「千里餽粮，士有饑色。」今各邊粮料，勢所難必；内地人民，理所當恤。若操畸盈者別有轉移通融之術，使近邊千里、五百里以内郡縣專實邊廩，而免令内地轉輸，尤為良
translation_en:
…were insufficient, so 180,000 shi of grain from Henan were diverted to provision Yulin. The mountain roads were difficult and long, leaving no practicable means of carriage by cart or pack animal. Transporting grain in kind would cost several times its value in freight; taking money to purchase grain would leave nowhere to obtain it. With no alternative, the additional expense had to be disregarded. Yet unless these enemies are destroyed, military operations will not cease, and the burden of transporting supplies westward may arise again. Without a sound method of handling this, hardship within the realm will inevitably result.

Under the Han and Tang, grain shipments all passed through Sanmen to supply Guanzhong. Today the Yellow and Wei rivers have no regular grain-transport route, and Shaanxi is not a regular destination for such shipments. Transport by successive relays and government purchase of grain at agreed prices are preferable to direct delivery, but no single prescription can meet both urgent and less pressing needs. Lu Zhi said: “To regulate state expenditure, one must take relative prices as the basis.” In present circumstances [?], one need only consider whether the harvest is abundant or poor and whether the need is urgent or can wait. If the harvest is abundant and the need can wait, one may take purchase funds and buy grain at agreed prices, or remit the purchase funds [?]. If the harvest is poor and the need urgent, one may transport grain in kind by successive relays, or deliver it directly. A sound policy is simply one that leaves the people undisturbed and the soldiers adequately fed.

The Guanzi says: “When grain travels five hundred li, the multitude looks hungry.” The Sunzi says: “When provisions are sent a thousand li, the soldiers look hungry.” At present, circumstances make it difficult to ensure supplies of grain and fodder at every frontier, while the people of the interior ought in principle to receive consideration. If those managing deficits and surpluses [?] have some further means of reallocating resources and adjusting financial arrangements, so that prefectures and counties within a thousand or five hundred li of the frontier take sole responsibility for filling frontier granaries, while the interior is spared the obligation to transport supplies, this would be particularly advantageous…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
便不然則夷患未除腹裏或先騷擾誠不
可不慮也謹對
第五問
何瑭
同考試官訓導張　批〔屯與漕相緩急屯治則漕省矣此篇能知之而因問款對文且通暢當是佳士〕
同考試官學正張　批〔策場能款荅者極少晚得此卷甚愜讀之不釋手卜子他日當為是科之榮〕
考試官訓導陳　批〔詳言屯田之弊而欲防禦塞下衆實腹裏其有用世之志者乎〕
===
考試官學正逯　批〔屯田之弊已甚書生能言之其學為有用矣録之〕
對田疇易而民富孟氏之論有徵金湯守
而惟粟墨翟之言無朽此屯田之利弊不
可不究也已利當興而不興是之謂慢弊
當革而不革是之謂欺慢與欺君子弗由
也請詳言之省饋餉合兵民固本國威戎
狄莫良於屯田也尚矣漢文帝募民屯塞
punctuated:
便。不然，則夷患未除，腹裏或先騷擾，誠不可不慮也。謹對。

第五問
何瑭
同考試官訓導張，批〔屯與漕相緩急，屯治則漕省矣。此篇能知之，而因問款對，文且通暢，當是佳士。〕
同考試官學正張，批〔策場能款荅者極少，晚得此卷甚愜，讀之不釋手。卜子他日當為是科之榮。〕
考試官訓導陳，批〔詳言屯田之弊，而欲防禦塞下，衆實腹裏，其有用世之志者乎？〕
考試官學正逯，批〔屯田之弊已甚，書生能言之，其學為有用矣。録之。〕

對：田疇易而民富，孟氏之論有徵；金湯守而惟粟，墨翟之言無朽。此屯田之利弊不可不究也已。利當興而不興，是之謂慢；弊當革而不革，是之謂欺。慢與欺，君子弗由也。請詳言之。省饋餉，合兵民，固本國，威戎狄，莫良於屯田也。尚矣！漢文帝募民屯塞
translation_en:
…convenient. Otherwise, before the threat from the non-Chinese peoples has been eliminated, the interior may already have fallen into disorder. This truly must be considered. Respectfully submitted.

Fifth Question
He Tang

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Military agricultural colonies and grain transport support one another as circumstances require; when the colonies are well managed, transport can be reduced. This essay recognizes this and responds point by point to the question. Its writing is also clear and fluent. He must be a fine scholar.〕

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Very few in the policy examination can answer point by point. Finding this paper late in the reading was most gratifying; once I began reading it, I could not put it down. I predict that you will one day bring honor to this examination cohort.〕

Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He discusses in detail the abuses of military agricultural colonies and wishes to defend the frontier and make the interior populous and prosperous [?]. Surely he aspires to put his abilities to use in the world?〕

Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔The abuses of military agricultural colonies have become very serious. That a scholar can discuss them shows that his learning has practical value. Select this paper.〕

Your servant replies: When the fields are cultivated, the people prosper: Master Meng’s argument is borne out by evidence. The defense of walls strong as metal and moats like boiling water depends upon grain: Mo Di’s words remain imperishable. Thus the benefits and abuses of military agricultural colonies must be thoroughly investigated. To fail to promote a benefit that ought to be promoted is called negligence; to fail to eliminate an abuse that ought to be eliminated is called deception. The gentleman follows neither negligence nor deception. Allow me to explain in detail. For reducing the conveyance of provisions, bringing soldiers and civilians together, securing the foundations of the state, and overawing the Rong and Di peoples, nothing surpasses military agricultural colonies. Their use goes far back! Emperor Wen of Han recruited commoners to establish agricultural colonies on the frontier…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
下漢武帝遣士田敦煌趙充國屯湟中而
罪幵服棗祗田許下而魏兵強陳項壽春
皆置屯田晉所以吞江左關中諸鎮皆置
屯田唐所以奠中國宋人北與遼接境而
於河北諸路大興營田西與夏連塞而於
陝西州軍皆置屯田一以防寇一以足食
此漢唐宋屯田之明驗也我
太祖皇帝既定四海設衛以治軍給田以啓屯
大率以二分居守八分務農歲收所入以
===
給軍食以紓民力
聖謨神猷布在天下我
太宗皇帝尤留
聖慮
詔旨丁寧惟恐弗至此
祖宗之時所以食足兵強以征則勝以守則固
也承平日久法制漸弛有屯田之名無屯
田之實於是兵餉之出於民者什常八九
而州縣歲入有常歲用日增財力漸耗兵
punctuated:
下。漢武帝遣士田敦煌，趙充國屯湟中而罪幵服，棗祗田許下而魏兵強。陳、項、壽春皆置屯田，晉所以吞江左；關中諸鎮皆置屯田，唐所以奠中國。宋人北與遼接境，而於河北諸路大興營田；西與夏連塞，而於陝西州軍皆置屯田。一以防寇，一以足食，此漢唐宋屯田之明驗也。
我太祖皇帝既定四海，設衛以治軍，給田以啓屯，大率以二分居守，八分務農，歲收所入，以給軍食，以紓民力。聖謨神猷，布在天下。我太宗皇帝尤留聖慮，詔旨丁寧，惟恐弗至。此祖宗之時所以食足兵強，以征則勝，以守則固也。
承平日久，法制漸弛，有屯田之名，無屯田之實。於是兵餉之出於民者，什常八九，而州縣歲入有常，歲用日增，財力漸耗，兵
translation_en:
…along the frontier. Emperor Wu of Han sent soldiers to cultivate land at Dunhuang. Zhao Chongguo established military agricultural colonies in Huangzhong, and the Zui and Jian [?] submitted. Zao Zhi cultivated land around Xu, and Wei’s forces grew strong. Military agricultural colonies were established at Chen, Xiang, and Shouchun: these enabled Jin to conquer the lands south of the Yangzi. Such colonies were established at the various garrisons in Guanzhong: these enabled Tang to secure the Central Lands. Under the Song, the northern border adjoined Liao, and agricultural colonies were extensively developed throughout the circuits of Hebei; the western frontier adjoined Xia, and military agricultural colonies were established throughout the prefectures and military prefectures of Shaanxi. They served both to ward off raiders and to ensure adequate provisions. These are clear demonstrations of the effectiveness of military agricultural colonies under Han, Tang, and Song.
After our Emperor Taizu had pacified all within the Four Seas, he established guards to administer the troops and allotted land to initiate military agricultural colonies. As a general rule, two-tenths of the men remained on garrison duty, while eight-tenths engaged in farming. The annual harvest supplied the troops with food and eased the burden on the people. His sagacious plans and inspired designs were implemented throughout the realm. Our Emperor Taizong devoted particular imperial attention to this matter; his edicts repeatedly enjoined compliance, his sole concern being that implementation might fall short. This is why, in the time of our imperial ancestors, provisions were plentiful and troops strong: on campaign they were victorious, and in defense they stood firm.
After many years of peace, the regulations gradually grew lax. Military agricultural colonies existed in name but no longer in substance. Consequently, eight or nine tenths of military provisions regularly came from the people. Yet the annual revenues of prefectures and counties remained fixed, while annual expenditure increased day by day. Financial resources were gradually depleted, and the troops…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
且日餒如河南衛所有經年不得支升斗
者言之可慨悪之無由使
國初屯田皆在而無隱皆治而不荒則軍士
何患乎餒百姓何病乎餉也是故連城繞
堡者塞下之屯田而鄙棄於無用跨州軼
縣者腹裏之屯田而多沒於久假餉丁綱
吏徒自勞苦使者有司互相同異始也有
衛必有田今或衛遷而田存始也有田必
有屯今則田在而屯亡為今之計莫如分
===
遣將士列屯塞内考覈錯農戰之策究充
國便宜之條寇來則戰寇去則耕庶幾乎
塞下屯壤之粟盡入於邊廩而戰士飽矣
委任忠誠查究卷籍以公道為主宰以覈
實為倚靠毋奪於利毋怵於勢庶幾乎腹
裏屯壤之粟盡歸於
朝廷而百姓飽矣今夫古今天下之事利與
害公與私而已矣利害係乎天下不係乎
己公私係乎己不係乎人苟行之以公則
punctuated:
且日餒，如河南衛所有經年不得支升斗者，言之可慨，悪之無由。使國初屯田皆在而無隱，皆治而不荒，則軍士何患乎餒，百姓何病乎餉也？是故連城繞堡者，塞下之屯田，而鄙棄於無用；跨州軼縣者，腹裏之屯田，而多沒於久假。餉丁綱吏徒自勞苦，使者有司互相同異。始也有衛必有田，今或衛遷而田存；始也有田必有屯，今則田在而屯亡。為今之計，莫如分遣將士，列屯塞内，考覈錯農戰之策，究充國便宜之條。寇來則戰，寇去則耕，庶幾乎塞下屯壤之粟盡入於邊廩，而戰士飽矣。委任忠誠，查究卷籍，以公道為主宰，以覈實為倚靠，毋奪於利，毋怵於勢，庶幾乎腹裏屯壤之粟盡歸於朝廷，而百姓飽矣。
今夫古今天下之事，利與害、公與私而已矣。利害係乎天下，不係乎己；公私係乎己，不係乎人。苟行之以公，則
translation_en:
…and the troops grow hungrier by the day. In the guards and battalions of Henan, for example, some have gone an entire year without receiving so much as a sheng or dou of grain. To speak of this is distressing, yet there is no way to remedy it [?]. If the military agricultural lands established at the dynasty’s founding all remained intact, with none concealed, and were all cultivated, with none lying waste, why would soldiers fear hunger, or the common people suffer from supplying their provisions? Thus the military agricultural lands along the frontier, linking walled towns and surrounding forts, have been cast aside as useless; those in the interior, stretching across prefectures and counties, have largely disappeared into prolonged loans of land. Provisioning laborers and grain-convoy clerks toil in vain, while commissioners and the responsible officials alternately agree and disagree with one another. Originally, wherever there was a guard, there was necessarily land; now some guards have moved while their lands remain. Originally, wherever there was land, there was necessarily a military agricultural colony; now the lands remain but the colonies have vanished. For the present, no plan is better than to dispatch officers and soldiers in separate contingents to establish colonies at intervals within the frontier, examine Chao Cuo’s proposals for farming and warfare, and investigate Zhao Chongguo’s recommendations for measures suited to circumstances. When raiders come, they should fight; when the raiders leave, they should farm. Then perhaps all the grain from frontier military agricultural lands will enter the border granaries, and the fighting men will have enough to eat. Entrust loyal and sincere men with examining the registers and records, taking impartiality as their guiding principle and verification of the facts as their support. They must neither be swayed by profit nor intimidated by power. Then perhaps all the grain from military agricultural lands in the interior will accrue to the imperial court, and the common people will have enough to eat.
Now, affairs throughout the realm, past and present, come down simply to benefit and harm, public-mindedness and private interest. Benefit and harm concern the whole realm, not oneself; public-mindedness and private interest depend upon oneself, not others. If one acts with public-mindedness, then…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
凡所以興利除害為國為民者惟以事之
是非理之可否為作輟而千鎰萬鍾不吾
誘勢威挫黜不吾遷也苟出於私則趨利
避害止計一身而患得患失無所不至矣
是故公而不私則天下無不興之利無不
革之弊私而不公吾未如之何也已書生
無通變之見請舉腐儒之常談以為對執
事以為何如
punctuated: 凡所以興利除害、為國為民者，惟以事之是非、理之可否為作輟，而千鎰萬鍾不吾誘，勢威挫黜不吾遷也。苟出於私，則趨利避害，止計一身，而患得患失，無所不至矣。是故公而不私，則天下無不興之利，無不革之弊；私而不公，吾未如之何也已。書生無通變之見，請舉腐儒之常談以為對，執事以為何如？
translation_en: …then, in all efforts to promote benefits and eliminate harms for the state and the people, one undertakes or suspends action solely according to whether the matter is right or wrong and whether it accords with principle. A thousand yi of precious metal and ten thousand zhong of grain cannot tempt me; power, intimidation, humiliation, and dismissal cannot sway me. If one acts from private interest, however, one pursues advantage and avoids harm, calculating only for oneself; anxious both to obtain and to retain what one has, one will stop at nothing. Thus, when one serves the public interest rather than private interests, there is no benefit under Heaven that cannot be promoted and no abuse that cannot be abolished. When one serves private interests rather than the public interest, I can do nothing about it. A mere scholar, I lack the insight needed to adapt to changing circumstances. Allow me to offer the commonplace observations of a pedantic Confucian as my reply. What do you, honored examiners, think of it?

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
惟河南古豫州之域當四方
之中去
京師纔千餘里
聖化漸被率先諸省一時賢俊之
出敭歷中外為耳目之官心
膂之寄台鉉師保之重望碩
===
今日為最盛焉嘗考豫之為言
舒也人稟中和之氣性理安
舒也然則中州之人物瓌奇
禮教修明信有由哉乃弘治
十四年辛酉秋河南以取士
較文之任屬諸〔言〕等錄成僉
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

惟河南，古豫州之域，當四方之中，去京師纔千餘里。聖化漸被，率先諸省。一時賢俊之出，敭歷中外，為耳目之官、心膂之寄、台鉉師保之重，望碩今日為最盛焉。嘗考豫之為言，舒也；人稟中和之氣，性理安舒也。然則中州之人物瓌奇，禮教修明，信有由哉！乃弘治十四年辛酉秋，河南以取士較文之任屬諸〔言〕等。錄成，僉
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

Henan occupies the territory of ancient Yuzhou, at the center of the four quarters, barely more than a thousand li from the capital. In receiving the pervasive influence of the sage emperor’s transforming instruction, it leads the other provinces. The worthy and talented men emerging in this age have served successively in posts at court and in the provinces—as officials who are the throne’s ears and eyes, as trusted servants who are its heart and sinews, and in the weighty positions of chief ministers, preceptors, and guardians. Men of eminent reputation are more abundant today than ever [?].

I have examined the meaning of “Yu”: it means ease. People here receive the vital energy of centrality and harmony, and their inherent natures are peaceful and at ease. Thus there is indeed a reason why the Central Region produces outstanding men and why its ritual instruction is cultivated and enlightened!

In the autumn of the xinyou year, the fourteenth year of Hongzhi [1501], Henan entrusted the responsibility for selecting men of talent and evaluating their compositions to us, Yan and the others. When the record was completed, all …

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
謂〔言〕宜有言以序其後竊謂
東西南北地異其方剛柔善
惡人異其質而中和之鍾於
人者果同與異與孔子之言
性相近兼氣質而言周子剛
柔善惡之論是也孟子之言
性善以理而言周子中正仁
===
義之論是也是則有同者焉
不能以或異得於天命之本
然不假於修為者也有異者
焉不能以皆同囿於形氣之
厖雜必假於修為者也師之
所以為教士之所以為學必
先乎此若古之成德達材或
punctuated: 謂〔言〕宜有言以序其後。竊謂東西南北，地異其方；剛柔善惡，人異其質。而中和之鍾於人者，果同與，異與？孔子之言性相近，兼氣質而言，周子剛柔善惡之論是也；孟子之言性善，以理而言，周子中正仁義之論是也。是則有同者焉，不能以或異，得於天命之本然，不假於修為者也；有異者焉，不能以皆同，囿於形氣之厖雜，必假於修為者也。師之所以為教，士之所以為學，必先乎此。若古之成德達材，或
translation_en:
…said that Yan should offer some words as a postface. I humbly hold that east, west, south, and north differ in their geographical situation, while people differ in their constitutions—firm or yielding, good or evil. Yet is the equilibrium and harmony bestowed upon people truly the same or different? When Confucius said that human natures are close to one another, he spoke with their material endowments also in view; Master Zhou’s discussion of firmness and yieldingness, goodness and evil concerns this. When Mencius said that human nature is good, he spoke in terms of principle; Master Zhou’s discussion of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness concerns this.

Thus there is something shared, which cannot be regarded as differing in particular cases: it is received from Heaven’s mandate in its original condition and does not depend on cultivation. There is also something that differs, which cannot be regarded as universally identical: it is constrained by the heterogeneous mixture of bodily form and vital energy and necessarily depends on cultivation. Teachers, in their teaching, and scholars, in their learning, must begin with this. As for the ancient practice of perfecting virtue and developing talent, sometimes…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
進之或退之予之爵賞憲令
或予之或奪之無非抑其偏
以歸之中而已當今之世一
道德以同俗仰
重明麗正之治而成雍熙泰
和之化雖要荒海徼之地而
皆儲梁棟桷榱之才況中州
===
之士生養毓秀于嵩洛之英
靈步趨仰止於程邵之門墻
產非遐陬學皆正學其所以
薰陶於善士良治者固宜其
蘭芷之芳罇罍之古也哉〔言〕
等幸與試事窮日夜殫心力
閱几案之易書聲氣之發越
punctuated:
進之，或退之，予之爵賞憲令，或予之，或奪之，無非抑其偏以歸之中而已。當今之世，一道德以同俗，仰重明麗正之治，而成雍熙泰和之化。雖要荒海徼之地，而皆儲梁棟桷榱之才，況中州之士，生養毓秀于嵩洛之英靈，步趨仰止於程邵之門墻，產非遐陬，學皆正學，其所以薰陶於善士良治者，固宜其蘭芷之芳、罇罍之古也哉！
〔言〕等幸與試事，窮日夜，殫心力，閱几案之易書、聲氣之發越
translation_en:
…advancing some and holding others back, bestowing ranks, rewards, and authoritative ordinances [?], sometimes granting and sometimes withdrawing them—all this serves only to restrain their partial tendencies and bring them back to the mean. In the present age, moral principles are unified so that customs may be made uniform. Looking up to a government whose renewed brilliance adheres to rectitude, we achieve a transformation marked by concord, prosperity, and great harmony. Even the remotest territories and coastal borderlands nurture men talented enough to serve as the beams, pillars, and rafters of the state. How much more must this be true of the scholars of Zhongzhou! Born and nurtured amid the spiritual excellence of Song and Luo, they follow reverently in the footsteps of Cheng and Shao and look up to their schools. Their birthplace is no remote corner; their learning is entirely orthodox. Formed by the influence of worthy scholars and good government, they should surely possess the fragrance of orchids and angelica and the antique dignity of ritual wine vessels!
We, Yan and the others, have had the good fortune to participate in conducting the examination. Working through day and night and exhausting our mental energies, we have read the writings upon our desks [?], the outpouring of their voices and vital spirit…

title: 弘治十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
雖不能悉其人必求其辭之
平淡典則敦厚易直中而無
陂和而不戾者錄之否則不
與焉爾多士既幸揚名據武
于
王庭尚當功交動靜致臻位育以
翊
===
明天子協中之治使天下匹夫匹
婦咸會極歸極於無黨無偏
之地庶幾乎中和之稱情而
無後乎東西南北之人可也
直隸松江府儒學訓導陳〔言〕
謹序
punctuated:
雖不能悉其人，必求其辭之平淡典則、敦厚易直、中而無陂、和而不戾者錄之，否則不與焉爾。多士既幸揚名據武于王庭，尚當功交動靜，致臻位育，以翊明天子協中之治，使天下匹夫匹婦咸會極歸極於無黨無偏之地。庶幾乎中和之稱情，而無後乎東西南北之人可也。
直隸松江府儒學訓導陳〔言〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Although we could not fully know the men themselves, we invariably sought out and selected those whose writing was plain and restrained, refined and correct, generous and sincere, straightforward and upright, centered without deviation, and harmonious without discord. Otherwise, we did not admit them. Now that these many scholars have fortunately made their names known and gained a foothold at the royal court, they should further apply themselves in both activity and stillness, attaining the proper ordering and nurturing of all things. Thus they may assist the enlightened Son of Heaven in his rule that accords with the Mean, enabling every ordinary man and woman throughout the realm to converge upon and return to the supreme standard, where there is neither faction nor partiality. Then perhaps their designation as men of centrality and harmony will accord with their true character [?], and they will not fall behind the people of the east, west, south, or north.
Respectfully prefaced by Chen Yan 陳言, Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Songjiang Prefecture in the directly administered territory.
